title: fix(xtask): the recording build writes its JSON to a file, not a pipe
body:
## What changed

The gate's recording build (`debug build: <crate> (--no-run)`) now writes cargo's JSON to a file in the temporary directory. It does not use a pipe for it any more (`xtask/src/direct.rs`, `direct::cargo`).

## Cause

`direct::cargo` read the JSON through a pipe, in a reader thread. It joined that thread after cargo exited. A process that the build starts and that outlives the build inherits cargo's stdout. The sccache server is such a process: the first `rustc` wrapper call starts it when no server runs. That server keeps a copy of the write end of the pipe. The reader then got no end of file until the server stopped (its idle timeout). No watchdog runs during that join, because the watchdog stops when cargo exits. So the step waited after a green build. The wait depends on the sccache server state. The issue names a cargo "rmeta handoff". This worker did not see that wedge here. The pipe hold is the one wait of the prebuild path that depends on the sccache state, and the test below shows it.

The watchdog counts the file size (from the open handle) as output, as it counted the pipe bytes before. The gate reads the file when cargo exits and then deletes it. A descendant that holds the file cannot hold the gate. The decision record is `docs/decisions/3675-prebuild-json-file.md`.

## Readings

- Pinning test with the old `direct.rs`: FAILED, "the step must end when cargo exits: 120.0331239s". The 60 s watchdog did not fire.
- Pinning test with the fix: pass, in less than 1 s.

## Pinning test

- `watchdog_tests::a_recording_build_ends_when_cargo_exits_not_when_its_descendants_do`: a fake cargo (the test executable, mode `orphan`) writes JSON and exits at once. Its descendant holds its stdout and sleeps 120 s. The step must end in less than 30 s, green, with the JSON.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p xtask --bin xtask`: 323 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- Heavy lanes: none reached (xtask only).

## Not exercised

- A full batch gate run on this machine. The shared sccache server already ran, so a cold server start was not available without stopping the shared server. A second, private sccache server (other port) failed its compiles ("connection was forcibly closed"). So the cold-server path did not run end to end. The reported wedge (cargo 1.99.1) was not seen on this machine (cargo 1.100.0). The pipe hold is the probable cause, not a confirmed one. If the wedge comes back with this fix, reopen #3675.
- `direct::record` still runs `cargo metadata` with a captured stdout. It builds nothing and was not changed.
- Linux and macOS: the change uses only `std::fs` and `std::process`.

Process change: yes
Changelog: none
Effort: medium

Fixes #3675

title: feat(xtask): the heavy reach reads test-only and binary-only source files
body:
## What changed

- New module `xtask/src/heavy_files.rs`. The function `seen_by` classifies a changed file `crates/<d>/src/<rel>`:
  - A module with a `#[cfg(test)]` declaration (or an ancestor with one) reaches only `<d>:lib` and its known-fail checks. The library that other targets and other crates link does not contain this code.
  - `src/main.rs` and `src/bin/..` reach only `<d>:bins` and the integration binaries of `<d>`. An integration test can run the binary through `CARGO_BIN_EXE_<name>`.
  - All other files keep the crate reach (the whole heavy lane of `<d>` and of each dependent crate).
- Each doubt gives the crate reach: a target `path` in the manifest, a source line that names the file (`include!`, `#[path]`, also over two lines), a missing, indented, inline or repeated declaration, an attribute that is not exactly `#[cfg(test)]`, an unreadable file.
- `heavy::plan` prints one `not run: <step> - the diff does not reach it` line for each heavy step that it skips. It also prints `heavy reach: <n> step(s) reached, <m> skipped (not run)`.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3560-heavy-reach-files.md`.

## Readings (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base HEAD --dry-run`, one-line probe edit)

| Changed file | Before (crate reach) | After |
|---|---|---|
| `crates/motion/src/drilling/tests.rs` (`#[cfg(test)]`) | 95 steps | 3 steps (motion lib + 2 known-fail checks), 99 not run |
| `crates/app/src/bin/camcraft-cli.rs` | 60 steps | 58 steps, 44 not run |
| `crates/motion/src/drilling/boss.rs` (library code) | 95 steps | 95 steps (no change, must stay wide) |

## Not in this PR

The main part of #3560 is not done: a library file still reaches the whole lane. A per-module `use` graph is not sound without guards for glob imports, re-exports, trait impls, method calls and registries. The issue goes to `effort:high` for that part. This PR is `Refs`, not `Fixes`.

## Pinning tests (`xtask/src/heavy_files_tests.rs`)

- `a_cfg_test_module_reaches_only_the_unit_tests_of_its_crate`
- `library_code_keeps_the_crate_reach` (must stay wide, also mixed with a test-only file)
- `a_binary_source_reaches_the_binaries_and_integration_tests_of_its_crate_only`
- `every_doubt_answers_library`
- `an_include_or_a_target_path_keeps_the_crate_reach`
- `the_dry_run_names_each_skipped_target_and_the_counts`

The existing pins in `heavy_plan_tests.rs` are unchanged and pass.

## Gate

- `cargo test -p xtask`: 328 passed in the bin, all integration binaries pass.
- `cargo clippy -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- No heavy lane ran (process change only).

Process change: yes
Changelog: none
Effort: medium (escalated to high for the remaining part)

Refs #3560

title: feat(machines): add the Ooznest WorkBee 1000x1500 (Estlcam) machine
body:
﻿## What changed

- New library machine `assets/machines/ooznest-workbee-1000x1500.mch`, "Ooznest WorkBee 1000x1500 (Estlcam)", kind `mill`:
  - X 1200 mm, Y 770 mm, Z 88 mm travel (written `-L..L`).
  - X and Y feed and rapid 2500 mm/min. Z rates are not stated.
  - Spindle power 2.2 kW (the WorkBee's owner). No rpm range is stated.
  - No coolant, no tool count, no `controller.post`.
- The machine picker row and the bundled include line in `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`.
- The decision record `docs/decisions/3038-workbee-estlcam.md` with all sources.

## Work area: the smaller value on each axis

The maintainer decided this on 2026-11-23. The WorkBee's owner (MisterMaker) gave 1200 x 800 mm (X x Y). Ooznest's public page for the 1000x1500 frame gives 1270 x 770 mm and Z 88 mm.
- X 1200 mm: the owner's figure, inside the published 1270.
- Y 770 mm: the published figure. The owner's 800 is more than it.
- Z 88 mm: the published figure. The owner has not stated Z.

A smaller travel can refuse a program that the machine could run. It never passes a move past the real end of travel. The WorkBee's owner must confirm his frame size and his real X/Y/Z travel before the values are final. The file name `ooznest-workbee-1000x1500.mch` names the frame, so it stays.

## Why no post is named

Estlcam publishes its rules for programs from other CAM programs (https://www.estlcam.de/steuerung_cnc_programme.php). Each motion line must have its own G word. Arcs use I/J only, with no full circles. The control ignores other G words with no message. No built-in post is confirmed to meet these rules. A post for them changes posted G-code and is under the safety floor. The follow-up is #3735 (`effort:high`).

## Sources (read 2026-11-23)

- https://ooznest.co.uk/product/black-1000x1500mm-workbee-z1-cnc-router-machine-ethernet-uk-power/ (working area 770x1270, Z 88, max feed 2500 mm/min, lead screw drive)
- https://ooznest.co.uk/product-category/self-build-solutions/workbee-cnc-machine/workbee-machines/
- https://www.estlcam.de/steuerung_cnc_programme.php
- https://www.estlcam.de/steuerung_hardware.php and https://www.estlcam.de/hardware.php
- The issue comments for the owner's frame, drive, work area and spindle (not public).

## Tests (final head)

- Pinning test: `ooznest_workbee_states_the_smaller_envelope_and_feed` (`crates/app/tests/machine_library.rs`).
- `every_shipped_machine_mounts_and_speaks_its_declaration` (`machine.rs`) lists the new machine.
- `every_shipped_machine_lists_and_validates_clean`, `every_machine_file_in_assets_is_in_the_library` and `every_shipped_machine_stays_standard` read it.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p camcraft-app --test machine --test machine_library --test axis_direction`: 17, 12 and 33 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No post was run against the machine. No post is named. The posted G-code of each existing machine does not change.
- No heavy lane and no light lane were run.

Changelog: New library machine "Ooznest WorkBee 1000x1500 (Estlcam)": X 1200, Y 770, Z 88 mm, the smaller of the owner's and Ooznest's published travel; the owner must confirm the travel, and no post is named until the Estlcam post (#3735) ships.

Effort: medium

Fixes #3038

title: fix(post): preserve Mach4 tap feed precision
body:
## What changed

Mach4 G84 now writes feeds with three metric decimals or four inch decimals.
The post refuses a tap if the written F/S pitch differs by more than 0.01 percent.
The diagnostic names G84 and the operation.
Other feed moves keep their existing formatter.

## Cause

G84 used the general feed formatter, which kept one metric decimal or two inch decimals.
For example, 34.56 mm/min became F34.6 without a warning.
Inch conversion and integer spindle speeds can also change the written pitch.

## Tests

Effort: high.
The tested final tree is commit `9e311f317c9d45376f94a578327da05d834908ce`.
The branch starts at upstream `d54580cad`.
Validation used the current upstream reference `37aca7f8c`.
The gate used merge base `d54580cad` for this branch's three changed files.

Pins in `mach4_feed_decimals`:

- `mach4_g84_keeps_two_and_three_mm_feed_decimals`
- `mach4_g84_keeps_four_inch_feed_decimals`
- `mach4_refuses_tap_feed_rounding_that_changes_pitch`
- `mach4_refuses_tap_speed_rounding_that_changes_pitch`

All four pins failed on the unchanged Mach4 script before the fix.
The old script wrote F34.6 instead of F34.56 and F1.36 instead of F1.3606.
It emitted G84 without the expected pitch diagnostic in both refusal cases.
All four pins pass with the fix.

Mutation results:

- Restore the old formatter: both precision pins fail. The refusal pins pass.
- Remove the pitch guard: both refusal pins fail. The precision pins pass.
- Copy the complete script from `git show upstream/main:assets/posts/mach4.cps`: all four pins fail.
- Restore the fix: all four pins pass.

Final checks:

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test mach4_feed_decimals`: 4 passed.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 63 steps passed, 0 failed, 0 stalled.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- The quick gate ran `script_mach4` and the three `example_catalog*` suites. All passed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --dry-run`: no post heavy step exists.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main --only post`: 0 steps ran; exit 2, no matching step.

The new test binary pins numeric tap feeds and pitch refusals.
No Mach4 domain directory suite exists.
The decision file records the chosen formatter, guard, and alternatives.

## Goldens moved

None.
The Mach4 recorded golden suite and `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, and `example_catalog_edge_work` passed.
`git diff --stat upstream/main -- "*.nc" "*.cl"` produced no output.
No recorded programs changed, so no regeneration was needed.

## Not exercised

No physical Mach4 control or cutting test ran.
No full heavy lane ran because no post heavy step or ignored tap test exists.
The heavy plan reached only the unrelated `app heavy: probe_no_coolant` suite, which was excluded.
There is no UI change, so no screenshots are needed.

## Overlaps

None.
Checks covered all three changed files and all open PRs before the push.

Changelog: Mach4 keeps G84 tap feed precision and refuses written pitch errors above 0.01 percent.

Fixes #3701

title: fix(xtask): the quick submodule filter reads trait impls and scoped pub as shared
body:
## What changed

- `xtask/src/quick_subs.rs`: these items in a submodule count as shared, so the whole suite runs:
  - `impl <Trait> for <Type>` (also generic and `unsafe impl`);
  - `pub` after attributes on the same line (`#[allow(dead_code)] pub fn`);
  - `pub(crate)`, `pub(super)`, `pub(in ..)`.

  An inherent `impl Type { .. }` of a private type keeps the `<sub>::` filter.
- `xtask/src/braces.rs` (`code`):
  - `cr".."` and `cr#".."#` are raw strings now. Before, `cr"a \"` read the rest of the line as a string.
  - An escaped char literal (`'\''`, `'\'`) ends at its last quote.
- `xtask/src/scan.rs` (`test_fns`): the new pins found two defects that were already on main.
  - A `#[test]` below a line like `#[allow(dead_code)] pub fn helper() {}` made `test_fns` loop forever, with no limit on the memory. The attribute walk took the fn line, and the loop did not move on. Now the walk stops at a line that holds a fn, and the loop always moves on. A quick plan of such a file hung the gate.
  - `fn_re` did not read `pub(crate) fn` or the `const` / `unsafe` / `extern "C"` qualifiers. Such a line was read as an attribute of the next test, so an edit there ran only that test.
- `xtask/src/directory_tests.rs`: `run_step` returns libtest's stdout.
- `xtask/src/directory_edges_tests.rs`: the loop variable `whole` is now `outside_fns`.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/3711-quick-subs-guards.md`.

## Readings (base origin/main `d54580cad`, head after the merge of main)

| Plan | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run`, all steps | 1297 | 1297 |
| the same, heavy steps | 101 | 101 (the same list, checked with `diff`) |
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run` | 1 (xtask unit tests) | 1 |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` | 0 | 0 |

Note: the base has 101 heavy steps, not 99. Main has moved since PR #3709. This PR does not change the heavy plan.

## Pinning tests

- `directory_tests::selection::a_trait_impl_or_a_scoped_pub_in_a_submodule_runs_the_whole_suite` (8 cases)
- `directory_tests::selection::an_inherent_impl_of_a_private_type_keeps_the_submodule_filter`
- `directory_tests::selection::a_submodule_step_runs_only_that_submodule_in_real_cargo`: a real `cargo test --test many -- --test-threads=6 alpha::` on a fixture crate. It reads `1 passed` and `4 filtered out` (top, beta, shared, gated). The fixture run takes less than 1 min.
- `braces::tests::a_mod_token_in_a_literal_or_comment_is_blanked_and_the_real_one_stays` (16 rows: `"..."`, `\"`, `r".."`, `r#".."#`, `br".."`, `b".."`, `cr".."`, `cr#".."#`, `c".."`, nested block comments, `'"'`, `'\''`, `'\'`, `b'"'`, lifetimes, `//` comment)
- `braces::tests::a_block_comment_and_a_string_carry_over_to_the_next_line`
- `braces::tests::a_test_after_an_attributed_fn_on_one_line_is_found_and_the_scan_ends` (the loop defect and the `pub(crate)` / `const unsafe` fn lines)

Red first: the trait-impl pin hung on the old code (the `scan::test_fns` loop, found in the first run). On the old code, the `pub(crate)` case planned `--exact alpha::a1`. A full red-first run of all pins on the old code was not done.

## Quick gate (final head, `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=6`)

- `cargo test -j 6 -p xtask -- --test-threads=6`: 322 unit tests and all integration binaries pass.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No real cut gate.
- A full red-first run of each pin on the old code.

Effort: medium (not escalated).

Changelog: none
Process change: yes

Fixes #3711

title: docs(process): a review finding keeps the PR ready; no draft round trip
body:
Process change: yes

Changelog: none

## What changed
- A `needs-rework` finding does not turn a ready PR back into a draft. The author pushes the fix to the same PR. A push moves the head, so the earlier review and `merge-ready` do not count for the new head.
- An orange `conflicts` verdict still makes one of our own PRs a draft.
- The first `needs-rework` comment names the class of each finding and asks for one rule that closes the class.
- Files: `AGENTS.md` (three passages), `.claude/skills/review-prs/SKILL.md`, `.claude/skills/resolve-conflicts/SKILL.md`, and the decision file `docs/decisions/3727-ready-flag-stays.md`.

## Why
Data from 2026-11-20 to 2026-11-23: 30 PRs, 36 switches from ready to draft. 27 followed `needs-rework`, 3 followed `conflicts`, 6 had no label cause. The median time from ready to draft is 1.6 hours. #3283 and #3284 flipped three times each. Each round trip costs one more read and one more trial.

## Authority
The maintainer ordered this change on 2026-11-23: "Do your changes as a docs changes, push it and merge it and announce it one go.. On my call." The independent review is waived by that order.

## Not exercised
No code, no label and no workflow changes. The PROCESS_VERSION bump follows after the merge, as AGENTS.md says.

Fixes #3727

title: docs(process): a new integration test joins an existing directory suite
body:
## What changed

`AGENTS.md`, "Testing", has a new bullet:

> **New tests join a directory suite.** Add a new integration test to an
> existing domain directory suite (`tests/<suite>/<submod>.rs`) before you
> make a new top-level test binary (#3187).
> - The suites in `ISOLATED` (`xtask/src/lanes.rs`) and `SLOW_BINARIES`
>   (`xtask/src/plan.rs`) are exempt. They must stay separate binaries.
> - A new top-level file in `crates/*/tests/` needs a one-line reason in the
>   PR body.
> - Why: each test binary of `camcraft-app` is about 100 MB. The count of
>   test binaries went from 412 to 1,020 in ten days.

Other changes:
- `AGENTS.md`, "Code shape": one line that points to the new rule.
- `.claude/agents/PR-reviewer.md`, step 6, Placement bullet: check (d). A new top-level file under `crates/*/tests/` needs the one-line reason in the PR body, or it must belong to `ISOLATED` or `SLOW_BINARIES`. If not, the reviewer requests a change. No heading changed.
- `docs/decisions/3187-directory-suite-rule.md`: the decision entry.

## Decision

Owner's decision (live answer in the question dialog, 2026-11-23, relayed by the main session and recorded by the coordinator in a comment on #3187): "YES, add it." The question was: add the rule "a new integration test joins an existing directory suite", with the exemptions `ISOLATED` and `SLOW_BINARIES`?

The directory-suite support in `cargo xtask` is on main (#3186, #3706).

## Tests

The text of `AGENTS.md` and `PR-reviewer.md` is pinned by xtask tests. After the merge of `origin/main` (build fix `8f60c1f8e`, Gate-map fix `9ff5013f0`), `cargo test -j 6 -p xtask -- --test-threads=6` is green:
- unit tests of the binary: 316 passed, 0 failed;
- `catalog` 4, `docs_images` 4, `example_line_endings` 3, `merge_ready_skill` 3, `release_site_tests` 3, `review_artifacts` 3, `post_merge_concurrency` 2, `post_merge_report` 1, `post_merge_stall` 1: all passed.

Not exercised: no heavy lane (the diff is text only). `.claude/PROCESS_VERSION` is not edited. No existing test file is converted to a suite.

body:
**Main does not build `camcraft-app`.**

The build fails with `E0004 non-exhaustive patterns: OpParams::MultiAxisDeburr not covered` at `crates/app/src/commands/operation/recipe.rs:78`. Two PRs merged minutes apart:
- #3283 (`a59faa5b5`) added `OpParams::MultiAxisDeburr`.
- #3399 (`2dd93d7ad`) added the exhaustive match in `has_saved_geometry`. Its review trial-merged an older main without #3283.

Each trial merge was clean on its own. The clash shows only when both are on main.

**What changed:** one line. `OpParams::MultiAxisDeburr { exclude_edges, .. }` joins the `Deburr` arm. Its `exclude_edges` are source edge picks, exactly as for the 3-axis deburr, so a recipe of a multi-axis deburr with excluded edges counts as saved geometry. A recipe without excluded edges applies, the same as for Deburr.

**Tested:**
- `cargo check -p camcraft-app --all-targets` and `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets`: build again.
- `cut_recipe`: 20 passed.
- The compiler's exhaustiveness check is the pin for the missing arm.

title: fix(xtask): quick runs one changed submodule; the heavy filter reads flat suites through their modules
body:
## What changed

**Part 1: the quick `<submod>::` filter** (`xtask/src/quick_subs.rs`, hooks in `xtask/src/quick.rs`)

- A change outside the test fns of one submodule file of a directory suite (`tests/<suite>/<sub>.rs`) runs `cargo test -p <pkg> --test <suite> -- <sub>::`.
- The whole suite runs when:
  - `main.rs` changes outside its test fns;
  - the submodule has a `pub`/`pub(..)` item, `macro_rules!`, `macro_export` or `macro_use`, now or at the merge base;
  - the submodule is cfg-gated (not precise);
  - the text at the merge base is not available;
  - more than one submodule of the suite changes;
  - another rule picks the suite whole.
- The exact fn picks inside the filtered submodule are dropped, because the filter runs them.
- `describe` and `by_fn` move to `xtask/src/quick_describe.rs`. `quick.rs` was at 400 lines; it is now 362.
- Not done: per-source Gate maps in `map_modules`. A src change still runs the whole suite (the safe side). The decision file records this.

**Part 2: flat suites in the heavy filter** (`xtask/src/plan.rs`, `xtask/src/suites.rs`, `xtask/src/braces.rs`)

- `may_run_ignored` reads every suite through its module files, flat suites too. A `mod common;` line alone no longer gives a heavy step.
- These keep the heavy step (the safe answer):
  - `ignore`, `include!`, `#[path`, `#[cfg_attr(.., path = ..)]` in any file;
  - an unreadable file, or a module walk error;
  - a declared module whose file is absent;
  - a `mod` token in code that the line scan did not read as a declaration (`mod a; mod b;` on one line, `#[cfg(test)] mod b;`). The new `braces::code` blanks strings and comments for this count. `braces::count` now uses it.

Decision file: `docs/decisions/3706-xtask-submodule-filter.md`.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate release --dry-run`, heavy steps: **273 before, 99 after**. 174 steps are dropped. No step is added.
- Check script, independent of the module walk: for each dropped step, `grep -rln ignore` over the entry file, plus `tests/<m>.rs` and all of `tests/<m>/` for each `mod <m>` of the entry. Result: **174 suites, 0 with a match.**

title: fix(xtask): a failed test build stops the quick gate and names the metadata error
body:
## What changed

This is a partial fix for #3601. The cause of the metadata errors is not proven, and the issue stays open.

- `xtask/src/build_stop.rs` (new): the stop rule and the metadata diagnostic.
- `xtask/src/exec.rs`: in a plan that runs one step at a time (quick), a failed step whose name ends in ` build (--no-run)` stops the plan. Before, only `debug build (--no-run)` stopped it. The summary lists each later step as `SKIP ... not run (build failed: <step>)`. The gate exits red, and the FAIL row names the build step.
- `xtask/src/exec.rs`: a failed build step whose log has `found invalid metadata files for crate`, `E0786`, `found possibly newer version of crate` or `E0460` prints one `BUILD FAULT` block. The block names the crate of the error and says that the build output is bad, not the tests. It gives two commands to try, one at a time:
  1. the same gate with `CAMCRAFT_GATE_JOBS=4`;
  2. `cargo clean -p <package>`, with the `-p` package of the step (`camcraft-ui` for the ui step).
- The gate does not retry and does not clean by itself. The job budget rule (#2814) does not change.
- Each stopped step gets a log with the one line `not run (build failed: <step>)`. `select::log_failed` reads that line as a failed step. Thus `cargo xtask gate quick --failed gate-logs/<run>` runs the build step and each stopped step (review of this PR). The summary row of a stopped step is `SKIP`, not `FAIL`, so the post-merge report and the light-lane note do not count it as a test failure.
- The `BUILD FAULT` block shows only for a failed step whose arguments have `--no-run`. A test step whose output quotes E0786 gets no block.
- `.claude/skills/gate/SKILL.md`: one paragraph says what quick does after a failed build, and how to rerun after a stop.
- `docs/decisions/3601-gate-build-failure-stops.md`: the choices, the dropped options, and the reading of the seed lead (`xtask/src/seed.rs`).

## Readings

- Red first: with the old stop rule, `a_failed_per_crate_build_stops_the_plan_like_the_whole_gate_build` and `quick_plan_stops_after_a_failed_per_crate_build` failed (the suite step ran after the failed build). For the review fix: without the stopped-step logs and without the `--no-run` check, `quick_plan_stops_after_a_failed_per_crate_build` (the `--failed` part) and `a_test_step_that_quotes_a_metadata_error_gives_no_block` failed.
- `cargo test -j 6 -p xtask -- --test-threads=6`: 301 passed, 0 failed (lib), all other xtask binaries green.
- `cargo clippy -j 6 -p xtask --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main --dry-run`: prints the plan, 1 step (`xtask unit tests`). An earlier body said 1168 steps: that was the batch fallback without `--base`.

## Pinning tests

`xtask/src/build_stop_tests.rs`:
- `a_failed_per_crate_build_stops_the_plan_like_the_whole_gate_build`
- `metadata_errors_name_the_crate_the_jobs_and_the_package_to_clean` (the three error texts: E0786 for `accesskit`, E0786 for `test`, E0460 for `png`)
- `an_ordinary_compile_error_gives_no_metadata_block`
- `quick_plan_stops_after_a_failed_per_crate_build` (a quick `Run` on a temp fixture; the build fails on a bad cargo flag, so nothing compiles; then `--failed` on its log directory selects the build step and each stopped step)
- `a_test_step_that_quotes_a_metadata_error_gives_no_block`

## Not exercised

- No real 16-job build that gives E0786 or E0460. The block is tested on log text only.
- The lanes path (batch, release, and the quick fallback to batch) is not changed. Its prebuilds already stop the suites.
- E0462 alone does not start the block (it came together with E0786 or E0460 in the reported runs).

title: fix(xtask): asset selection, the catalog check and the heavy filter read directory suites
body:
## What changed

- `xtask/src/assets.rs` (`suites_for`): the asset match reads the entry file and each module file of a suite (`suites::sources(&suites::entry(...))`). A directory suite whose child module names an asset is now selected (#923). A flat suite whose `mod x;` file names an asset is also selected. This can only add suites.
- `xtask/src/catalog.rs` (`map_catalog`): the check uses `suites::entry(root, "app", "example_catalog")`. The flat file is still found first, so the behaviour on main does not change.
- `xtask/src/plan.rs` (`may_run_ignored`): a directory suite (`tests/<b>/main.rs`) is read through all its module files. A `mod x;` line alone does not plan a heavy step. These still plan a heavy step: `ignore`, `include!` or `#[path` in any file, an unreadable file, a module walk error, and a declared module whose file is absent.
- `xtask/src/suites.rs`: new `sources_and_missing`, which also counts the declared modules whose file is absent. `sources` keeps its signature.
- A flat suite keeps the old rule: a `mod x;` line plans a heavy step. A flat walk removes about 175 heavy steps of the cut plan. That change needs its own review, so it is recorded in #3706.
- Decision file: `docs/decisions/3186-xtask-directory-suites.md`.

## Not in this PR

The `quick.rs` part of #3186 (per-source Gate maps and the `--test <suite> <submod>::` filter) is in the follow-up #3706. It needs a new pick kind in `Picks`, `describe` and `steps`. That is more than half of this work. Thus this PR says `Refs #3186`.

title: fix(examples): regenerate the first router part after the tabbed contour entry change
body:
## Cause

Commit `ac03087a3` (PR #3684) changed where a tabbed outside 2D Contour starts its untabbed levels. Now an untabbed level that is alone on its level starts at the same point as the tabbed level. The committed demo `examples/first-router-part.camproj` kept the old cached path of `2D Contour1`. The test `first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal` rebuilds the demo by commands. It compares the two posted programs and failed at `crates/app/tests/first_router_part.rs:282`. The contour stamp did not change, so the old cache read as fresh.

## What changed

The demo was regenerated by the documented commands only. There is no hand edit.

1. `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test first_router_part` writes `examples/first-router-part.camproj`.
2. `camcraft-cli process examples/first-router-part.camproj -o examples/first-router-part.nc` writes the program.

## Readings

`examples/first-router-part.nc`: only the `2D Contour1` section changes (lines 81-132, section header at line 78).

- The line count stays at 165.
- The depths (Z-4, Z-8, Z-9 and the tab level Z-12) do not change.
- The feeds (F400 plunge, F1800 cut), S9500, and the Z15 and Z2 heights do not change.
- Old start of the untabbed levels Z-4, Z-8, Z-9: X173.514 Y24.198, with an arc lead into the corner at X170 Y27. Old exit: X167.711 Y23.694.
- New start of the same levels: X176 Y80.991, with an arc lead onto the right side at X173 Y77.991. New exit: X176 Y74.991.
- The new start is the start of the tabbed level Z-12. The Z-12 level does not change.
- The drill and pocket sections do not change.

`examples/first-router-part.camproj`: the writer made these changes outside the contour cache.

- `"version": 73` becomes `78`. This is the current file version of the writer.
- In the stored machine block, `"kind": "mill"` becomes `"router"`. The source is the machine file `assets/machines/sienci-altmill-4x4.mch`, changed by `afa612d2f`.
- In the stored machine block, `"post": "grblHAL"` is new. The source is the same machine file, changed by `2fdc4200f`.

All other changes are in the cached moves of `2D Contour1`. No operation parameter changes. No stamp changes. The `2D Pocket1` and `Drill1` caches do not change. The posted program changes only in `2D Contour1`.

## Tests (quick gate, debug, on the final head)

- `camcraft-app --test first_router_part`: 4 passed. It was red before: 3 passed, 1 failed at line 282.
- `camcraft-app --test first_part_programs`: 2 passed. This test pins the `.nc`.
- `camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 39 passed, 4 ignored.
- `camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting`: 2 passed.
- `camcraft-motion --test contour_tab_entry`: 3 passed. This test pins #3684.

The guide pages that name the demo quote no changed contour line or number. No guide file changes.

## Not changed / not exercised

- The op stamp salt (`crates/app/src/operation/stamp.rs:46`) is not changed. The comment at that line asks for a bump only when a verify law that a cache records changes. No written rule asks for a bump when generator output changes. Thus a project saved before #3684 posts the old contour start until the user regenerates the operation.
- Heavy lanes and the light lane were not run. This is a `P2` PR with no code change.
- The GUI was not opened.

Changelog: none

Fixes #3698

title: fix(post): the Haas feed word keeps its decimals, so a tap feed gives the exact pitch
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/haas.cps`, `ff()`: the F word keeps its fraction. An mm feed has up to three decimals. An inch feed has up to four decimals (it had two). The post trims the trailing zeros and always writes the point (`F600.`, `F34.5`, `F133.2`, `F1.3583`). One formatter writes each Haas feed, not only G84.
- `assets/posts/haas.cps`, new `tapPitchHolds()`, called in `onCycle()` for G84: the post compares the pitch of the written words (F / S) with the stream pitch (feed / rpm). If the difference is more than 0.01 percent of the pitch, the post refuses the cycle by name through `msg()`. It writes no partial block.
- `docs/decisions/3694-haas-tap-feed-exact.md`: the options, the option taken, the source of the feed format (Haas Mill Operator's Manual 96-8000, Setting 77) and the worst case of the residual pitch error.

## Readings (before -> after)

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| G84, mm, 34.5 mm/min at S115 (M1.4 x 0.3) | `F35.` | `F34.5` |
| G84, mm, 133.2 mm/min at S333 (M2 x 0.4) | `F133.` | `F133.2` |
| G84, inch, 34.5 mm/min at S115 | `F1.36` | `F1.3583` |
| G84, inch, 635 mm/min at S500 (1/4-20) | `F25.` | `F25.` |
| G1, mm, 50.8 mm/min | `F51.` | `F50.8` |
| G1, mm, 12.4 mm/min | `F12.` | `F12.4` |
| G84, inch, 2 mm/min at S100 | `F0.08` (1.6 percent off) | refused by name |
| G84, mm, 34.5 mm/min at 115.4 rpm (written S115) | `F35.` | refused by name |

## Pinning tests

`crates/post/tests/haas_feed_decimal_point.rs`:

- `haas_g84_writes_the_exact_tap_feed_in_mm` (new)
- `haas_g84_writes_the_tap_feed_at_four_inch_decimals` (new)
- `haas_refuses_a_tap_pitch_its_words_cannot_hold` (new)
- `haas_keeps_the_fraction_of_an_mm_feed` (new, 12.4 mm/min, #3692)
- `crates/app/tests/program_units.rs` `every_inch_post_writes_the_mm_program_in_inches`, with the two new Haas inch goldens.
- `haas_writes_every_mm_feed_word_with_its_point`: the pin at line 210 changed from `F51.` to `F50.8`. This is the intended change.

The five tests are red with the `haas.cps` of `origin/main` (`F35.` for `F34.5`, `F1.36` for `F1.3583`) and green with the fix.

## Quick gate (head 30c4c7ef0)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-post` (whole crate, `--no-fail-fast`): all binaries pass.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app` with `--test` for `conformance`, `rigid_tapping`, `tap_hand`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle`, `fine_bore_cycle`, `control_comp`, `wear_comp`, `program_entry`, `golden_cl`, `example_catalog`: all pass.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --lib -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Review fix, run on head 30c4c7ef0: `cargo test -p camcraft-app` with `--test program_units`, `--test post_unit_word`, `--test program_info` and `--test conformance`, and `cargo test -p camcraft-post --test haas_feed_decimal_point`. All pass.
- The mm goldens did not change. They hold only whole feeds (`tap_plate.nc` `F750.`, `synth_haas.nc` `F240.`).
- Two Haas inch goldens changed: `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/haas/contour_plate_with_hole.nc` and `drill_peck.nc`. `program_units` was red before the new files were written (`every_inch_post_writes_the_mm_program_in_inches`). The new files come from `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test program_units`. A script compared them with the old files. Only F words changed (43 words). title: fix(post): Haas feed words carry a decimal point
body:
## What changed

- `assets/posts/haas.cps` `ff()`: each F word gets a decimal point, in mm and in inch. The function puts its result through `pt()`, the helper that the length words use (#1836). The zero literal is `0.`.
- The mm feed stays rounded to a whole mm/min. Precision does not change.
- A positive feed that rounds to zero (under 0.5 mm/min, or under 0.005 in/min) keeps its fraction. Before, it posted `F0`.
- A positive feed below the inch four-decimal step is refused by name (`msg()`). It is never posted as `F0.`.
- Dwell P (ms), S, T, H and D stay integers.
- `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`: the #1836 rule gets one line for the Haas feed word.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3681-haas-feed-decimal-point.md`.

Source: Haas Mill Operator's Manual 96-8000 (2009), Settings, "77 - Scale Integer F". The reporter cited rev V. A web check of the same manual agrees with the issue. At the default, an mm control reads an integer F with three implied decimals. The manual recommends a decimal point on each F word.

## Readings (before / after)

- `nc/haas/arc_planes.nc`: `G18 G3 X15. Y0. Z0. I-5. K0. F600` / `... F600.`
- `golden/bore/haas.nc`: `G86 X10. Y10. Z-12. R2. F120` / `... F120.`
- `comp.rs` Haas engage: `G1 G42 X0. Y0. Z-2. D2 F500` / `... F500.`
- Inch, 50.8 mm/min: `F2` / `F2.`
- 0.3 mm/min: `F0` / `F0.3`

Goldens: 30 Haas files, 658 lines changed. A normalising diff (strip the point from `F<digits>.`) gives 0 lines that differ in anything other than an F word. No non-Haas golden changed. No Haas golden has an F word without a point now.

## Pinning tests

New: `crates/post/tests/haas_feed_decimal_point.rs`. It was red on the old `haas.cps` (4 of 4 failed) and is green with the fix.
- `haas_writes_every_mm_feed_word_with_its_point`
- `haas_writes_every_inch_feed_word_with_its_point`
- `haas_keeps_the_fraction_of_a_feed_that_rounds_to_zero`
- `haas_refuses_a_feed_below_its_smallest_inch_step`

The mm and inch tests check each F word against `F<digits>.<digits>*`. They cover:
- G1 moves, a plunge and an arc;
- G31 probe moves (guard, touch, retreat);
- canned cycles G73, G76, G81, G82, G83, G84, G85, G86 and G89. The test fails if one of these cycles does not post.

Updated text pins:
- `crates/post/tests/comp.rs:129`
- `crates/post/tests/fine_bore_cycle.rs:176` (the context pack did not list this one)
- `crates/app/tests/fine_bore_cycle.rs:291`

## Gate (final head, -j 6)

- `camcraft-post`, full suite: 129 binaries, 1050 passed, 0 failed.
- `camcraft-app`: 40 binaries, 323 passed, 0 failed. These are each app test binary that names Haas (`mcp_live` excluded), plus `conformance`, `control_comp`, `program_entry`, `wear_comp`, `post_cycle_feed_spindle`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive` and `example_catalog_edge_work`.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- Targeted heavy step (P1 rule): `cargo xtask gate heavy --only "app heavy: conformance"`: ok, 493 s. Note: the binary has no `#[ignore]`d tests, so this step ran 0 tests (7 filtered out). The debug `conformance` run above compared the Haas goldens (7 passed).

## Not exercised

- No real Haas control. The manual text is the only check of the control behaviour.
- `mcp_live` and the UI suites did not run.
- The light lane did not run.
- The other 21 post scripts are not in this PR. A follow-up issue holds them.

Changelog: The Haas post writes each feed word with a decimal point (`F600.`), so the feed is correct at each value of Haas Setting 77.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #3681

title: fix(ui): a relative model link resolves against the project folder
body:
## What changed

- `crates/ui/src/model_link_watch.rs`: the new function `resolve` joins a relative link path to the folder of the open project file (`state.project_path`). An absolute link stays as it is. A project that is not saved has no folder, so its link stays as it is.
- The watch reads the digest from the resolved path. It queues the re-import with the resolved path.
- `linked_name` is now `linked_to`. It finds the linked model by the link text or by the resolved path. It also gives the link text.
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs` (`finish_import`): a re-import of a linked file keeps the link text as it was written. Thus a relative link stays relative after a re-import.
- The app layer has no function that resolves a link path. The app tests (`example_catalog`, `model_link`) do not run the link watch. Thus the fix is in the UI watch only. The app crate does not change.

## Readings

Before (origin/main 10a0a39c0, Windows, `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test catalog_render`):

```
test catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly ... FAILED
...\examples\catalog\3d\rough-finish\rough-finish.camproj failed to open: rough-finish kept as it is: its linked file model/rough-finish.obj cannot be read (The system cannot find the path specified. (os error 3))
```

After (this branch): `catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly ... ok`, `test result: ok. 2 passed; 0 failed; 1 ignored`.

## Pinning tests

- `model_link_tests::a_relative_link_resolves_against_the_project_folder`: a link `part.stl` in a temp folder, with the working directory `crates/ui`. The watch gives no link error. A change of the file imports it again, and the link stays `part.stl`.
- `model_link_tests::an_absolute_link_ignores_the_project_folder_and_an_unsaved_project_keeps_the_path`: an absolute link is read as it is when the project is in a different folder. A relative link of a project that is not saved keeps the old reading and is refused by name.
- `catalog_render::catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly` (not changed).

## Quick gate (head 64bace673)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test catalog_render`: 2 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib model_link`: 5 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

## Not exercised

- The GUI on a desktop. The tests use the headless state only.
- The real open of a project from disk with a relative link and a file change after the open. The test sets `project_path` directly.
- The MCP and CLI paths. They do not run the link watch.
- No heavy lane. This is a P2 UI change.
- `crates/ui/src/state.rs` is already longer than 400 lines. This PR adds 10 lines to `finish_import` and does not split the file.

Changelog: A linked model with a relative path is now read from the folder of the project file, not from the folder the program started in.

title: fix(2d): enter the first tabbed contour level where the levels above cut
body:
## Cause

The untabbed levels of a 2D Contour start at their own seat (the axis start or the lead-room reseat). The tabbed levels cut windows between the tabs. The first window began after the last tab, not at that seat. So the lead-in of the first tabbed window stood in sheet that no level above cut. The dive fed from the plunge height to the level in one move (`contour_step.rs` `graze`, `descent_dive.rs` `feed_down`).

The context pack named a second cause: the tabbed levels skip the reseat. On the fixture, the raw start and the reseated start are the same point. That change alone had no effect, and this PR does not make it.

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/tab_clear.rs`: new `level_start`. It returns the untabbed ring, started at the point where window 0 of the tabbed levels begins.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/contour.rs`: the untabbed levels of a tabbed ring use `level_start`. The tab layout does not change.
- Exception: a ring keeps its old seam if it shares a level with another ring of its band, or with another band of a whole-model contour (`PreparedBand::room`). Two rings that cut the same path must split it at the same seam. Without this exception, the path crossing law blocked the post in `contour_whole_step.rs` case 1 and case 2 (`Crossing { moves: [15, 59] }`).
- A contour with no tabs, a ring that walks no tabbed level, and a picked start do not change.

## Readings

Fixture `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs`:
- L-shape, Outside, `bottom_z` -18.3, stepdown 4.5, 4 tabs 10 x 3, D6.
- Plunge entry, Arc lead r3, clearance 25, retract 12.

"Disc floor" is the highest floor under the full tool disc that the earlier level passes left. "Crescent" is how far the disc reaches past the cut under its centre.

PLANAR links, before (origin/main 44c13a01d):

| level | entry XY | plunge Z | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| -4.5, -9, -13.5, -15.3 | (43.514, -5.802) | 2 -> level | 4.5, 4.5, 4.5, 1.8 | 0 |
| -18 window 0 | (46.000, 8.865) | 2 -> -18 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18 windows 1-3 | (10.153, -6), (-6, 29.525), (21, 30.029) | 12 -> -18 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18.3 windows 0-3 | as -18 | 2 or 12 -> -18.3 | 0.3 | 0 |

PLANAR links, after:

| level | entry XY | plunge Z | below disc floor | crescent |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| -4.5, -9, -13.5, -15.3 | (46.000, 8.865) | 2 -> level | 4.5, 4.5, 4.5, 1.8 | 0 |
| -18 window 0 | (46.000, 8.865) | 2 -> -18 | 2.7 | 0 |
| -18 windows 1-3 | unchanged | 12 -> -18 | 18.0 | 2.501 |
| -18.3 windows 0-3 | unchanged | 2 or 12 -> -18.3 | 0.3 | 0 |

Stay-down ramp preset (`level: KeepDown`, `transition: Ramp`), after: window 0 enters at the untabbed start (46.000, 8.865). The levels below the first do not cut the lead-in, so the disc floor there is -4.5. The dive is 13.5 mm below it, with a 2.501 mm crescent. Before, it was 18.0 mm at (46.000, 8.865) with the untabbed start at (43.514, -5.802).

Lead None: every window dives on the ring, 2.7 mm below the tab-top level, before and after. Window 0 now enters at the untabbed start.

Tab hops are not changed: a feed rise from the level to Z12, a rapid, and a plunge back to the same level.

## What is not fixed here (scope split by the coordinator)

- Refs #3678 (P3): a guard for a dive deeper than one stepdown below the disc floor. It covers windows 1-3 (18 mm, 2.5 mm crescent) and the stay-down ramp window 0 (13.5 mm). It also covers a ring that keeps its seam by the exception above.
- Refs #3679: the verifier passes such a plunge with a centre-cutting tool. The issue has the evidence (the reporter's `verify` result and a code read). No verifier law is added in this PR.

## Pins (red first)

`crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_entry.rs`:
- `the_first_tabbed_window_enters_where_the_levels_above_cut_its_lead_in`
- `the_first_tabbed_window_of_the_stay_down_ramp_enters_at_the_untabbed_start`
- `a_tabbed_level_without_a_lead_enters_in_the_kerf_of_the_level_above`

Each test was red on origin/main: window 0 did not enter at the untabbed start. The pinned window 1-3 readings change on purpose with #3678.

## Files that moved

- `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs/contour-tabs.nc`: 44 lines. It was regenerated with `cargo xtask catalog --case 2d/contour-tabs`. The Z4 and Z2 levels now lead in at `X51. Y-6.515`, where the Z0 tabbed level enters. Before, they led in at `X38.514 Y-30.802`. The Z0 lines (`G00 X51. Y-6.515 Z8.` / `G01 X51. Y-6.515 Z0. F300`) did not change. Now the two levels above cut that point.
- `examples/catalog/2d/contour-tabs/contour-tabs.camproj`: the cached toolpath of the same case (348 lines). The open PR #3251 also changes this file. #3251 will need a refresh after this PR merges.
- No golden moved: `golden_cl`, `conformance` and `first_part_programs` pass with no change.

## Gate (final head, debug, `-j 6`)

- motion: `--lib`, `--no-run`, and these binaries pass: `contour_auto_side`, `contour_inside_ramp`, `contour_outside_floor`, `contour_start`, `contour_start_comp`, `contour_tab_bridge`, `contour_tab_entry`, `contour_tab_height`, `contour_tab_lead`, `contour_tab_necks`, `contour_tabs`, `contour_whole`, `contour_whole_new_outline`, `contour_whole_no_floor`, `control_comp`, `lead_room`, `machining2d`, `pass_start_levels`.
- app: `--lib`, and these binaries pass: `conformance`, all 13 `contour_*`, `docs_troubleshooting`, `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `first_part_programs`, `golden_cl`, `mcp_verify`, `offset_pass_start`, `verify`.
- `cargo xtask catalog --check`: pass.
- clippy `-D warnings`: motion `--all-targets`, app `--lib`: clean.

## Not run

- No heavy lane and no light lane (P3).
- No app window and no reporter file. The q07 project was not opened.
- No fresh `verify` run of the fixture (see #3679).

Effort: high (no escalation).

Changelog: 2D Contour with tabs: the levels above the tabs now start where the first tab window enters, so that window dives into the cut of the level above and not into uncut sheet.

title: fix(sim): march 256 steps and give an exact verdict at exhaustion
body:
## Cause

The stock preview march stopped after 64 steps (`crates/ui/src/trace.wgsl` and its CPU twin `crates/sim/src/stock_sim/preview/march.rs`). Over a flat face, each step is 0.9 x the height above the face. Thus a ray at a small angle to a faced floor comes near the floor slowly. At 64 steps, the ray got status 2 (no verdict). `composite.wgsl` discards each pixel that is not a hit, so the grid showed through the stock.

## What changed

- `MAX_STEPS` is 256 in the two twins (it was 64).
- New exhaustion verdict in the two twins (`exhausted`). A ray that uses all its steps gets a hit only when material is proved on the ray:
  - the last sample is inside, or
  - the sample one cell further along the ray is inside (the probe of the existing hit law).
- Then 6 bisections of that one-cell bracket put the hit within 1/64 cell of the surface, on the material side (`BISECT`).
- Each other exhausted ray keeps status 2. A near miss is never painted.
- The hit law, the miss law and `composite.wgsl` do not change.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3612-preview-march-steps.md`.

## Readings (CPU twin)

Fixture: a 10 x 10 x 5 box on 1 mm cells, faced to z 4.5 with a flat r 2 tool. The frame is 64 x 64. The eye is 30 mm from the floor centre. The table gives the rays with no verdict, for each step cap, before the fallback:

| Angle above the floor | 64 (old) | 96 | 128 | 192 | 256 | 512 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 60 deg | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 30 deg | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 10 deg | 2 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 5 deg | 70 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 3 deg | 152 | 42 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 2 deg | 166 | 62 | 6 | 0 | 0 | 0 |
| 1 deg | 112 | 70 | 64 | 24 | 0 | 0 |

- At 64, rays that surely meet the box read as a miss: 5 deg 8, 3 deg 68, 2 deg 30. After the fix: 0 at each angle.
- Rays that surely miss the box and are painted: 0 at each cap, with and without the fallback.
- The fallback alone at 64: 5 deg 70 -> 32, 3 deg 152 -> 56. It cannot help a ray that passes above the floor and misses. That ray keeps status 2, which is correct.
- After the fix (256 + fallback): 0 unresolved from 60 deg down to 1 deg. At 0.5 deg, 16 rays have no verdict, and none of them is a sure hit.
- CPU preview time of the fixture (debug, whole frame with the column cache): 1 deg view 577 ms at 64 -> 643-661 ms at 256 (about +11 %). The other views are in the noise. On the GPU, only the pixels that used to run out pay for the extra steps.

## Pinning test

- `crates/sim/tests/stock_preview.rs`: `a_grazing_faced_floor_resolves_and_stays_see_through`. It compares each ray with an analytic box silhouette (one cell of slack):
  - From 60 deg to 1 deg: 0 unresolved, and no sure hit reads as a miss.
  - At each angle, 0.5 deg included: no sure miss is painted.
  - At 64 steps, this test fails (see the table).

## Gate (head 12c6d0805)

- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim -j 6`: 95 binaries, 857 passed, 0 failed.
- `CAMCRAFT_REQUIRE_GPU=1 cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test trace_parity -- --test-threads=1`: 5 passed. The tests ran on an adapter (with the variable set, a missing adapter is an error, not a skip). `gpu.unresolved == cpu.unresolved` stays green.
- Same for `--test trace_composite`: 5 passed. `--test gpu_render`: 19 passed, 1 ignored.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -j 6`: 1516 passed, 0 failed, 8 ignored.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings` and `-p camcraft-ui --all-targets`: clean.

## Not exercised

- No app window was opened. The picture of the user is not reproduced on screen. The fix is shown on the CPU twin and by the GPU parity test.
- `trace_parity` and `trace_composite` have no GPU lock (#3605). This PR does not change these files. I ran them with `--test-threads=1`.
- No heavy lane. This is a P3 PR.

Changelog: The cut stock preview no longer shows holes on a faced floor at a low view angle: the march takes up to 256 steps and gives a hit only where material is proved on the ray.

Effort: high (no escalation)

Fixes #3612

title: feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal
body:
feat(multiaxis): stated rotary axis from the machine line, with a disagreed-face refusal

## What changed

Issue #2772, parts 1 and 2 of the plan in
`docs/decisions/2772-rotary-4axis-refusal.md`. The rotary kinds
(Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel, Rotary Offset) read their rotation
axis from a STATEMENT first; today's free fit is the fallback, and
nothing stated keeps every behaviour bit for bit.

1. The stated-axis resolver, `camcraft_app::rotary_stated` over
   `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::axis_stated`:
   - the op's own `stated_axis` direction first, else the mounted
     machine's stated rotary lines (a stated `axis` vector, else the
     RS-274 letter's line - the index-swing clause's own
     `rotary_line` reading, so one law reads both doors);
   - each line anchored through the setup's work offset origin (the
     indexed post's setup law: the WCS sits on the rotary
     centreline), canonicalized the fit's own way (signed, pinned to
     the `o . u = 0` foot), so a part truly on the line keeps the
     fitted path move for move;
   - JUDGED, never trusted: the fit's own concurrency share,
     coarseness skip and bearing law about the stated line
     (`axis_stated::judged_any`). A disagreement refuses by name:
     the part's own fitted axis and the two acts that fix it when
     the model is a revolve placed off the line; the freeform's
     4-axis wording (with the pinned "share no rotation axis"
     words) when no axis fits at all. Never a silent fall back to a
     free fit when a line was stated. A stated line that leans or is
     no direction refuses by name, as the swing clause does.
2. The caller switch, stated first / fit fallback:
   - `fixture::rotary_axis_of` - feeds the sim's chord pass
     (`stock_sim_rotary::rotary_plan`), the first traverse and the
     post gate's struck-steel law (`fixture_struck`): all three
     follow with no change of their own;
   - `first_traverse::turned_axis` - already prefers the job axis,
     which is now the stated-or-fitted line;
   - `rotary_law::rotary_into` - the radial field verdict takes the
     job's resolved axis (`rotary_axis`), keeping its fail-closed
     Gouge for the nothing-known case;
   - `rotary_picks::usable` and the centre-cutting audit's
     `revolved_bar_stated` - judge and read the resolved axis;
   - the letter door `rotary_gate::letter_gate` (moved from
     generate.rs) - a stated line answers the letter without a fit,
     held to the machine inventory;
   - the three motion kernels grow `*_stated` entries
     (`rotary_contour_stated`, `rotary_parallel_over_stated`,
     `rotary_offset_stated`) that take the judged axis; the plain
     entries keep the fit inside, so turning, drilling and every
     existing golden path are untouched.
3. The op param: `stated_axis` on the three arms - a direction
   ratio, never unit-scaled (the machine file's own law for its
   `axis` vector), through the WCS origin, overriding the machine
   line. UI edit (the rotary page's Passes tab, an armed group of
   three direction numbers riding the existing EditOperationParams
   commit), MCP patch (`edit_operation`'s merge patch over the DTO,
   automatic), project round-trip (`stated_axis`, PROJECT_VERSION
   steps v77 -> v78: an older reader must refuse rather than drop
   the statement and turn the part about an axis the user never
   named).
4. The cache stamp: the op's own direction, the machine's stated
   lines and the WCS anchor enter the digest ONLY when a line is
   stated - no cached path of a document without one goes stale.

## The readings

- The WCS origin is the stated line's anchor: the post subtracts the
  work offset from world coordinates, so in program coordinates the
  rotary centreline passes through the WCS origin - the same law the
  index-swing clause and the lathe spindle law read.
- The judge is the fit's own (`axis.rs`'s `data_of` + `judge`): the
  tolerance, the 90% concurrency share, the coarseness skip and the
  bearing law, evaluated about the stated line instead of a candidate
  from the eigen search. On the reporter's helical rotor the judge
  fails and the radial raster stays LOCKED (the decision doc's law:
  its radial pose can gouge on helical lobes) - the disagreement
  refusal says so and names the 4-axis case.
- A machine whose work-turning rotary states no `axis` vector keeps
  today's fit (absent is not stated, never zero). A trunnion's
  work-turning pair is read in chain order and the first line the
  model holds wins, so a standing revolve takes the C and a lying
  one takes the A.

## Pinning tests

- motion `axis_stated_tests`: a revolve holds its stated line and
  reads the fitted axis bit for bit; the canonical line is signed
  and pinned; a stated line away from the part names the part's own
  axis; the helical screw refuses with the 4-axis wording; an empty
  mesh refuses like the fit.
- app `rotary_stated_axis`:
  `a_stated_machine_line_generates_the_fitted_path` (microARC 4 +
  laid revolve: move-for-move the fitted program),
  `the_millturns_stated_c_carries_the_standing_bar` (C answered
  without a fit, the stamp runs),
  `the_screw_rotor_on_a_stated_A_is_refused_by_name` (the radial
  kinds stay locked on the screw),
  `the_screw_rotor_without_a_stated_line_keeps_the_old_refusal`
  (the pinned "share no rotation axis" words untouched),
  `a_stated_line_away_from_the_part_names_the_parts_own_axis` (both
  the disagreement and the letter-door wordings),
  `a_stated_line_the_part_holds_on_a_machine_that_has_it_generates`
  (the op's own statement, either sign),
  `a_work_offset_move_moves_the_stated_line_and_refuses` (the
  anchor is the WCS's own position),
  `the_stated_axis_round_trips_the_project_file` (v78 round-trip,
  v77 steps up unstated),
  `a_v77_file_opens_and_a_newer_file_is_refused` (the version pin).
- app `rotary_gate`: `a_stated_line_answers_the_letter_without_a_fit`
  (the screw's fit refuses, the stated line still answers).
- app `rotary_field_parity`:
  `the_stated_axis_parallel_reads_the_radial_law` - the heavy-lane
  parity of the stated-A program (the field eye vs the radial law,
  `#[ignore]`d like its three siblings; the quick suite pins the
  path equality, this lane proves the stated axis flows the whole
  sim pipeline at the verdict class).
- The continuous 4-axis example regenerated at v78 (its op follows
  the microARC's stated line - the same path the fit reads).

## What was NOT exercised

- The heavy parity lane runs at a cut, not here (the quick gate
  pins the path equality instead).
- No UI pixel snapshot is touched (release-lane only).

## Not included (the issue stays open)

- The RADIAL DROP FINISH KERNEL and the radial-step roughing
  (decision part 3/4): the live claim on
  `mkinney:issue/2772-radial-drop` holds that work. This PR's
  disagreement refusal keeps the radial kinds locked on helical
  parts until that kernel can consume the stated axis safely.
- No 360-degree radial drop finish for Rotary Parallel, no
  Doosan/Fanuc posting of one - same slice.

Changelog: Rotary Contour, Rotary Parallel and Rotary Offset read a
stated rotation axis first (the operation's own direction, else the
machine's stated rotary line through the work offset origin), judged
against the model's faces - a part on the stated line cuts the fitted
path unchanged, a part whose faces disagree refuses by name (the
4-axis case named), and nothing stated keeps the fitted axis (v78
project files).

title: fix(geometry): import AC1015 DXF files with CLASSES and layout objects
body:
## What changed

The DXF reader now imports an AutoCAD 2000 (AC1015) export with a `CLASSES` section.

- The reader skips the `CLASSES`, `THUMBNAILIMAGE` and `ACDSDATA` sections to their `ENDSEC`. These sections hold no geometry. A missing `ENDSEC` is a named error. Each other unknown section stays refused.
- The `OBJECTS` reader reads a balanced group 102 bracket (`102 {ACAD_REACTORS` .. `102 }`) as opaque data. An unclosed, nested, unopened or malformed bracket is a named error.
- A `DICTIONARY` keeps all its checks from #3176.
- Each other object (for example `LAYOUT`, `ACDBDICTIONARYWDFLT`, `ACDBPLACEHOLDER`) is an inert record. The reader takes only its handle and its owner. The object must join the ownership graph of #3176. An unowned object, a duplicate handle and an object count over the limit are refused.
- Second review (new in this push): a record with an entity name (`LINE`, `LWPOLYLINE`, `INSERT` and so on) in `OBJECTS`, `CLASSES`, `THUMBNAILIMAGE` or `ACDSDATA` is refused. Before this change, such a record without the `AcDbEntity` marker was dropped with no diagnostic. The list is `ENTITY_KINDS` in `crates/geometry/src/dxf/entities.rs`.

This change loosens a refusal that #3176 added on purpose. `docs/decisions/3450-dxf-classes-section.md` says how the #3176 law changed. Rule 1 (no section that can hold geometry is skipped) and rule 2 (no record is accepted by its name) stay. Rule 3 (each object type has its own checks) is replaced, for objects other than `DICTIONARY`, by one general rule: the reader takes no value from an inert object, and an object is drawn only through an entity in `ENTITIES` or `BLOCKS`, which stay strict.

## Readings

The three QA files of the issue were read through `dxf::parse` and `SketchData::from_dxf` on this branch, with a temporary local test. The files are not committed, because they are not ours to commit.

| File | Primitives | Closed chains | Open | Rejected |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| `q04-vcarve-sign-letters.dxf` (AC1015) | 300 | 2 (261.70 mm² each) | 0 | 0 |
| `q04-vcarve-sign-letters-r12.dxf` | 894 | 2 (261.79 mm² each) | 0 | 0 |
| `q06-die-lines.dxf` (AC1015) | 117 | 1 (617.34 mm²) | 0 | 0 |

The R12 twin gives line segments for the arcs, so its area is 0.04 % larger.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/geometry/tests/dxf_ac1015_fixture.rs` (new, hand-written fixture with the section and object layout of the real export):
  - `an_ac1015_export_gives_the_same_closed_chains_as_its_r12_twin`
  - `a_truncated_ac1015_export_never_imports`
  - `a_mutated_ac1015_export_never_panics`

- `crates/geometry/tests/dxf_classes_section.rs` (8): for example `classes_section_is_skipped_and_entities_import`, `classes_section_without_endsec_is_a_named_error`, `other_unknown_sections_stay_refused`, `an_entity_in_a_section_without_geometry_is_refused`.

body:
## What changed

This PR adds the catalog case `examples/catalog/3d/rough-finish`. It is the first catalog case with a 3D Pocket and a 3D Finish.

- Model: an original part. It is a 50 x 50 x 8 mm plate with a spherical dome (36 mm base diameter, 10 mm high, top at Z18). The generator `model/gen_rough_finish_obj.py` makes a watertight height-field mesh (1.25 mm grid, 3680 triangles, 86 KB). The script checks each edge before it writes.
- Stock: a 50 x 50 x 22 mm box. Machine: "3-axis mill", like `2d/first-part`. Heights: clearance at top of stock + 25 mm, like the 2D cases.
- Tools: `EM-0600-4FL` (rough) and `BN-0600` (6 mm ball, finish). Holder `none`, like the neighbours.
- Operations:
  1. `3D Pocket1` (`EM-0600-4FL`): stepover 3 mm, stepdown 2 mm, stock to leave 0.5 mm, strategy `auto`, helix entry, from the top of stock down to Z8.
  2. `3D Finish Parallel` (`BN-0600`): pattern `parallel`, stepover 1.5 mm, tolerance 0.1 mm, direction angle and pass start at their defaults.
  3. `3D Finish Waterline` (`BN-0600`): pattern `waterline`, tolerance 0.1 mm, stepdown from the scallop law, pass start at its default.
- `crates/app/tests/example_catalog/case_3d_rough_finish.rs` registers the two case tests (`regenerates`, `rebuilds`). `example_catalog.rs` includes it with one line. The file was at 404 lines before this PR, so the module is in its own file.

The `.camproj` and `.nc` come only from `cargo xtask catalog --case 3d/rough-finish`.

No product code changes.

## Readings

- Verifier: `cam.verify()` gives `ok` with no blocking finding. The script stops before the post if it does not.

- #3671: the rapid between two levels goes down to the floor of the last cut with no margin (lowest `G0` at Z10, NC line 1625).

title: test(app): read the troubleshooting sources with any line end
body:
Cause: the test `troubleshooting_messages_still_exist_in_the_sources` joins string literals that continue on the next line with a backslash. It split on backslash plus LF. On a checkout with `core.autocrlf=true` the line end is CRLF, so the join did not match and the message stem was not found. LF checkouts and the runners were green.

The change (test code only, `crates/app/tests/docs_troubleshooting.rs`):
- New helper `normalise_eol` replaces CRLF with LF.
- The join code is now the helper `join_continuations`, which calls `normalise_eol` first. The sources go through it.
- The docs page text goes through `normalise_eol` too.
- No assert and no stem changed.
- New test `join_continuations_accepts_crlf_line_ends` pins the fix.

Red-first evidence: the new test was run with the `normalise_eol` call in `join_continuations` disabled. It failed with "CRLF continuation was not joined". With the call restored, both tests pass.

CRLF-file run: `crates/sim/src/verify/types.rs` (it holds backslash-continued refusal strings) was converted to CRLF on disk only. `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting -j 6` gave 2 passed, 0 failed. The file was then restored with `git checkout`.

Commands run:
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting -j 6`
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --test docs_troubleshooting -j 6 -- -D warnings`: clean.

Not run: the batch and release gates, and any test on a real `core.autocrlf=true` checkout (the reporter is asked to run it).

title: feat(gcode): add the camcraft-gcode reader crate for 3-axis RS-274 and ISO 6983 programs
body:
## What this PR does

This PR adds the new crate `crates/gcode` (`camcraft-gcode`). The crate reads RS-274/NGC and ISO 6983 3-axis milling programs. It gives `cl::Toolpath` sections and a 1-based line map. It refuses unsupported words by name and line number.

- The crate depends on `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-geometry` and `thiserror` only.
- It decodes the modal groups, `I`/`J`/`K` and `R` arcs in `G17`/`G18`/`G19`, and the canned cycles `G73`, `G81`, `G82`, `G83`, `G84`, `G85`, `G86`, `G89` with `G98`/`G99` and `L`.
- It splits sections at `T`/`M6`. It reads `S`, `M3`-`M5`, `M0`-`M2`, `M30`, `G4`, `G61`, `G64`, `G53`, `G28` and `G30`.
- It refuses `G41`/`G42`, macros (`G65`, `M98`, `#`), probing (`G31`, `G38.2`), `R` full circles, a missing `G20`/`G21`, a missing reference position, and `A`/`B`/`C`.

Sources: RS-274/NGC (NISTIR 6556), ISO 6983, and the public controller documents that `crates/gcode/src/dialect.rs` names for the dwell and arc presets. No other parser code was used.

## Held work

- Commit `711314efd` by Mike Kinney, from `mkinney:issue/2217-camcraft-gcode`. It has the crate, its 9 tests, the decision file and the gate plan entries.
- This PR keeps that commit and its author unchanged. A merge commit (`db23cf9bd`) joins it to main `60376ccbb`.

## Added after the held commit

- `db23cf9bd` merge: the conflict resolution (next section).
- `75b33ace3` `test(xtask)`: two xtask tests of main list the crates by hand. `heavy_plan_tests::reach_follows_the_crate_dependencies` now expects `gcode` in the reach of `geometry`. `step_tests::batch_prebuild_leaves_suite_steps_fresh_with_truck_dev_dep` now writes a stub `crates/gcode`. `Cargo.lock` takes the version `0.25.0` for `camcraft-gcode`.
- `92627aef0` `test(gcode)`:
  - Each gcode suite has a `Gate map: covers camcraft_gcode::{..}` line. Quick then selects the suites for a change in each `crates/gcode/src` module.
  - The new suite `degenerate_input` checks malformed programs. Each one gives a value or a refusal, with no panic and no hang.
  - The decision file records the merge.

## Conflict resolution

All three conflicts were lists. No logic hunk had a conflict.

- Root `Cargo.toml`: the `members` line has main's `"crates/gpu"` and the held `"crates/gcode"` (after `"crates/cl"`). The `camcraft-gcode` workspace dependency merged without a conflict.
- `xtask/src/plan.rs`: `BATCH_CRATES`, `ALL_CRATES` and `CLIPPY` have `"gcode"` after `"cl"` and main's `"gpu"` after `"app"`.
- `xtask/src/tests.rs`: the release step count keeps main's known-fail `checks` term. It uses the held `plan::ALL_CRATES.len()` in place of the fixed `10`.
- `Cargo.lock` merged without a conflict.

## New crate edges

- `camcraft-gcode -> camcraft-cl`: `ArcPlane`, `Cycle`, `CycleKind`, `MoveKind`, `PathBuilder`, `Toolpath`, `lattice`.
- `camcraft-gcode -> camcraft-geometry`: `geo2d::Point2`, `Point3`, `units::{from_display, Unit, MM_PER_INCH}`.
- `docs/decisions/2217-camcraft-gcode.md` gives the imported items, the reason that a caller cannot pass the values in, and the rebuild impact. No crate depends on `camcraft-gcode` yet.

## Tests

- `gcode_3axis`:
  - `modal_groups_track_and_sections_split_on_tool_changes`
  - `ijk_and_r_arcs_xy_xz_yz_and_full_circle`
  - `r_major_vs_minor_arc_centers_differ_as_expected`
  - `canned_cycles_expand_into_move_chains_and_honor_g98_g99`
  - `unit_scaling_g20_inches_to_mm_and_unscaled_s_t_p`
  - `reference_moves_g53_g28_g30_execute_when_configured_and_refuse_when_missing`
  - `unsupported_codes_and_bad_inputs_refuse_by_name_with_line_number`
- `dialects_and_planes`:
  - `vertical_plane_r_arcs_xz_and_yz_minor_and_major`
  - `dialects_dwell_units_ream_and_m6_tool_order`

## Gate

All results are on head `92627aef0`.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: the batch plan, because `Cargo.lock` changed. Result: 1133 steps, 1 failed, 0 stalled. The failed step is `clippy -D warnings` in `camcraft-gpu`. See "Known red step".

## Known red step

The failed quick step is not caused by this PR.

title: fix(motion): 2D Adaptive keeps the full tool clear of "Do not touch" items
body:
## What changed

"Do not touch" now applies to 2D Adaptive operations, with the Spiral method and with the Trochoidal method. Before this change, the operation refused the protected items.

- `do_not_touch_applies` accepts `OpType::Adaptive2D`. The refusal text, the MCP tool description and the guide name 2D Adaptive with Trace (#3348), 2D Offset, 3D Pocket and Face (#3343).
- The new module `machining2d::adaptive_avoid` gives one law to the two methods:
  - The keep-out is one region. It covers each tip height from the floor up to the clearance plane. Thus it holds every cut, every entry and every descent of the path, for the flutes, the shank and the holder.
  - The planner removes that region from its cutter-centre area. Then it plans as it does without protection. The crossing law, the entry and link certificates and the Offset-rings fallback (Spiral) or the move check (Trochoidal) read the reduced area.
  - Rapid links are lifted over the items (`elevate_rapid_links`). A link that cannot clear them refuses the operation.
  - A corner relief that enters the keep-out refuses the operation, as on 2D Offset.
  - When no item reaches the region, both methods call the plain planner. The path does not change.
- **Pass starts at** (#3355) is read on the protected Spiral path too (`adaptive_spiral_avoid_on`). The Trochoidal method still refuses Inside and Outside by name.
- The generic checks in `generate.rs` (`route_links`, `verify_avoid`) and the post gate (`live_avoid_problems`) already read each kind that `do_not_touch_applies` accepts. They have no change.

The decision is in `docs/decisions/3346-adaptive2d-do-not-touch.md` (with the dropped options).

**Known cost:** 2D Adaptive plans one area for all levels. Beside a protected item that is lower than the top of the cut, it leaves more stock than 2D Offset, which keeps out level by level. The guide says so. This costs cut area. It does not cost safety.

## Merge of main

The branch merges `upstream/main` three times:

- `1d1bd090f` (main `6cfc0a6d4`): conflicts with #3343 (Face) in `do_not_touch_applies`, its refusal text, the MCP description, the UI test and the guide. Both sides are kept. A conflict with #3355 in the 2D Adaptive arm of `generate.rs` is resolved by commit `067a914a1`, which threads the `StartSide` into the protected Spiral path.
- `f73493967` (main `74ea8988d`): no conflict.
- `241f6aeb5` (main `f35202134`): conflicts with #3348 (Trace) in `do_not_touch_applies`, its refusal text, the MCP description and the UI test. Both sides are kept: the list is now "Trace, 2D Offset, 2D Adaptive, 3D Pocket and Face". Main also removed "only so far" from the refusal text. Thus the 2D Adaptive UI test now checks that no "is supported on" note shows. The old check looked for text that main no longer writes.

## Pinning tests

- motion `avoid_adaptive`:
  - `a_spiral_adaptive_keeps_the_full_tool_clear_of_a_protected_pin_with_no_crossing`
  - `a_spiral_adaptive_with_no_keepout_on_the_region_is_the_plain_path`
  - `a_spiral_adaptive_with_a_pass_start_keeps_the_full_tool_clear_of_a_protected_pin`
  - `a_trochoidal_adaptive_keeps_the_full_tool_clear_of_a_protected_pin`
  - `an_empty_avoid_gives_the_plain_trochoidal_path`
  - `a_trochoidal_adaptive_with_no_room_left_is_refused_with_the_item_named`
- app `do_not_touch_adaptive`:
  - `adaptive2d_do_not_touch_keeps_the_full_tool_clear_and_clears_back_to_the_plain_path`
  - `adaptive2d_with_no_room_clear_of_the_protection_is_refused_with_the_item_named`
  - `adaptive2d_do_not_touch_round_the_tower_at_the_default_load_posts` (heavy lane)
- ui `do_not_touch`:
  - `adaptive2d_shows_the_pick_protected_button_and_no_unsupported_note`
  - `unsupported_op_shows_do_not_touch_note_without_pick_button` (new text)

## Gates

On `241f6aeb5` (the head of this PR):

- Quick gate (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1 cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 769 steps, 0 failed, 1 stalled. The stalled step is `ui suites: lib`: it gave no output for 15 min. The cause is local: on the author's machine the NVIDIA Vulkan driver hangs in `vkEnumerateInstanceExtensionProperties` while it waits for an X server reply (`vulkaninfo` hangs too). Each GPU lib test hangs there, and the #3589 lock holds the other GPU tests behind it. A rerun of that step alone with `DISPLAY` unset (`--only "ui suites: lib"`) passed: 1493 tests, 91 s.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 253 steps, 0 failed, 56.6 min. Four known fails were red as expected (#1950 three times, #2849 one time).
- `cargo clippy --no-deps -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean. Without `--no-deps`, clippy stops in `camcraft-gpu` (`needless_range_loop`). This branch does not change that crate, and main has the same code.

Earlier runs:

- On `f73493967`: quick gate 765 steps, 0 failed (one stall in `app build (--no-run)`, which passed alone). Heavy lanes 252 steps, 0 failed.
- On `067a914a1`: one failure, `first_part_programs::first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`. Main's #3464 left `examples/first-router-part.nc` stale, and main fixed it in `74a87c662`. The merge `f73493967` brings that fix.

## Not exercised

- No machine air cut.
- No per-level keep-out. A level above a low protected item loses the same area as the floor level.

Changelog: 2D Adaptive (Spiral and Trochoidal) honours "Do not touch": the full tool (flutes, shank, holder) stays clear of each protected face or edge by the clearance, or the operation is refused with the item named.

Fixes #3346
