title: fix(multiaxis): Rotary Parallel cuts the full turn of the bar
body:
## Cause (measured)

Rotary Parallel ran the 3-axis swarf raster one time, in a frame that lays the rotary axis down with local z up. That raster finishes the bar from above only. Two stages lose the bottom of the bar:

1. The ring ladder stops at Bottom, read as a tip height in the laid frame. With Bottom at -R, the last ring has its ball centre 30 degrees under the horizontal.
2. With a lower Bottom, the rings stop 45 degrees under the horizontal. `build_sups` turns each facet normal to the sky, so the bottom quadrant counts as shallow (raster) ground. The raster takes the top tangent and never reaches that ground. The rings skip loops that touch only shallow facets.

A third fault hid the band: the rotary path dropped the raster and ring notes on the default path.

## Measured arc

Laid bar R 3 mm, 1 mm ball, Bottom -R (`crates/motion/tests/rotary_coverage.rs`):

| Case | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| stepover 0.8 | 126 deg uncut, 210..336 deg (270 = bottom); 4 empty 30-degree sectors | 0 empty sectors; widest gap 12.1 deg |
| stepover 0.25 | 126 deg uncut, the same arc | 0 empty sectors; widest gap 8.1 deg |

With Bottom at -R-2r (stage 2 only), the uncut arc was 94.6 deg. The example part (Journal, Bottom 9.525 mm under the axis) is held by stage 2: about 90 deg, a quarter of the turn. The issue said 10-20 %.

## What changed

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary.rs`: Rotary Parallel plans the bar in two halves. Half A is the laid frame. Half B is the same frame turned half a turn about the axis.
- New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary/halves.rs`:
  - Each half keeps the cut over its own upper half.
  - Half B goes back into A's frame by the rigid half turn.
  - The seam: A keeps centres down to half a ball radius under the axis plane. B keeps only centres strictly under A's lowest kept centre, on each side, read over the turned surface. No pass is cut twice. The seam step is one ring step (6.4 deg on the fixture).
  - Half B is held to Bottom where the radially posed ball touches the bar. A Bottom above the axis thus keeps the cut to the upper arc, as before.
  - The lifts of half B become links, so the radial relink rebuilds them along the radius.
- Review rework (head `864897476`): no cut of the single-frame path is lost on a part that is not round, and no place is cut twice:
  - A cut of half A under the seam stays where no kept cut of half B stands at the same place (a ball centre within half a pass spacing). Example: the lower wall of a keyway, which half B cannot see.
  - A cut of half B over the seam is added where half A cuts nothing at the same place (a wall that faces down).
  - The pass spacing is the stepover, or the scallop step `sqrt(8 r tol)`, the larger.
  - New `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary/gaps.rs`: the ball-centre cover (a grid hash) and a reach reading on a fixed grid of at most 48 stations x 72 angles. A ray from the axis finds the outermost surface. A place under Bottom, or a corner where no ball fits, is skipped. A place with no ball centre within one pass spacing gets the note `Rotary Parallel: no pass reaches the surface over <a0>..<a1> deg about the axis (from the top of the laid bar toward its +y side) at stations <s0>..<s1> mm along it - that surface stays uncut`. Only a path with no such place has the full-turn note. Follow-up for this note: #3658 (its cost on a dense mesh, the document unit, a frame that the user can see).
  - Round bars: `rotary_coverage`, the example program and the microARC wrap golden are byte-identical to the first head. This is a measured result for these fixtures, not a law. On another bar a cut of half A under the seam can stay where no sample of half B is within half a pass spacing. Such an extra cut is one that the single-frame path makes too.
  - If half B fails with an error other than `Empty`, the whole operation is refused (also where the single-frame path posts). The refusal is visible. This is recorded in the decision file.
- All base notes (raster, rings) now reach the path. A path that cuts under the axis has the note `Rotary Parallel: the passes go all the way round the bar - the machine must turn the part on a rotary axis through the whole turn; set Bottom above the axis to cut only the upper arc`.
- No change to `build_sups` or to any shared finishing helper. The planning time of Rotary Parallel is about two times the old time.

A ball sphere that is clear of the model stays clear under a rigid rotation. The radial pose keeps every ball centre. So each half is as safe as the old single run. The new moves go through the existing held-end clip, picked-face clip, radial relink (no rapid through the part) and radial pose.

## Goldens that moved

Only the two Rotary Parallel programs that had the band moved. The review rework moved neither of them again.

**`crates/app/tests/golden/nc/tormach/wrap_rotary_parallel_microarc4.nc`** (the microARC test part, Bottom -R): regenerated with `WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test microarc_test_part`. Lines 3246 -> 2684, G1 2924 -> 2191, G0 226 -> 415; diff +1333 / -1895. The feed moves that turn A, binned in 30-degree A sectors: before `187 154 122 108 436 319 328 472 97 116 148 186`, after `187 154 122 116 148 186 187 154 122 116 148 186`. The two halves now give the same cut in each half turn. The first head did not run this binary.

**The example:** It was regenerated with the test's own tool (`WRITE_GOLDEN=1 cargo test -p camcraft-app --test continuous_4axis_part`). No hand edits.

| `examples/first-continuous-4axis-part.nc` | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Lines | 3125 | 2866 |
| G1 lines | 1662 | 1508 |
| G0 lines | 1398 | 1300 |
| Mid-journal feed endpoints in each 30-degree A sector | 31 30 3 5 11 0 0 9 5 3 16 30 | 31 30 3 3 16 30 31 30 3 3 16 30 |

- Diff: `.nc` +1426 / -1685 lines, `.camproj` +8531 / -12275 lines.
- The program has fewer lines: the deep rings of the old single frame (under the equator) go, and half B cuts the bottom with raster lines.
- The start and the end are as before: the same header, the same T1 change, the first `G53 G0 Z0` then `G0 A44.604`, the same first passes, then `G94`, a G0 retract, `M9`, `M5`, `G53 G0 Z0`, `M30`.
- The guide page `first-continuous-4axis-part.md`, its two toolpath pictures (made again by `site/tools/first_continuous_4axis_pictures.py`) and its pins in `site/tests/test_first_continuous_4axis_part.py` follow the new program: the line count, the excerpts, the A range -85.708..265.687, the last A, the A180 line and the second note.
- No non-rotary golden moved. `golden_cl`, `example_catalog*`, `first_part_programs` and the finish3d suites are green with no change. No shipped example or catalog case uses Rotary Parallel on a machine with limited rotary travel.

## Maintainer decision (owner's standing word 2026-11-22: choose recommended while he sleeps)

1. The example is regenerated with the test's own tool. Dropped: hand edits.
2. `operations::rotary_parallel_generates_radial_axes_and_verifies_clean`:
   - Old assert (main): every cut tip, read as a vertical ball in the laid frame, is not under Bottom (`lowest >= -4`).
   - First head: `a >= -4 || b >= -4`. The review found this vacuous, because `b` holds for each move under the axis.
   - Review rework: the per-half reads in each half's own frame could not fail on this bar (over the axis plane `low >= -3`; under it B's `-cz - 3 > -3`), so they are removed. The bounds are now:
     - every feed and plunge of either half, including the cuts of half A under the axis plane that the filter keeps, touches at or over the Bottom in world z (`tip z >= -4.1`);
     - both halves cut more than 20 moves;
     - each 30-degree sector holds a pass;
     - the "last line IS the Bottom" assert stays.
   - Mutation: with the bound raised by 1 mm (`-3.0 - 0.1`), the test is red (`a cut touches under the Bottom: Move { kind: Plunge, ... to: ... z: -3.7798895192744437 ...}`). The lowest touch on the fixture is -4.1, at the bound.
   - Dropped: the old one-frame law, because it pinned the band.
3. Limited rotary travel (`tilthead.mch`, B -120..120): a full-turn path is refused by the machine check. The check names the move, the axis, the angle and the travel, and nothing posts. The way to the reachable arc is a Bottom above the axis: the existing tilt-head fixture (Bottom 1) posts clean with no change. New pin: `a_full_turn_rotary_parallel_refuses_on_a_head_that_cannot_reach_under`. The clean post on a 4-axis A machine is `continuous_4axis_part` (microARC 4). Dropped: clipping the cut to the machine's reach in the generator, because the generator does not know the machine. Follow-up: #3649 (a parameter for the angular range).

The decision file is `docs/decisions/2970-rotary-parallel-halves.md`. Also dropped: the `build_sups` change of the earlier plan, because it changes every 3D pattern and makes the split depend on the mesh winding.

## Pins

- `crates/motion/tests/rotary_coverage.rs`:
  - `the_rotary_parallel_goes_all_the_way_round_a_laid_bar`
  - `the_rotary_parallel_goes_all_the_way_round_at_a_fine_stepover`
  - These two tests check the empty sectors, the seam step against the flank, no pass cut twice, no move emitted twice, and the full-turn note. Both are red on main.
  - `the_rotary_parallel_keeps_the_ladder_notes` (a `rings:` note reaches the path)
  - `a_bottom_over_the_axis_keeps_the_cut_to_the_upper_arc`
- `crates/app/tests/operations.rs`: `rotary_parallel_generates_radial_axes_and_verifies_clean` (sector coverage added; verifies clean with stock)
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_verify.rs`: `a_full_turn_rotary_parallel_refuses_on_a_head_that_cannot_reach_under`
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary/single_frame_tests.rs` (review rework; in `--lib`). The reference is the generator before the halves (laid swarf, radial relink, radial pose), kept for tests only:
  - `a_keyway_loses_no_cut_of_the_single_frame_path`: keyed bar R 10, keyway walls at z = +-5, 6 mm ball. Before the rework, 52 centre samples that the single frame cuts were lost (stations 23.7..36.3 mm, 347 deg: the lower keyway wall). After the rework, 0 are lost.
  - `a_keyway_is_cut_once_in_each_place`: no two passes that are not neighbours stand within 0.1 mm.
  - `the_reach_reading_names_the_arc_no_pass_reaches`: the arc and stations are named. No note for a full turn, and no note for a Bottom over the axis.
- `crates/app/tests/rotary_parallel_keyway.rs` (new): `a_keyed_bar_cut_all_the_way_round_leaves_only_the_corner_rest`, the keyed bar in bar stock. The only blocking finding is the keyway corner rest that a 6 mm ball cannot reach (envelope gouge 0.020 mm, rest 1.95 mm). The test accepts it only with a gouge of 0.05 mm or less, at a move over the keyway (stations 17..43 mm, +y side). The verdict names the move nearest in plan only; here it is a plunge at the keyway's end, station 40. The single-frame path reports the same finding (gouge 0.020, rest 1.99). Both halves cut. Each rapid ends on the clearance cylinder. The full-turn note is there.
- Not covered: an eccentric section (a round collar off the axis). The axis fit refuses every variant that was tried ("every axis fits this model equally"), so no such part reaches Rotary Parallel. The decision file records this gap in the evidence.

## Gate of the delta (head `b4eda8a40`, after `git merge origin/main`)

- app: `operations` (121), `rotary_parallel_keyway`, `microarc_test_part`, `continuous_4axis_part`: green.
- motion: `--lib rotary` (12), `rotary_coverage`: green.

title: feat(multiaxis): Rotary Flow kernel - flow lines between picked helical guide chains
body:
## What changed

The first slice of the Rotary Flow kind (issue #2824, part of #2804): a 4-axis cylindrical flow-line kernel in `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/`, split over four files under the 400-line law.

- `rotary_flow.rs` - the public entry. `rotary_flow(chains, facets, ax, p, c)` takes the picked guide chains, the part facets, the STATED rotation axis (the #2772 seam - the axis is a parameter, never fitted here), `RotaryFlowParams` and `AxisControl`. The params carry the `Tool` itself, so the ball-nose requirement is refused by name. Clearance and retract read as ball-center radii about the axis.
- `rotary_flow_unwrap.rs` - each chain unwound to a continuous `(theta, v)` track (the radian twin of `cl::unwrap_near`), each adjacent pair aligned by the nearest whole turn, the band developed `(s = R_ref * theta, v)` with `R_ref` the chains' outermost radius, and the picked-chain ground checks (finite, distinct, on-model, off-axis).
- `rotary_flow_pass.rs` - the iso-parametric flow curves between the aligned pair, each station's ball center pushed out along its radial until the `closest_pt_tri` oracle clears every facet (march, then bisect), the curve chorded within `min(ARC_FIT_TOL, tolerance)` over the union of the two chains' arc-length knots.
- `rotary_flow_emit.rs` - tips via the pivot law (`retip`), cut poses through the lean law on the radial (`tilt`), links rebuilt radially on the retract cylinders (`rotary_links`' law: feed retract, chorded index short way round, radial plunge), the program opening on the clearance pose (M13.8).

Refusals by name: a tool that is not a ball-nose, fewer than two chains, a non-finite point, a point off the model, a point on the axis line, chains wound in opposite senses, a band with no width, a stepover or tolerance at the scallop ceiling (the finishing kinds' own law), a station the push-out cannot clear within five radii, a pass count over the 4096-pass ceiling, a clearance that does not clear the work.

The decisions taken unattended are in `docs/decisions/2824-rotary-flow-kernel.md`: the `Tool`-carrying params (the drilling precedent), the ball-center radius reading of the heights, `R_ref` at the chains' outermost radius (ground inside it gets finer, never coarser), and one band per adjacent chain pair with both edge passes kept (a shared middle chain is walked once per band - the re-cut is the same geometry at the same depth).

## The readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 29 steps, 0 failed - motion lib, `multiaxis`, `rotary`, the new `rotary_flow` binary, and the reached app suites (operations, posed_contact, rotary_fixtures, rotary_verify, and the rest). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.
- On the rotor groove fixture: the developed band reads 4.000 mm at R 8.000 mm; 6 flow passes at a 0.9 mm stepover; the first pass rides the wall push-out (rho about 11), interior passes ride the floor a ball radius off it; every cut station's ball keeps its radius off the part.

## Pinning tests

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/rotary_flow/rotary_flow_tests.rs` (15 tests): every refusal by name (non-ball tool, chain count, empty model, off-model at its spot, on-axis, degenerate band, opposite senses, both scallop ceilings, low clearance), the pass count law, `align_pair`'s nearest whole turn, `lerp_at`, `unwrap_near`, and a small on-model band that poses, clears and opens at clearance.
- `crates/motion/tests/rotary_flow.rs` (3 run, 1 heavy): `a_rotor_floor_band_flows_multi_turn_without_gouge` (the no-gouge pin over every station against `camcraft_sim`'s own `dist_seg_tri`, multi-turn span, wall vs floor riders), `a_pair_straddling_the_branch_aligns_by_a_whole_turn` (same pass count as the unshifted band, the note stating the shift), `climb_reverses_each_pass`, and the ignored `the_rotor_envelope_stays_gouge_free_at_the_scallop_law` (heavy lane: release --ignored, the 4-turn fine rotor envelope scanned station by station).

## What was not exercised

- The app layer, the command and the MCP tool are owed to the #2804 sub-issues; this PR changes only the motion kernel.
- The whole-turn alignment is pinned by the kernel basis' own branch (e1 = +Y on a Z axis); a pair straddling a different frame's branch reaches the same law through the same shift.
- A band whose pair meets at a whole-turn boundary exactly (offset = half a lap) is not tested; the nearest-turn law would pick either side.
- `graphify update` did not run: the `graphify` command is not on this session's PATH.
- Heavy lane: only the ignored envelope scan touches it; it runs at the cut.

Changelog: multiaxis: Rotary Flow - a 4-axis flow-line finishing kernel between picked helical guide chains on a stated rotation axis

title: perf(sim): index verifier island slices exactly, keep every plane
body:
The gate is green. This PR waits for an independent review; it stays a draft until then.

## What changed

Law (c)'s island membership test no longer scans the whole cached slice on
every point query. `Rest::island_holds` now asks an exact Y-slab point index
(`crates/sim/src/verify/slice_index.rs`). The index keeps every cut plane and
every sample; it reads only the edges whose Y span holds the query point, and
it computes the crossing with the same expression, in the same order, as
`Region::contains`, so the answer is bit for bit.

The rejected levels-plus-deepest plane set is removed:
`crates/sim/src/verify/cut_planes.rs` is deleted, and `reach.rs` and `mod.rs`
are back on main's plane loop (`rest.cut()`, one slice per cut plane).

Files:
- `crates/sim/src/verify/slice_index.rs` (new: index and its direct pin)
- `crates/sim/src/verify/rest.rs` (cache holds `Rc<IndexedSlice>`)
- `crates/sim/src/verify/reach_tests.rs` (stepped fixture, model-parameterized compare)
- `crates/sim/src/verify/mod.rs` (module)
- `docs/decisions/3615-verify-cut-levels.md` (accepted design)

## Equivalence

`verify::reach_tests::a_many_plane_ramp_reads_only_the_samples_near_its_discs`
compares law (c) with the all-plane reference (`reach_reference`) and fails if
any finding, its order, or the slice count moves.

- Sloped ramp `ramp_at(500, 36.0)`: equal findings; `slices 500 == 500`;
  `sample_tests 20,192` new vs `1,394,117` reference.
- Stepped fixture (wide low block under a narrow tall block) at Y 49: equal
  findings; `slices 500 == 500`; `sample_tests 28,368` vs `1,390,052`.
- Away-from-wall ramp `ramp_at(500, 34)`: equal findings; `sample_tests 0`
  vs `2,004,000`.

The stepped fixture exposes the levels-only failure: on a temporary variant
that keeps only the wide low block (the deepest section's sample set), the
reference convicts 93 `ShankHit { part: true }` moves and the wide-only set
convicts 63, losing moves 250 to 279 (30 part-true). The narrow band's Y 45
wall sample is what catches them.

The index itself is pinned directly: `verify::slice_index::tests::the_index_equals_region_contains_bit_for_bit`
compares it with `Region::contains` over a grid that lands on every vertex
line and between them, for a U, a staircase and a holed region.

## Gates run

- `cargo test -p camcraft-sim --lib verify::`: 160 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base 65b52cca6 --only "app heavy: verify"`: ok in
  450 s (`--release --ignored`, the sim verify heavy lane).
- `cargo xtask gate light --base 65b52cca6`: not run. Its three twins are the
  motion slot, motion trochoidal and app pocket-pass-start lanes, none of
  which read the verifier; the light build links every motion and app test
  binary in release, a cut-level cost.

## Not exercised

- The full mechanical heavy reach (`app heavy: every target`, `motion heavy:
  every target`) is a cut-level run; the sim verify heavy coverage is the
  `app heavy: verify` lane.
- The real #3577 fig8 path: the counterexamples are the sloped and stepped
  fixtures.

Fixes #3615

title: feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour
body:
feat(wire): closing overlap, centre-line slit and open-run skims for Wire Contour

Wire Contour gains the three polish cuts of #3216. Each is stated, never
inferred, and refused by name where it has nothing to state.

What changed

- Closing overlap (closed profiles). `WireContourOp.overlap` and
  `WireParams.overlap` (mm, default 0) ride the cut past the seam by the
  stated arc length before the lead-out returns to the threading point,
  so the start of the cut is burnt over and no witness mark is left.
  The past-seam extension walks the ring from the seam point and cuts
  the last point to the exact remainder; the kerf law judges the return
  move like every other. Refused: with tabs (tabs pin the seam), on an
  open run (no seam), at a negative or non-finite length. A skim
  inherits the overlap. The note says the ride.
- Centre-line slit (open runs). New `WireSide::Centre`: the wire rides
  the run itself, the kerf burns both sides, no side is kept - so the
  kerf law has no product to protect and is not applied, while the
  corner/doubling-back law and the run-out laws still refuse what the
  wire cannot follow. The note says "no side kept".
- Skims on open runs. `check_passes` no longer refuses an open run; the
  offset-ordering laws judge it like a closed profile. `wire_passes`
  routes each open-side skim through the open-run generator: every pass
  re-enters from the air at the run's start end, at its own run-in
  point, walked in the run's own direction - a reversed pass on an open
  run is refused by name (one pinned semantic), and no move joins one
  pass's run-out to the next pass's run-in (the wire is threaded anew).
- Wire verify (sim). `CutSide::Centre` is judged as an open run whose
  kerf law is skipped by statement (`CENTRE_SKIP` on the report line);
  the ends' clearance is still judged. Skims on an open run are
  generated but named as not verified here yet (the verify reads one
  open pass) - a follow-up can extend the open law to per-pass kerfs.
- App, file and UI. The overlap rides the seed, the command door's
  sanity, the op stamp (only when stated, so no existing stamp moves)
  and the project DTO (`overlap`, absent reads 0); `side` reads and
  writes `centre`. The wire page gains the Closing overlap row and the
  Centre choice; its test count grows by one.

Pinning tests

- `the_closing_overlap_rides_past_the_seam_and_is_refused_without_a_seam`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): ride length past the seam, inherited
  skim ride, lead-out home, and each refusal by name.
- `a_centre_slit_rides_the_run_itself_and_takes_skims_from_the_air`
  (camcraft_motion::wire_edm): centre ride on the line, air threading
  per pass at its own offset, reversed refused.
- `skim_laws_refuse_by_name`: the open-run skim refusal is replaced by
  the offset laws accepting it.
- `wire_closing_overlap_and_centre_side_apply_and_undo` (camcraft-ui).

Readings: the overlap ride of 1.0 mm on a 40x20 die ends at
(1.000, -9.835) with K = 0.165; a centre slit's left skim threads at
(60.000, -1.145) against the rough's (60.000, -1.165).

Not exercised

- Skims on an open run are not judged per pass by the wire verify (it
  refuses them by name); a follow-up can split the passes and judge
  each at its own kerf.
- Taper, burnout and 4-axis cuts do not read the overlap; each refuses
  an open run or walks the closed lap as before.

Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`, 665 steps)

- All sim, motion, app and ui suites green, the three pinning tests
  included.
- Three steps are red, each not caused by this change:
  - `app suites: docs_troubleshooting` - the stem of a clearance
    message spans a line-continued string in `crates/sim/src/verify`;
    no file of this change is in its sources.
  - `app suites: example_catalog` (2d/drill-overfeed) - the fixture
    `refusal.txt` on disk reads CRLF against the generated LF; a
    checkout line-ending state, no fixture touched here.
  - `ui suites: lib` - a native STATUS_ACCESS_VIOLATION at 20 test
    threads after all tests printed ok; it re-runs green in full
    (`1431 passed; 0 failed`) and at 1 and 4 threads. A teardown race
    of the headless window harness on this machine, not this change.

title: feat: open a project read-only with --read-only and open_project read_only
body:
## What changed

`camcraft-ui --read-only job.camproj` opens a project read-only. The MCP
tool `open_project` takes `read_only: true` for the same result. A save
over the opened file is then refused on every save route, and the file
stays byte for byte. A save to another file works and ends read-only. The
title bar shows `CamCraft - job.camproj (read-only)`.

- One rule, `project::refuse_read_only_save` in `crates/app/src/project/`,
  refuses a save to the file that the project is open read-only from. The
  window's `State::save_project_path` and `script::api::v_save` call it.
  `v_save` serves MCP `save_project`, script `cam.save` and the live MCP
  seam of a window.
- The rule compares canonical paths, so a save from the Save As dialog
  to the opened file is refused too.
- In the window, Save on a read-only project opens the Save As dialog, as
  the editor for shipped machines does. The Save of the unsaved-changes
  prompt does the same.
- Changes stay allowed in memory.
- The read-only state is kept next to the document path:
  `State::project_read_only` in the window, `Env::doc_read_only` in a
  headless MCP session or a script run. The live seam gets the window's
  state through `LiveOptions::read_only`.
- A model file with `--read-only` is imported as usual. A headless start
  ignores the option. The live seam still refuses `open_project`.
- The same option name and behaviour as the open SolidCraft proposal
  for `--read-only` (tangency-labs/solidcraft#20830).
- No change to the file format or `PROJECT_VERSION`.
- Docs: the `--help` text, `docs/user-guide/start-options.md`,
  `site/content/guide/automate/cli.md` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- Decisions: `docs/decisions/3609-read-only-open.md`.

This branch starts at upstream/main `60b19abe8`. Two merges of upstream
main follow it: `b94dcd378` (main `82db54282`) and `98cd5b28b` (main
`3fc0e017b`). There is no rebase.

- The first merge had conflicts with #3608 (overwrite guard) and #3584
  (start options). Both sides added lines in the same places. The merge
  keeps both sides.
- In `v_save` and `State::save_project_path`, the read-only check runs
  first, and then the overwrite guard of #3608. Thus `overwrite: true`
  does not write over a file that is open read-only.
- `--read-only` comes after `--no-activate` and `--minimized` in the
  options table, the `--help` text and `start-options.md`.
  `run_windowed` takes the start mode and `read_only`.
- `LiveOptions` and `Env` have `read_only` and `doc_stamp`. The
  `save_project` description has the sentences of both changes.
- `crates/app/tests/save_overwrite_guard.rs` gets one line,
  `read_only: false`, in its `LiveOptions` value. This is the only line
  outside the files of this change.
- The second merge had no conflicts. It brings in #3687 (a relative
  model link resolves against the project folder).

## Tests

New in `crates/app/tests/read_only_open.rs`:

- `the_rule_refuses_only_the_opened_file_of_a_read_only_project`
- `a_read_only_project_refuses_a_save_over_its_file_and_keeps_it`
- `a_save_to_another_file_works_and_ends_read_only`
- `a_plain_open_ends_read_only_and_a_bad_flag_changes_nothing`
- `a_script_save_after_a_read_only_open_is_refused`
- `the_live_seam_refuses_an_approved_save_over_a_read_only_window_project`

New in `crates/ui/src/launch_file_tests.rs`:

- `a_read_only_project_refuses_a_save_over_its_file_and_save_as_ends_read_only`
- `read_only_changes_nothing_for_a_model_file`

New in `crates/ui/src/cli_options_tests.rs`:

- `read_only_is_a_switch_that_keeps_the_file_after_it`

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on the head `98cd5b28b`
(Windows 11). The diff since main `3fc0e017b` is 23 files. 226 of 229
steps passed, and 0 stalled. The three red steps are not from this
change:

- `example_catalog`: `catalog_2d_drill_overfeed::{rebuilds,regenerates}`.
  The refusal text is equal, and only the line end is different. The
  checkout uses `core.autocrlf=true`, so `refusal.txt` has `\r\n`.
- `catalog_render`: `catalog_cases_open_and_frame_cleanly`. The case
  `3d/rough-finish` links `model/rough-finish.obj`. With
  `core.autocrlf=true` the file on disk has `\r\n`, so its sha256 is not
  the one in the project, and the link check imports it again. The blob
  in git has the sha256 of the project.
- `first_router_part`:
  `first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal`. Main
  is red with this step (#3698).

The steps of this change and of #3608 all passed:

- `read_only_open`: 6 passed.
- `save_overwrite_guard`: 7 passed.
- `mcp_live`: 14 passed.
- `mcp_doc_drift`: 6 passed.
- `mcp`: 29 passed.
- `scripting`: 20 passed.
- `project_roundtrip`: 80 passed.
- `first_part_programs`: 2 passed (#3574 is fixed on main).
- The app lib tests: 303 passed.
- The `camcraft-ui` lib tests: 1524 passed, 8 ignored. These include
  `launch_file_tests` and `cli_options_tests`.
- 15 of the 16 ui suites passed, among them `gpu_render`, `shell` and
  `operations`. The red one is `catalog_render` (above).

The other app steps are the suites that the gate maps from
`app::project`, `app::script` and `app::mcp`.
`cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`
on `98cd5b28b`: clean (exit 0). The only warning is the manifest note about the unused workspace dependency `truck-polymesh`, which is not from this change.
Heavy lanes: not run (no heavy step for a `P2` or lower PR, #3556).
Reach from `cargo xtask gate heavy --dry-run` at `144d07a85`: every `app`
heavy target (212 steps), because `crates/app/src/mcp/live.rs` changed.

## Manual check

Windows 11, debug build of `98cd5b28b`. A person did the keyboard and
dialog steps. The window title and the files were read through Windows
and on disk.

1. `camcraft-ui --read-only edge-work.camproj`, a copy of
   `examples/catalog/2d/edge-work`. The title is
   `CamCraft - edge-work.camproj (read-only)`. The status line says
   `opened ... (read-only; Save As writes your own copy)`. The file does
   not change.
2. Ctrl+S opens the Save As dialog.
3. Save As to the same file: Windows asks to replace the file, and the
   user selects yes. CamCraft refuses the save. The status line shows
   `save refused: ... is open read-only; write your copy to a different
   file` in red. The file does not change: the sha256 and the
   modification time are the same.
4. A change to the machine sets the unsaved mark `*` in the title. The
   change stays in memory.
5. Save As to a new file writes `edge-work-copy.camproj`. The title
   becomes `CamCraft - edge-work-copy.camproj`, without `(read-only)` and
   without `*`. The first file does not change.

Finding, not changed in this PR: after the user says yes to the replace
prompt, the user expects a write. The refusal shows only on the status
line, and a narrow window cuts the line. The user in this check did not
see the refusal. A possible follow-up is a notice that the user must
close.

## Not in this change

- A read-only open on the live seam. The live seam refuses
  `open_project`, so that an agent cannot skip the window's
  unsaved-changes prompt. The window's read-only state still reaches a
  live `save_project`.
- A new script form `cam.load(path, options)`. Scripts use
  `cam.call("open_project", {path, read_only: true})`.
- `read_only` in `get_job`.
- The window does not follow the path of a live `save_project` with a
  new path. This is the behaviour today. The window keeps its path and
  stays read-only.
- A reopen from the recent list, or in a later session, is not
  read-only. The recent list keeps paths only.
- The read-only bit of the file on disk.
- A hand-off of the flag to a running window. CamCraft has no
  single-instance hand-off.

## Not exercised

- An automated test of the Save As dialog route in the window. A
  headless test cannot open a native dialog. The tests pin the refusal
  behind it, and the manual check above did the route by hand.
- The live seam through a real window and the AI chat's Allow prompt.
  A test calls `answer_live_with` with the options that the window builds.
- Linux and macOS.
- A project on a network share.
- No test sets a project read-only and then calls `save_project` with
  `overwrite: true` over its own file. The order of the two checks
  (read-only first) is in the code, but no test pins it.

Changelog: `camcraft-ui --read-only` and `open_project` with `read_only: true` open a project read-only: Save never writes over the opened file, and Save As writes your own copy.

title: fix(2d): note the corner reliefs that get no spur
body:
## What changed

A planned corner relief whose start no pass vertex reaches, and for which no legal detour exists, was dropped without a diagnostic (#3249). It could leave material the operator does not expect.

- `inject_relief_spurs` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief_spur.rs`) now reports each skipped relief: the caller gets the relief start points in a `misses` vector.
- The pocket emit path (`pocket_emit.rs`) and the pocket avoid path (`pocket_avoid.rs`) write one note per corner into the `PathBuilder` / path notes: `corner relief at (x, y) is not cut: no pass vertex reaches the relief spur`. Notes are de-duplicated by corner, so a multi-level cut or a retry names each corner once.
- The four-dogbones rest test keeps its no-note assert: a reached relief adds no note.

Changelog: A 2D Pocket corner relief that no pass reaches is now named in the operation notes instead of being dropped silently.

## Pinning tests

- `machining2d::corner_relief_spur::tests::a_relief_no_pass_reaches_is_reported_as_a_miss` (crates/motion/src/machining2d/corner_relief_spur.rs): the miss is reported and no spur is spliced in; a reached relief reports no miss and gets its spur.
- `unreachable_corners_and_bad_overrides_are_refused` (crates/motion/tests/corner_relief.rs): the island-blocked spur refuses at plan time.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_corner_relief.rs`: the rest pass keeps its no-note assert.

## Not exercised

- The note text in a posted NC program through the full post pipeline.
- The avoid-path note on a multi-level cut with more than one skipped corner.

title: fix(2d): enter a dead-end later Outside pass by a ramp along the pass
body:
## What changed

With "Pass starts at: Outside", a later pass of 2D Offset or 2D Pocket (Waterline or Offset rings) that starts at a dead end now enters by a ramp along its own pass. Before, it entered by a plunge or a helix into uncut stock (#3567).

**Maintainer decision** (issue #3567, 2026-11-22): "At a dead end of a later pass of 2D Offset with "Pass starts at: Outside", the tool enters with **a ramp along the pass**." The coordinator's standing-word decision (#3567, 23:24Z) accepts the ramp at the ramp angle and names the ramp angle as the control of the load.

**The entry.**
- `level_order::order` marks each later pass of an Outside plan that no lead-in reaches (`LevelPlan::ramp_starts`).
- `ladder_links::pass_link` calls `level_ramp_entry::dead_end_ramp` first. At a marked start, the tool goes down by the existing ramp fallback: the zig-zag along the start of the pass (`descent::ramp_fallback`).
- The ramp angle is the entry's ramp angle, or 3 degrees (`links::DEFAULT_RAMP_ANGLE`) when the operation sets none. The leg limit is the entry's maximum ramp length.
- The ramp starts at the material top of the level plus the plunge height. The last leg lands on the pass start at depth. The pass then cuts the ramped stretch again at the floor.
- The ramp lead is thinned by Douglas-Peucker within `ARC_FIT_TOL` (0.01 mm). Each kept point is a vertex of the pass.

## Review items (review of e7ae538a3)

1. **No silent plunge.** `level_ramp_entry::too_short_at` checks each dead end at the deepest descent of any cut level. A dead end that is too short for the ramp sends the area to the Auto order with `StartSide::ramp_fallback_note`. That note carries `RINGS_FALLBACK`, so the op raises `Warning::StrategyFallback`. If the ladder still cannot plan the ramp, it names that on the path. Pinned by `a_dead_end_too_short_for_the_ramp_falls_back_to_pure_auto`, `a_dead_end_too_short_for_the_ramp_is_found` and `the_ramp_fallback_note_is_a_rings_fallback`.
2. **Slope law in the pin.** `late_entry_cut` counts a descending feed as a ramp only when it is at or under the ramp angle plus 0.05 degrees and on the pass path (within 0.02 mm of a floor feed). A steeper feed counts like a plunge (`a_steep_straight_feed_is_not_a_ramp`). The pin asserts that a ramp ran. New pins:
   - `outside_dead_end_entries_are_no_steeper_than_the_ramp_angle`
   - `outside_floor_under_each_dead_end_ramp_is_cut`
   - `outside_dead_end_ramps_width_reading_of_the_stepover_band` (it reads the band width; it is not a proof against a full-width cut)
3. **A replaced entry is named.** When the ramp replaces the user's Plunge, Helix or Arc entry, the path says so one time, in the #2265 stand-in form (`level_ramp_entry::stand_in_note`, pinned by `a_replaced_entry_is_named`).
4. **The trigger.** Only marked dead ends get the ramp. The first entry of each level and the ring 0 pieces keep the entry of main: a helix or a plunge into solid stock at the first entry is normal and outside this issue. The Auto-order plan after a completeness-guard fallback has no marks, so it stays pure Auto (pinned byte for byte by `a_dead_end_too_short_for_the_ramp_falls_back_to_pure_auto`). The ladder does not scan the earlier moves with `plunge_law::into_solid` at each pass link.
5. **The ramp, in plain words.** The ramp is an entry into uncut stock at a dead end. Where the ring cut before does not reach the dead end, the ramp cuts a slot at nearly the full tool width, at the ramp angle. After the ramp, the pass cuts at one stepover. The ramp angle is the control. Measured on the band of the pins (tool D8, stepover 4):
   - About 25 percent of the tool disc (about 12.6 mm2 of 50.3 mm2) is uncut stock at the start of each of the 8 ramps.
   - The band width during the ramps is 4.78 mm at most, under the limit of 5.375 mm.
   - The earlier "83 percent" number was the stock that each helix of main cut over its whole orbit (332.88 mm2 / 8 = 41.6 mm2), not the stock in the disc at the start.
   - Each ramp runs at 3.000 degrees from Z 2.0 to Z -3.0 over 95.41 mm along the pass.
   - The decision file `docs/decisions/3567-ramp-entry-at-dead-end.md` says this and quotes the two decisions.
6. **`levels.rs` does not grow.** It has 456 lines (459 on main). The builders are in the new module `level_ramp_entry.rs`.
7. **The file collision with #3566.** This PR keeps `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs` and moves its grid to `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement/grid.rs`. #3566 must drop its copy, or take its four sibling pins onto this file after this PR merges.

## Readings

- The late-entry pin `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock`: 332.88 mm2 on main, 0.00 mm2 with the ramp.
- `pass_start_levels`: 7 of 7, with no limit changed.

## The slow pin is a test-speed problem, not a block

The verification of `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge` is slow. It is a test-speed problem, filed as #3587 (`P5`). The verifier speed is filed as #3588 (fix PR #3595, draft). Neither issue blocks #3577.

Readings on this head (`d41c2b76a`):
- `pocket_pass_start`: 5 passed of 6. The sixth test, `fig8_pocket_outside_starts_each_level_at_the_stock_edge`, did not complete. It stopped at 29 min 23 s. The earlier run tripped the 15-min stall watchdog at 961 s.
- Every other suite is green:
  - motion `pass_start_engagement` 6/6, `pass_start_levels` 7/7;
  - motion lib `machining2d` 267 passed and 10 ignored, `level_ramp_entry` 4/4;
  - app `offset_pass_start` 4/4, `golden_cl` 33/33, `conformance` 7/7, `adaptive_pass_start` 4/4, `bore_pass_start` 3/3;
  - the catalogs 37/1/1;
  - clippy clean;
  - the light lane 2 twins green.

Where the time goes (temporary timers, removed):
- The motion plan and emit take 0.21 s (8850 moves).
- In the verifier (`camcraft_sim::verify::verify_bodies`), tangency takes 34.7 s for 2232 ramp moves. `reach::band_reach` does not finish in more than 3 minutes.
- Each ramp move ends at its own Z. The verifier cuts a new slice of the model at each distinct Z (`Rest::islands_at`). `band_reach` adds the boundary samples of each slice to one sample set and tests each move against all of them.

## Gate

The readings above are the gate of this head. The pinning tests are in `crates/motion/tests/pass_start_engagement.rs`. The motion lib pins are in `level_ramp_entry`, `pass_start`, `level_rings` and `level_order`.

## Not exercised

- No machine run. No posted G-code was read on a controller.
- No release-build run time of the fig8 Outside pocket.
- Adaptive with Outside keeps its old entry at dead ends.
- No heavy lane (P2, AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

Changelog: 2D Offset and 2D Pocket Outside: a later pass that starts at a dead end now enters by a ramp along the pass at the entry's ramp angle (3 degrees by default), not by a plunge or helix into uncut stock. At a dead end, the worst sampled start cuts with about 25 percent of the tool disc in uncut stock (12.6 mm2 of 50.3 mm2 for the 4.780 mm band), so the zig-zag cuts a slot at nearly full tool width at 3 degrees. A dead end too short for the ramp cuts the area in the Auto order, and the path names it.

title: test(2d): port the offset engagement pins
body:
Ports three engagement pins from PR #3439 onto main's Pass start law
(`crates/motion/src/machining2d/level_rings.rs` and `level_order.rs`).
The change is test-only. It changes no product code.

## What is ported

- `outside_on_a_figure_eight_band_never_slots`: Outside on a synthetic
  figure-eight band cuts no wider than 1.5 stepovers over any 3 tool
  radii of floor feed. Main pins this law only in the ignored heavy app
  test `fig8_outside_offset_cuts_no_move_at_full_width`. This pin gives
  default-suite coverage.
- `inside_on_the_band_clears_the_whole_band`: Inside on the round-part
  band leaves less than 0.5 mm2 of stock off the part wall. It checks
  both climb directions.
- `auto_on_the_band_slots_so_the_measure_sees_a_slot`: Auto (core first)
  on the same band slots. This pin is the positive control for the width
  measure.

## Readings

| Test | Result | Time |
|---|---|---|
| outside_on_a_figure_eight_band_never_slots | pass | 0.94 s |
| inside_on_the_band_clears_the_whole_band | pass | 2.08 s |
| auto_on_the_band_slots_so_the_measure_sees_a_slot | pass | 0.55 s |

Each test ran alone in debug with `-j 3`:
`cargo test -p camcraft-motion --test pass_start_engagement -- --exact <name>`.

## Not ported

- `outside_entries_after_the_first_land_in_cleared_stock` fails on main.
  The later entries cut 332.88 mm2 of uncut stock. Main's law does not
  lead a re-entry from cleared stock.
- `outside_on_a_split_band_never_slots` repeats main. The test
  `outside_band_split_by_the_part_cuts_no_move_at_full_width` already
  pins the same Outside split-band law.
- `pass_start::tests::a_start_on_a_wall_is_named_and_a_start_in_air_is_not`
  does not apply. It calls `start_wall_note`, which main replaced with
  `StartSide::wall_first_note`. Its assertions name one string that main
  splits into two strings.

## Not exercised

The figure-eight STEP app test stays in its heavy lane. This PR does not
change it and does not run it.

title: feat(3d): add waterlines switch to skip steep-flank ring pass
body:
## What changed

- Added `waterlines: bool` (default `true`) across `Finish3DParams`, `OpParams::Finish3D`, `ParamsDto::Finish3D`, MCP tools (`add_operation`, `edit_operation`, `list_operation_types`), project serialization (`#[serde(default = "default_true")]`), and the 3D Finish Passes UI tab (`Steep flanks`: `Waterlines` / `Leave uncut` with an inline consequence note).
- Updated `rings_and_tail_with_trim` and `swarf_multi` so `waterlines: false` skips the steep-flank waterline ring pass on shallow-first patterns, emits a visible steep-flank note on `Toolpath::notes` (surfaced in the UI status banner and MCP output), keeps uncut steep-flank stock visible to downstream rest checks, and refuses all-steep or no-shallow-cut models with `GenError::Empty`.
- Refused `waterlines: false` by name for ring-dependent patterns (`Waterline`, `Blend`, `Morph`), and hid the switch in the UI for patterns without a steep-flank waterline pass (`Waterline`, `Blend`, `Morph`, `Flat`, `Pencil`, `Corner`, `Geodesic`).
- Addressed all review items:
  - Pattern switch to `Waterline`, `Blend`, or `Morph` resets `*waterlines = true`, and the `Steep flanks` row stays visible whenever `!*waterlines` so users are never stranded on a refused value; stacked `Waterlines` and `Leave uncut` vertically inside `prop_row` in `crates/ui/src/egui_app/mill3d_page.rs` (378 lines) so radios do not overlap the `"Steep flanks"` label, pinned by `finish3d_waterlines_pattern_switch_resets_and_stays_visible_when_off`.
  - Added direct stamp test `finish3d_waterlines_flag_changes_op_stamp_directly` in `crates/app/tests/operations.rs` comparing `operation::op_stamp` between `waterlines: true` and `waterlines: false` (`0x4E`).
  - Added `1280x1180` before/after Passes tab screenshots on orphan fork branch `pr-screenshots/3550`.
- Merged `upstream/main` cleanly keeping `direction_angle`, `pass_start`, `Finish3D` Do not touch, and `waterlines` together, and recorded design decisions in `docs/decisions/2811-finish-waterlines-switch.md`.

## Screenshots (before / after, Passes tab at `1280x1180`)

| State | Screenshot |
|---|---|
| Before change | ![Passes tab before](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paulsvc/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3550/finish3d-passes-before.png) |
| After (`Leave uncut` selected + consequence line) | ![Passes tab after](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/paulsvc/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3550/finish3d-passes-after.png) |

## Verification

Verified via separate `gate-runner` under `PROCESS_VERSION 140` (#3556):

- Head `cb5e2c4fefca323bdbc7bab4aaca203c988bdc63` (differs from `b16439561` only in adding `waterlines: true` to test file `crates/motion/tests/rotary_coverage.rs`):
  - `cargo test -j 10 -p camcraft-motion --test rotary_coverage --test finish3d_waterlines`: `finish3d_waterlines` 5 passed, `rotary_coverage` 4 passed, 0 failed.
  - `cargo test -j 10 -p camcraft-app --test operations --test example_catalog --test mcp_doc_drift --test project_roundtrip`: `operations` 124 passed (6 ignored), `example_catalog` 39 passed (4 ignored), `mcp_doc_drift` 6 passed, `project_roundtrip` 82 passed, 0 failed.

title: fix(2d): support Do not touch on 2D Pocket operations
body:
Stacked on #3353 (merge #3353 first)

## What changed

- Add `OpType::Pocket` to `do_not_touch_applies` in `crates/app/src/operation/types/avoid.rs`.
- Update `do_not_touch_unsupported` to list `2D Pocket, 2D Offset and 3D Pocket`.
- Update the `set_operation_do_not_touch` text in `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`.
- Wire `OpParams::Pocket` with `avoid_spec` in `crates/app/src/operation/generate.rs` to `pocket_avoid_entered_with_relief`, `rest_pocket_avoid_with_relief`, and `rest_pocket_previous_avoid_with_relief`.
- Extract per-level planning (`plan_avoid_level`), relief checks (`check_reliefs_avoid`), crossing-free checks (`enforce_level_crossing_free`), and rest dispatch (`emit_rest_avoid`) into `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid_level.rs`.
- Unify plain and rest avoid paths in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/pocket_avoid.rs`, `rest2d.rs`, and `rest_prior.rs` under `pocket_avoid_over`.
- Check overhead keep-out zones up to `p.clearance_z.max(z)` so entry rapids and final clearance lifts clear overhead obstacles.
- Guard `Descent::Helix` (`m.solid_restart`) and `entry_restart` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/descent.rs` and `descent_dive.rs` with `helix_clears_prior`, `find_clear_helix_raw`, `moves_clear`, and `helix_cross_fallback`.
- Record between-pass `KeepDown` chords in `LinkState.level` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/ladder_links.rs`.
- Derive `Clone` for `LinkTally`, `LinkState`, and `WalkState`.
- Add pinning tests in `crates/motion/tests/avoid_pocket.rs`, `crates/app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`, and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/do_not_touch.rs`.
- Record the design choice in `docs/decisions/3345-do-not-touch-2d-pocket.md`.

## Cause

- `do_not_touch_applies` refused `OpType::Pocket`, and `OpParams::Pocket` in `generate.rs` dropped `avoid_spec`.
- `pocket_avoid` supported plain 2D Offset only. It lacked `PreHole` entries and rest plans, and it checked overhead obstacles only up to `retract_z`.
- When keep-out zones trimmed inner passes across depths under `OffsetRings` + `KeepDown` + `Helix`, restarted helices overlapped earlier helices in XY at shared entry depths.

## Tests

- Before the fix, `pocket2d_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face_and_edge` failed in `set_operation_do_not_touch`.
- Before the fix, `pocket2d_boundaries_shows_pick_protected_and_takes_viewport_click` panicked on the missing `"Pick protected"` button.
- After the final edit, `camcraft-motion --test avoid_pocket` passed all 6 tests (`empty_avoid_matches_plain_paths_exactly`, `pocket_avoid_all_strategies_entries_holder_and_edge`, `pocket_avoid_keeps_final_clearance_lift_clear_of_overhead_obstacle`, `pocket_avoid_offset_rings_keep_down_never_crosses`, `pocket_avoid_predrilled_and_rest_stay_clear`, `pocket3d_avoid_shell_rest_and_adaptive_stay_clear`).
- After the final edit, `camcraft-app --test do_not_touch` passed all 5 tests (`pocket2d_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face_and_edge`, `pocket2d_without_do_not_touch_gives_identical_toolpath`, `offset2d_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face_and_edge`, `pocket3d_do_not_touch_keeps_clear_raises_links_and_blocks_impossible_cut`, `do_not_touch_post_gate_blocks_violations`).
- After the final edit, `camcraft-app --test mcp_doc_drift` passed all 6 tests.
- After the final edit, `camcraft-ui --lib` passed all 4 `egui_app::tests::do_not_touch` tests (`pocket2d_boundaries_shows_pick_protected_and_takes_viewport_click`, `unsupported_op_shows_do_not_touch_note_without_pick_button`, `geometry_boundaries_shows_do_not_touch_controls_rows_and_viewport_marks`, `avoid_marks_cache_reuses_still_frames_and_follows_input_changes`).
- After the final edit, `env -u RUSTC_WRAPPER cargo clippy -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed with zero warnings.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed all 400 runnable steps with zero failures (`motion` 83 steps, `ui` 11 steps, `app` `lib` and 305 suites run in `--only` batches). `app build (--no-run)` was omitted because each batched `app` step built and ran its target directly, and `sccache` was disabled because the local cache server was unreachable.
- Mutation checks (reverted and restored):
  - Reverting `avoid.rs` made `pocket2d_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face_and_edge` fail in `set_operation_do_not_touch`. Restoring it passed.
  - Reverting `generate.rs` made `pocket2d_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face_and_edge` fail with gouges, `rapid_in_stock`, and flute and shank hits. Restoring it passed.
  - Mutating `top_above` in `pocket_avoid.rs` to `retract_z` made `pocket_avoid_keeps_final_clearance_lift_clear_of_overhead_obstacle` fail (`AvoidHit { at: 95, item: 1, part: Holder, short_mm: 13.0 }`). Restoring it passed.
  - Bypassing `helix_clears_prior` and `moves_clear` in `descent_dive.rs` made `pocket2d_do_not_touch_keeps_full_tool_clear_of_protected_face_and_edge` fail (`feed moves 55 and 437 cross in XY at shared depth`). Restoring it passed.

A temporary headless test rendered the real shell (`ShellUi`, `egui_kittest`, wgpu). The test is not in this branch.

title: fix(sim): judge spot drill cones at the part top
body:
The parent stack #3472 is merged. This branch is refreshed on the latest `main`.

## What changed

Judge an ordinary axial spot cone at the measured part top.
Use a separate optional `VerifyContext::rim_top_z` bound for finished hole walls.
Keep the stock top for rapid and collision checks.
Keep the nominal cutter radius for invalid caps, lateral feeds, and untrusted cutter geometry.
Other callers retain the stock-top fallback.

The synthetic case has a part top at Z12 and a stock top at Z13.
An 8 mm, 90-degree spot with its tip at Z10 now verifies and posts.
Its radius is 2 mm at the part top, inside the 2.5 mm hole radius.
A spot with its tip at Z9 still gives a gouge warning and blocks posting.

The decision record is `docs/decisions/3451-spot-drill-part-top.md`.

## Cause

The #3020 cone check measured the radius at the raw stock top.
Stock above the finished part enlarged that radius from 2 mm to 3 mm in this case.
The check then reported a finished-wall cut that did not exist.

## Tests

Application suite `spot_drill_verify`: 4 passed.

- `spot_cone_below_extra_stock_clears_the_part_and_posts`
- `spot_cone_below_extra_stock_that_cuts_the_part_blocks_post`

Verifier suite `spot_drill_radius`: 11 passed.

- `extra_stock_above_the_part_does_not_enlarge_the_spot_footprint`
- `a_spot_that_cuts_the_part_wall_still_gouges_below_extra_stock`
- `nonfinite_part_top_never_clears_the_nominal_radius`
- `a_part_top_does_not_clear_a_lateral_feed`

Parent regression after the refresh: `part_off_saved_before_3452`: 2 passed.
`a_part_off_saved_before_3452_loads_stale_and_does_not_post` reads `Stale` for the saved unsafe part-off and refuses the post.

Readings on head `f3c19705e`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 686 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 61.5 minutes.
- `spot_drill_verify`: 4 passed. `spot_drill_radius`: 11 passed.
- `part_off_saved_before_3452`: 2 passed. `turning_part_kerf`: 6 passed.
- `example_catalog::turning_cone_thread_case_posts_the_taper_and_the_thread`: 1 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 3 -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-sim --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

The new application clearance pin failed before the production change with `Gouge { at: 1 }`.
Restoring `radius.rs` from `main` made the direct clearance pin fail.
Restoring the fix made it pass.
Restoring `generate.rs` from `main` also made the application pin fail.
That mutation added only inert `rim_top_z: None` fields so the new context type compiled.
Restoring the fix made it pass.

The quick gate and the named pins are green on the refreshed head.
The readings are in the review comment of this PR.

## Goldens moved

None in this PR after the refresh.

The stack parent #3472 changed four NC files and two catalog project files.
That parent is now on `main`, so this PR has no golden or catalog diff:

- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`
- `crates/app/tests/golden/nc/inch/fanuc-lathe/groove_part.nc`
- `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.nc`
- `examples/catalog/turning/groove-part-off/groove-part-off.nc`
- `examples/catalog/turning/cone-thread/cone-thread.camproj`
- `examples/catalog/turning/groove-part-off/groove-part-off.camproj`

The two `.camproj` files changed the file format and their cached paths.
The tool rewrote each whole file: format 73 to format 76, new stamps, and new cached paths.
The posted `.nc` of each other operation is byte for byte the same.
`example_catalog` regenerates and compares it.
The cone-thread rough-profile cache changed from 476 moves to 433.
The cache differences come from `main` changes after the last catalog regeneration, not from this PR.

No CL golden changes.

## Not exercised

The original QA project and its preceding Face operation were not replayed.
The synthetic pin uses a legal R plane at raw stock Z13, with the part top at Z12 and tip at Z10.
Drill cannot use a tilted operation frame.
Framed contexts retain their conservative stock cap.
No UI window, real control, or machine was used.

title: fix(turning): part-off states the piece kept and a back stock
body:
Refreshed onto `main` after #3472 merged. The branch is no longer stacked.

## What changed

The Part (part-off) operation gets one setting, `kerf: PartKerf` (`crates/motion/src/turning/parting_law.rs`). It has two values:

- `kept`: the piece that is the finished part.
  - `CutOff` (the default) is the #3452 rule. The whole kerf is on the chuck side.
  - `Chuck` keeps the piece in the chuck. The whole kerf is on the free-end side, and a stub comes off the free end.
- `back_stock` (mm, 0 or more, default 0): the whole kerf stands this far off the parting plane, into the scrap side. The part keeps that much on its end face for a later facing pass.

Where the setting is:

- Kernel: `part_in` reads the scrap side and the kerf flank from the setting.
- Gouge law: `part_kerf_refusal_for` judges the kerf against the part that `kept` names. It treats the back stock as part material. The old `part_kerf_refusal` calls it with the default.
- Ambiguous setup (`job.rs`, `generate.rs`): #3472's `part_off_problem` and `plane_inside_model` rule refuses the default (`CutOff`) where the model goes on past the plane on both sides and the setup cannot say which end is free. When the user sets `Chuck`, the setting states the side and the ambiguity refusal does not fire. The refusal message names the setting: "Or set 'The part is' to 'Chuck piece' to state the side."
- Project file: the keys `kept` (`cut_off` / `chuck`) and `back_stock` (`project/part_kerf_dto.rs`). Each key is written only when it is not the default.
- Page: the Passes tab of the Part op has "The part is" (Cut-off piece / Chuck piece) and "Back stock". Apply rides `EditOperationParams`.
- MCP: `edit_operation` patches `kept` and `back_stock` through `EditOperationParams`. No new tool is necessary.
- Validation: a negative or non-finite back stock is refused at the command door (`is_sane`), in the kernel and in the verdict.
- Stamp: the setting is folded only when it is not the default. A Part cache made by the old centred-kerf algorithm reads Stale through #3472's `part-off-kerf-side-v1` salt and does not post until the op is generated again.

The decision record: `docs/decisions/3469-part-kept-side.md`.

## Cause

#3472 put the whole kerf on the chuck side, and no parameter could change the side. In a flipped second setup the chuck holds the finished part. #3472 had to refuse every part-off there, which refuses a legal program (issue comments of 2026-11-22).

## Readings (3 mm GT-0300 blade, orientation 2: the -Z corner is posted)

| case | kerf | posted Z |
|---|---|---|
| #3452 pin, end face Z-70, default | Z-73..-70 | Z-73 (no change) |
| same, back stock 0.5 | Z-73.5..-70.5 | Z-73.5 |
| same, chuck piece | refused: "nothing to part ... stands wholly on the free-end side (higher Z) ... set 'The part is' to 'Cut-off piece'" | - |
| stubbed pin in the OP20 flip setup, plane Z-14, default | refused by name (names `Chuck piece`) | - |
| same, chuck piece | Z-14..-11 | Z-14 (the part's end face) |
| motion: part Z0..70 in the chuck, stub to Z84, plane Z70, chuck piece | Z70..73 | - |
| same, chuck piece, back stock 1 | Z71..74 | - |

## Tests

New pins. Each was red on the unchanged code (#3472 head 6c18258d1): the motion and app pins did not compile (no `PartKerf`, no `kerf` field), and the flip pin is refused there.

- `crates/motion/tests/turning_part_kept.rs` (new, 5 tests): the default #3452 case, the back stock, the chuck piece, the refusal with no model on the chuck side, and a back stock that is not a size.
- `crates/app/tests/lathe_part_off_kerf.rs`: the flipped-setup default refusal (now #3472's precise rule, and it names `Chuck piece`), the flipped setup with `Chuck` that posts Z-14, the back stock that posts Z-73.5, the chuck piece with nothing in the chuck, and the undoable edit that rides the project file.
- `crates/app/tests/mcp_part_kerf.rs` (new): `edit_operation_sets_the_kept_piece_and_back_stock_and_undo_restores_them`.
- `crates/ui/src/egui_app/part_kerf_tests.rs` (new): `the_kept_piece_row_names_both_pieces_and_its_pick_applies_and_undoes`.
- `crates/app/tests/part_off_saved_before_3452.rs` (from #3472): opens a project recorded before #3452, asserts Stale and a refused post, then regenerates and posts.

Mechanical: each `OpParams::Part` and `PartParams` literal in the tests gets `kerf: Default::default()`.

### Mutation checks (each guard put back to the old code, then restored)

| mutation | result |
|---|---|
| kernel uses `chuck_side()` and the plane (ignores the setting) | RED: 3 tests of `turning_part_kept` |
| verdict ignores the back stock zone | RED: `a_back_stock_moves_the_whole_kerf_into_the_bar` |
| verdict uses `chuck_side()` (ignores `kept`) | RED: 2 chuck-piece tests |
| ambiguity refusal ignored for `Chuck` (the #3472 code) | RED: `a_flipped_setup_keeping_the_chuck_piece_cuts_the_stub_off_the_free_end` |
| no back stock check at the command door | RED: `the_kerf_setting_is_an_undoable_edit_and_rides_the_project_file` |

After the restore, all pins are green.

### Screenshots (the fork's images-only branch; no image is in this branch)

- Before: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/mkinney/Camcraft/1829a04cef3bc212316daaee35dd78c5c8c8c57a/3503/2026-11-22/part-passes-before.png

### Gate

- `cargo check -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets`: clean.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main` was started on the refreshed tree. The motion build and `motion suites: lib` passed (573 passed, 0 failed, 10 ignored, 204 s). The broad 714-step plan was stopped: a conflicts refresh runs the touched suites, not the whole plan.
- Pins on the pushed head `d9fd514b6142960a897b31c70806748dd5b1c28d`:
  - motion `turning_part_kept`: 5 passed.
  - motion `turning_part_kerf`: 6 passed.

  - app `mcp_part_kerf`: 1 passed.
  - app `part_off_saved_before_3452`: 2 passed.
  - app `setup_align_lathe`: 4 passed.
  - app `example_catalog` (full): 37 passed, 4 ignored.
  - ui `part_kerf_tests`: 1 passed.
- `cargo clippy -j 3 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.

### Heavy lanes

Not run. This is a `P3` PR (#3558). The cut gate runs the heavy lanes.

## Goldens moved

None. The merge of `main` brings #3472's corrected `cone-thread.nc` (`G01 X0. Z12. F0.02`) and its pin. The diff of this branch against `main` changes no `.nc`, `.cl` or catalog file.

## Not exercised

- A real control or machine. Lathe posts other than `fanuc-lathe.cps`.
- The UI in a live window (the page is tested through the kittest harness).

## Overlaps

- #3472 is merged, so this branch is no longer stacked.
- These open PRs touch the same files, but other functions or other kinds. None changes the Part variant, the Part page arm or the part-off law. Whichever merges second refreshes:
  - `operation/types/params.rs`, `project/params.rs`, `project/params_impl.rs`, `operation/kinds.rs`: #3494, #3441, #3439, #3426, #3402, #3391, #3387, #3353, #3283, #3251, #3103, #3058, #2890, #2831.
  - `operation/types/sane.rs`: #3426, #3402, #3283, #3251, #3058, #2831.
  - `operation/job.rs`, `operation/generate.rs`: #3458, #3283, #3251, #3115, #3059, #3058, and older ones.
  - `crates/ui/src/egui_app/mod.rs` (one `mod` line): many open UI PRs.

Effort: high (not escalated).

Changelog: Part (part-off) has a new setting. "The part is" chooses the cut-off piece (the default, as before) or the chuck piece, which cuts a stub off the free end of a part held end for end. "Back stock" moves the whole kerf that far off the parting plane, so the part keeps material on its end face for a later facing pass. The gouge check judges the kerf against the part that the setting keeps. Where a setup cannot say which end of the part is free, the default is refused and the refusal names the setting. An explicit chuck-piece setting states the side. Existing projects post the same program, and a pre-#3452 part-off cache is refused until it is generated again.

title: fix(post): post a short arc whose written ends share one angle as a straight move
body:
## What changed
- **Post rule.** `arcFateOf` (`crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs`) has one more rule. The written start and the written end differ, but they are on one ray from the written centre (the same angle). Or one end is on the written centre. If the record turns half a circle or less, the answer is `"linear"`. The post writes its straight feed move.
- The written centre is the centre that the control computes: the written start plus the written `I J K` increment (the script passes `inc`). The Heidenhain posts write an absolute centre and pass no `inc`.
- The rule reads the numbers of the written words. It uses only the zero of the cross product and the sign of the dot product. A mirrored axis or a lathe diameter word does not change these.
- A record whose own ends in the stream are on one ray (stream sweep 0) stays an arc in the post. `emitArcWithRadius` reads that as a full turn.
- **Stream writer rule (second review).** `cnc_arc_lattice::short_arc_on_lattice` (called by `cnc::serialize`) has the same rule on the micrometre lattice. The rounded ends differ, they are on one ray from the rounded centre (or one is on it), and the true sweep is positive and not more than half a turn. The writer then gives a `Feed` to the rounded end. A turn of more than half a circle keeps its arc record.
- `fanuc-lathe.cps` and `tormach-lathe.cps` now write the feed move for `"linear"` in their meridian arc path. Before, they wrote no block for any answer that was not `"arc"`.
- The full-turn test keeps main's exact stream endpoint equality.
- Decision: `docs/decisions/3474-same-angle-arc.md`.

## Cause
The #3442 guard compares only the written ends. When the ends differ only along the radius, the guard returned `"arc"`. Example, Fanuc mm: `G01 X10.011 Y5.` then `G03 X10.01 Y5. Z5.5 I-0.011 J0. F180`.

The start and the end are at the same angle about the centre. The radii are 0.011 and 0.010. RS-274 / ISO 6983 reads an arc whose end is at its start angle as a full turn. No control ran these blocks. A straight move is correct for each reading.

The app posts through `cnc::serialize`, which writes whole micrometres. A mm post with three decimals writes those numbers again. For the arc of the issue, the stream has a zero sweep, and the post cannot tell a short arc from a turn of 359.99 degrees. Only the writer knows the true sweep. Thus the writer has the rule too.

## Tests
`crates/post/tests/same_angle_stream.rs` (new, each test starts from unrounded geometry and goes through `serialize`):
- `the_arc_of_3474_through_the_stream_writer_posts_as_a_straight_move_on_fanuc`: a `Toolpath` through `dump` and `cnc::serialize`, Fanuc in mm and inch. No arc block, `G01` to the written end, byte-equal to the straight feed.
- `every_mill_post_writes_the_arc_of_3474_through_the_stream_writer_as_its_straight_move`: 15 mill posts in each unit that they offer.
- `the_lathes_post_a_same_angle_meridian_arc_through_the_stream_writer_as_a_straight_move`: `fanuc-lathe` and `tormach-lathe`, mm.
- `the_long_way_round_keeps_its_arc_through_the_stream_writer`: the same ends CW stay one arc block.

`crates/post/tests/cnc_arc_lattice.rs`:
- `a_short_arc_whose_rounded_ends_share_one_angle_is_written_as_a_feed`: XY, a helix, an end on the centre, XZ and YZ.
- `a_long_turn_an_opposite_end_and_a_visible_arc_keep_their_arc_record_on_one_line`.

`crates/post/tests/same_angle_arcs.rs` (the post rule on hand-written streams):
- `fanuc_and_linuxcnc_post_a_same_angle_arc_as_a_straight_move`
- `every_post_writes_a_same_angle_arc_as_its_straight_move`
- `a_same_angle_arc_about_the_written_incremental_centre_posts_as_its_straight_move`
- `arc_fate_reads_a_same_angle_short_arc_as_a_straight_move`

### Pin proof (on head `927a883be`)
- The writer ignores the ray rule: red. `same_angle_stream` fails 3 tests (Fanuc, each mill post, the lathes). `cnc_arc_lattice` fails 1 test. Restore: 4 + 4 passed.
- `_arcWrittenCentre` ignores `inc`: red (`same_angle_arcs`, 2 tests). Checked on `8f81cb1c`.
- The `1e-5` full-turn band is put back: red (`coincident_arcs`, 2 tests). Checked on `8f81cb1c`.

### Gates (on head `927a883be`, base `upstream/main` `4dba7019d`)
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 252 steps, 0 failed.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: 213 steps, 0 failed, 35.0 min.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: passed.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored. `example_catalog_adaptive`: 1 passed. `example_catalog_edge_work`: 1 passed. `short_arc_lattice`: 2 passed.
- `same_angle_arcs` 4 passed; `coincident_arcs` 8 passed; `radius_arcs` 7 passed.

The gates ran on the PR head, not on a merge with main. `git merge-tree` with `upstream/main` is clean.

## Goldens moved
None. The catalog suites, the quick gate and the heavy lanes ran on the final head. No recorded program (`.nc`, `.cl`, `examples/catalog/**`) changed.

## Not exercised
- No control ran the blocks. The reading of the controls is from RS-274 / ISO 6983, not from a run.
- A written end behind the written start (a written sweep of nearly a full turn on a short record). We found no input that makes it. It is recorded as dropped in the decision.
- Plasma and wire posts get the two rules through the same `arcFate` call and the same writer. They have no witness of their own. There is no inch lathe witness.
- A straight move of one or two output steps under active cutter compensation (G41/G42) was not checked on a control.
- No UI change: no screenshots.

Changelog: A post now writes a straight move for a very small arc whose written start and end have the same angle about the centre. Before, a control could read the block as a full turn.

title: fix(multiaxis): rotate the rotaries before the first five-axis approach descent
body:
## What changed

Five-axis generators set the first station's pose on the modal builder
and then pushed the descend to first contact, so the rotary swing rode
the approach move: the machine turned the A/C head while the tool
descended, and the ball swept through unknown air and through the rim
it approached.

The fix splits the approach. The pose is stated as its own zero-travel
Rapid (a standstill rotary index - the tip held on the hop plane, or at
the tip the machine already holds), and the Plunge/cut descends under
the pose already stated:

- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/curve.rs` (`contour_curve`): every
  chain's approach swings first, then plunges.
- `crates/motion/src/multiaxis/stamp.rs` (the stamp emit loop, all
  posed kinds - parallel5d, flow5d, swarf5d, rough, contour5d): at
  every rapid-to-cut re-entry where the pose changes, the swing is
  emitted at a standstill before the cut. Intermediate cut moves keep
  the modal tilt law unchanged.

No new `MoveKind`. The builder already keeps a zero-travel move whose
pose changed (it drops one only when the tip AND the pose both stand),
and the post already solves a zero-travel segment as a pure rotary
reorientation (`ds_tip == 0` in `crates/post/src/post/g93.rs`), so the
swing always commands. That is the answer to the zero-travel question:
the swing is a zero-travel rapid, not a short travel move - a travel
move would drag the tip sideways while the head turns, and a dropped
zero-travel move cannot occur, because a drop needs the pose to match
the held one, in which case no rotation is due.

## Readings

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 28 steps, 0 failed
  (motion lib 536 passed, multiaxis, multiaxis_avoid, multiaxis_rough,
  pivot5d, swarf_pose_continuity, app operations, posed_contact and the
  rest all green).
- The existing laws were amended where the swing touches them, each in
  its own terms: a TRAVEL rapid still inherits its pose
  (`rapids_hold_the_pose_they_inherit`, `rapid_pose_contract` - the
  zero-travel index is the second legal way a rapid states a pose,
  beside the swarf link's ball-centred swing); the air-link ratchet
  counts travel links only; the pivot-law ball readers skip the
  swing (it cuts nothing) through `no_swings`/`sans_swings` helpers.
- A decision record sits in `docs/decisions/3414-approach-rotary-order.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `the_approach_rotates_before_it_descends` (crates/motion/tests/pivot5d.rs):
  a zero-travel rotary swing precedes the first descend; the plunge
  holds the pose the swing stated; no pose change rides any move that
  crosses from air to material, over contour_curve, parallel5d, flow5d
  and swarf5d.

## What was not exercised

- No posted G-code golden was regenerated (the post's pure-rotary path
  is covered by its own suite; the swing was not posted end to end on
  a real machine file).
- The heavy lanes were not run; the diff touches `camcraft-motion`, so
  the release-tier lane check stays with the review/cut.

## Changelog

Five-axis approach moves rotate the machine to the first pose before
the tool descends to the part, no longer while it descends.

Fixes #3414

title: fix(multiaxis): close the Rotary Offset Zigzag levels with a ring that skips the seam
body:
## What changed

Rotary Offset Zigzag levels now finish their walls with a ring, as the
planar #3129 levels already do. On the wrap the plan drops only the
seam's own edges: a boundary loop that spans a whole period wraps the
seam, and its two cover-end edges are the seam's two copies at one
azimuth. That loop's ring keeps one period of boundary per leftover arc;
each arc arrives open and ends on the seam copy of its start azimuth -
closed on the work - while the rows cut the seam columns. A loop that
wraps no azimuth closes exactly as the planar ring always did. The
no-seam path is byte-for-byte the old `zigzag_ringed_passes` behaviour.

Before the fix the wrap kept its rows alone, so every wall perpendicular
to the rows kept cusps between row ends. Measured on the new test's
D-flat: the worst wall scallop falls from 0.071 mm to under 0.02 mm at
every level between the flat and the skin.

Placement: `machining2d::pocket_zigzag::ringed_passes` (the seam law,
one `Option<f64>` period), called from `machining3d::hsm::plan_level`.
Decision record: `docs/decisions/3168-rotary-zigzag-seam-rings.md`.

## Pinning tests

New suite `crates/motion/tests/rotary_zigzag_rings.rs`:

- `the_wrapped_ring_cuts_no_azimuth_twice` - on a developed cover two
  periods wide, the target band's ring cuts every azimuth once: no
  azimuth bin takes radial feed runs in both directions, and the band's
  walls stay within the wall-reach bound. This is the failure the old
  "a ring there would cut one seam line twice" comment feared.
- `the_dflat_edge_walls_are_ringed` - a D-flat bar wraps and its edge
  walls (perpendicular to the rows) finish within the wall-reach bound
  at every level between the flat and the skin. Run against the unfixed
  tree it fails with `scallop 0.071 mm`.

## What was not exercised

- The Adaptive seam law (`Seam::crossed_by`, the named refusals) is
  untouched and its own suites still cover it.
- No posted G-code golden was re-recorded; the change alters Zigzag
  wrap toolpaths by adding rings, which the level law's own tests do not
  pin.
- The heavy lanes reached by a `motion` diff were not run locally; the
  review runs them per AGENTS.md.

Changelog: Rotary Offset Zigzag levels finish their walls with a closing
ring that skips the seam, removing wall cusps on flats and other
perpendicular walls.

Fixes #3168

title: fix(3d): keep Finish3D clear of protected items
body:
Stacked on #3462 (merge #3462 first)

## What changed

3D Finish now accepts protected faces and edge chains.
The generator clips cuts outside a keep-out for the flutes, shank and holder.
The keep-out covers tip heights from the cut bottom to the clearance plane.
It rotates with the work coordinates.
Rapid links rise above protected items.
The final full-tool check refuses remaining contact and names the item.
The path notes that material beside protected items can remain unfinished.
Without protected items, the moves stay the same.
The existing command supplies undo and redo.
MCP help and its committed reference now name the supported kinds.

The change reuses `AvoidSpec::keepout_region`, `finish_clip::clip_path` and the existing WCS transform.
The decision record is `docs/decisions/3347-finish3d-do-not-touch.md`.

Review round 1 (head `f7ff1d080`):

- The branch now contains `upstream/main` `054c1e24b` (a merge commit, no conflict).
- The Trace fixture of `do_not_touch_click.rs` uses the 1,400 px height of Finish3D. The "Not taken" Start point and Exit point groups of #3324 moved "Pick protected" below the 1,100 px harness.

## Cause

Finish3D was absent from `do_not_touch_applies`.
Its generator did not read the protected geometry.

## Tests

App pins in `do_not_touch_finish3d`:

- `finish3d_accepts_protected_faces_and_edges_and_keeps_unprotected_moves`
- `finish3d_keeps_flutes_shank_and_holder_clear_of_a_protected_face`
- `finish3d_refuses_an_impossible_protected_cut_by_name_and_blocks_post`
- `finish3d_lifts_links_above_a_protected_face_higher_than_clearance`
- `finish3d_rotated_wcs_keeps_the_protected_face_in_setup_coordinates`

UI pins:

- `finish3d_shows_pick_protected_button`
- `finish3d_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click`
- `trace_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click`

The first app pin failed on unchanged production code with the unsupported-kind diagnostic.
All five app pins and the UI pins pass.
The checks include independent tool-band samples and the live protected-geometry check.
They cover a named refusal, blocked NC output, undo and redo, and unchanged unprotected moves.

Each mutation failed semantically, then passed after restoration:

- Restore the old upstream allow-list: protected Finish3D picks are refused.
- Restore the old upstream generator: the holder violates the protected face clearance.
- Skip the keep-out clipping: the final check refuses the holder contact.
- Skip the WCS conversion: the rotated path meets the protected face.
- Skip rapid routing: a link meets the tall protected face with the shank.
- Remove the named clip error: the refusal omits the protected item.
- Trace fixture at 1,100 px (the old height) on the merged tree: `trace_takes_a_protected_face_and_edge_by_viewport_click` fails at line 82 ("the group is armed"). At 1,400 px, all 8 `do_not_touch` UI tests pass.

Results on the final head `f7ff1d080`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: 171 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (69.5 min). This includes `ui suites: lib` and the eight UI integration suites.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- `cargo test -p camcraft-app --test example_catalog`: 37 passed, 4 ignored (the 4 are in the heavy lane, which passed).
