title: feat(motion): engrave and trace open and closed sketch chains
body:
Engrave and Trace now follow open and closed chains from a placed sketch. The user can select a profile, individual chains or a layer. The operation preserves the cut direction of lines, arcs and circles. It applies the sketch placement and the work-coordinate rotation to both endpoints and arc centers. A lift separates disconnected strokes and gaps accepted by the drawing tolerance.

Each depth level approaches from the stock surface. The existing stock, fixture, shank and mark-depth checks can hold the post, including jobs that have no part solid. Very short arcs below the post resolution give a diagnostic. A major arc is split into two arcs that keep its center and sweep. #3442 tracks the separate case where a native Fanuc post accepts a short arc supplied directly in an intermediate file.

The 18-move CL fixture contains an open line and clockwise quarter arc, a closed semicircle and diameter, and a full circle in two arcs. It records the tool rising to clearance between the three strokes.

## Goldens moved

No existing golden moves. One new recorded file is added.

- `crates/app/tests/golden/sketch_engrave_trace.cl` (NEW, not moved)

The new CL file records 18 moves. It contains an open line and clockwise quarter arc, a closed semicircle and diameter, and a full circle in two arcs. It records the tool rising to clearance between the three strokes. The test `placed_sketch_marks_keep_open_and_closed_arcs_and_retract_between_strokes` compares the generated moves with this file.

## Verification

- On the parent source, `placed_sketch_marks_keep_open_and_closed_arcs_and_retract_between_strokes` failed because an operation could not use picked sketch chains. The same test passed on this fix. The original CLI also refused both Engrave and Trace on a whole profile.

- `short_and_near_full_arcs_keep_their_center_and_sweep_through_a_rotated_work_offset` checks the arc centers and sweeps. The native CLI generated, verified and posted six synthetic drawings across both operations. Short representable arcs kept distinct endpoints. The 270-degree and near-full sweeps used split arcs with the correct centers. Both sub-resolution cases gave a named refusal and wrote no NC file.
- The focused gate passed 480 app tests, 127 post tests, and 29 motion tests on the final commit. Strict Clippy passed for all app, motion, and post targets with warnings denied. A broader motion run passed 646 tests with 10 ignored on the earlier branch revision with identical motion source.

title: feat(app): saved cut recipes - apply an operation's settings to new geometry
body:
## What changed

Saved cut recipes hold an operation's parameters, its tool name, and its workpiece material. A user library stores them in `recipes.camrecipes`, with a `camcraft-recipes/1` envelope. The folder is `CAMCRAFT_RECIPES`, else `<platform data dir>/camcraft/recipes`.

`ApplyCutRecipe` wraps `CreateOperation`. One undo removes the new operation. MCP tools `save_cut_recipe`, `list_cut_recipes`, and `apply_cut_recipe` use this library. Each tool accepts an optional `library` path. The generated MCP reference and the guide list the tools.

The caller supplies the new source. The command refuses a recipe by name if its saved parameters contain geometry that the API cannot replace. The audit covers:

- Drill holes and cross holes; bore and thread holes.
- Contour chain overrides and excluded deburr edges.
- Contour start and exit picks.
- Per-corner relief overrides of Pocket, Adaptive2D and Offset2D. A recipe with only the global relief kind still applies.
- Tilted plane origins.
- Circular centers, slot endpoints, probe targets, and undercut endpoints.
- Wire start and sync points; sinker burn positions.
- Waterjet tab positions. A waterjet recipe without tab positions still applies.

The command also refuses a missing tool, an unknown material, and a material mismatch. When a recipe names a material, the destination must have that material in force. An absent destination material now causes a refusal with the recipe name.

The library format stays the same. The decision record is `docs/decisions/3073-cut-recipes.md`.

## Review fixes and pin proof

The first review found two defects. Applying a recipe copied geometry from its previous source. The material check also accepted an absent destination material.

Regression pins in `crates/app/tests/cut_recipe/safety.rs`:

- `cut_recipe_does_not_transfer_holes_to_a_different_source`: transfer between plates with holes at different coordinates.
- `cut_recipe_refuses_other_saved_coordinates_by_name`: other operations with saved coordinates.
- `cut_recipe_refuses_saved_picks_and_plane_origins`: cross holes, entity picks, and tilted plane origins.
- `cut_recipe_with_a_named_material_requires_a_destination_material`: command refusal when the destination material is absent.
- `cut_recipe_mcp_refuses_an_absent_destination_material`: MCP refusal for the same case.

The second review found saved contour start and exit picks. The pins are in `crates/app/tests/cut_recipe/picks.rs`.

The four original tests in `crates/app/tests/cut_recipe.rs` also cover save, load, apply, generation, undo, and the existing refusals.

Mutation evidence: Removing the geometry guard made the geometry pins fail. Restoring the old material guard made both absent-material pins fail.

### Review of `44191d272`: per-corner relief overrides

The review found that a saved per-corner relief override passed the audit. Each override holds a source corner XY. `has_saved_geometry` now checks `corner_relief.overrides` of Pocket, Adaptive2D and Offset2D.

Pins in `crates/app/tests/cut_recipe/relief.rs`:

- `cut_recipe_refuses_saved_corner_relief_overrides_by_name`: command refusal for the three kinds.
- `cut_recipe_mcp_refuses_saved_corner_relief_overrides`: the MCP reproduction of the review (40 x 40 stock, override at `[20, 20]`, then 60 x 60 stock).
- `cut_recipe_applies_global_corner_relief_without_overrides`: a global dogbone recipe applies for the three kinds.
- `cut_recipe_mcp_applies_global_corner_relief`: a global dogbone recipe applies and generates through MCP.

Mutation evidence: with the new check removed, the two refusal pins failed (16 passed, 2 failed). With the check restored, all 18 recipe tests passed.

### Review of `d8f36c3a2`: waterjet tab positions

Newer `main` has `OpParams::WaterjetProfile` (#3058). The exhaustive `match` in `has_saved_geometry` did not cover it, so the trial merge did not compile. The branch now has a merge of `upstream/main` (`8473cb6a8`, no conflict) and the new arm (`e04a76c8e`). A tab position (`tabs.at`) is a world X, Y of the source contour. `ApplyCutRecipe` refuses a recipe whose `tabs.at` is not empty. A waterjet recipe without tab positions applies.

Pins in `crates/app/tests/cut_recipe/waterjet.rs`:

- `cut_recipe_refuses_saved_waterjet_tab_positions_by_name`: command refusal. The same parameters are legal in `CreateOperation`.
- `cut_recipe_applies_a_waterjet_recipe_without_tab_positions`: the recipe applies and generates.

Mutation evidence: with the arm changed to `false`, the refusal pin failed (19 passed, 1 failed). With the arm restored, all 20 recipe tests passed.

## Final validation

Head: `e04a76c8e979db89db4bf73e3e55c304ffc1f220`
Base: `upstream/main` at `ddc4d82741f65f483cdadcddb256464fb56ab883`. The head contains a merge of that base. All gates ran on the merged head.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 364 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (22.5 minutes).
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 219 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled (29.8 minutes).
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `app suites: cut_recipe`: 20 passed, 0 failed.
- `app suites: example_catalog` and `app suites: first_router_part` passed in the quick gate. `app heavy: example_catalog` passed in the heavy gate.
- The golden suites that the diff reaches ran in the quick gate. All passed.
- `cargo xtask gate light` did not run in this round.

## Goldens moved

None. After the catalog suite and the gates ran, the working tree was clean. No recorded program or golden file changed.

## Not exercised

- UI screenshots do not apply. This PR changes no UI files.
- There is no GUI recipe panel. Issue #3393 holds that work.
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill has no row for the new tools. This PR supplies the generated reference and guide entries.
- Recipes omit coolant and area controls. Coolant depends on the machine. Area controls depend on the geometry.
- Automatic geometry matching is not exercised. The command refuses recipes that need replacement geometry.

title: feat(release): optionally sign and notarize the macOS packages
body:
The macOS packaging step can sign the app and its three executables with Developer ID. It can submit the app and the DMG to the Apple notary service. It staples the app before it makes the final ZIP. It staples and validates the DMG before publishing either archive.

With no signing inputs, the packager keeps the ad hoc path and reports it. An incomplete set of inputs stops packaging. The release workflow passes the five optional secrets only to the packaging step. A private temporary keychain holds the certificate. The script removes temporary credentials on exit. The release triggers and permissions stay the same.

## Verification

On commit `e536469d0`, all five packaging fixture tests passed, including six simulated failure cases. `test_signed_zip_and_dmg_include_validated_tickets` checks the two archives. `test_partial_signing_settings_fail_before_packaging` checks incomplete inputs. The original script failed nine fixture assertions. Shell parsing, release workflow YAML parsing, the five secret mappings, and the commit whitespace check passed.

A second test used native macOS tools and three small universal Mach-O programs. It extracted the ZIP and mounted the DMG read-only. It verified ad hoc signatures, the arm64 and x86_64 slices of each program, the icon, an example, and the Applications link. This test exposed an incompatible two-architecture lipo check. The final script checks each architecture separately.

## Limits

The Developer ID and notary service tests used simulated credentials and command responses. No production identity, Apple submission, release upload, or hosted workflow ran. A maintainer with the release credentials must confirm Apple's acceptance on a signed build.

Changelog: macOS release packages can use Developer ID signing and Apple notarization when the release credentials are configured.

Effort: medium

Fixes #1642

title: feat(text): place typed text in a TrueType outline font as closed shapes
body:
## What changed

- New module `camcraft_geometry::outline_text`. It reads a TrueType outline font and makes a typed string into closed shapes, in mm, on the layer `text`.
  - `ttf.rs` is our own reader, written from the public OpenType specification. It reads `cmap` formats 4 and 12, `loca`, `glyf` (simple and composite glyphs), `hmtx`, `hhea`, `maxp`, `head` and the `OS/2` cap height. Each read has a bounds check.
  - `mod.rs` flattens the quadratic contours to lines, with a chord error of 0.005 mm or less. It then makes a `SketchData` with closed chains only.
  - `sample_font.rs` makes a small test font in memory. It has our own glyphs, so the repository stores no font file.
- New undoable command `InsertOutlineText` (`crates/app/src/commands/insert_outline_text.rs`). It reads the font once at construction. The profile keeps the shapes, not the font, so the project file format does not change.
- New MCP tool `insert_outline_text` (`crates/app/src/mcp/outline_text_tools.rs`). The tool is also in `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (generated) and in the MCP guide table.
- These inputs are refused by name:
  - a font that cannot be read, a CFF font (`.otf` with PostScript outlines) or a font collection;
  - an empty text, or a character that the font does not have;
  - outlines that cross or touch;
  - a nested outline that runs in the same direction as the outline around it (`OutlineTextError::Winding`);
  - a height or a spacing outside the limits;
  - a setup that does not exist, a setup with no stock, or a name that is in use.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/3072-outline-text.md`.

## Cause

This is a new feature (#3072). Before this PR, typed text was only single-stroke engraving text (`insert_text`, #2679).

## Review fixes

Round 1:

- Large curves keep the 0.005 mm chord tolerance. A curve can use up to 4096 pieces. A curve that needs more is refused.
- Composite glyphs apply `SCALED_COMPONENT_OFFSET`. A component with both offset flags is refused.
- Table reads use each declared table boundary. Character maps also use each declared subtable boundary.

Round 2:

- Nonzero winding fill. The sketch reads holes by nesting, but a TrueType font fills by the nonzero winding rule. These two readings agree only when each outline runs opposite to the innermost outline around it. `check_winding` in `outline_text/mod.rs` refuses all other arrangements by name. Thus a same-direction inner contour is never made a hole.
- Red verification result. The branch was 106 commits behind `upstream/main`. On the old base, `blind_slot`, `corner_relief_safety` and one post-dialog UI test failed. The trial merge of the reviewer passed them. I merged `upstream/main` into the branch with a merge commit (no rebase, no conflicts). The earlier author run reported a working graphics adapter and a green quick gate on its then-current head. The current round results are below.

Round 3:

- Merged current `upstream/main` `edcbfe4dd678da799d1102cd8324403afaa5c344` with a clean merge commit.
- The GPU bounds loop now iterates over dimensions. This clears the reported upstream `needless_range_loop` warning and preserves every bounds check.
- No UI test was changed or disabled. The current sandbox run cannot find a Metal graphics adapter. No software fallback is available in this build.

Round 4 (second safety read on `4cc0638ee`):

- Composite visit budget. One glyph can make at most 4096 component visits (`MAX_PARTS` in `outline_text/ttf.rs`). A tree of empty parts is refused as `FontError::Corrupt`. The point count is now kept as a running budget.
- Text vertex budget. The flattened points of the whole text are limited to 2,000,000 (`MAX_VERTICES`, the primitive limit of the sketch chainer). The budget is charged before each point is made. A text over the limit is refused as `OutlineTextError::TooManyVertices`.
- Glyph coordinate range. A coordinate outside the 16-bit range is refused. A simple glyph has at most 65,536 points, so the i32 sum cannot overflow. Without the check, an out-of-range coordinate was accepted with no message.
- The decision file now states that kerning (`kern`, `GPOS`) and `USE_MY_METRICS` are ignored. It also states that fonts with overlapping contours are refused.
- `sample_font::build_font` makes the hostile test fonts in memory. It accepts raw glyph bytes and an optional `OS/2` cap height.
- I merged current `upstream/main` (`82fb91a0f`) with a merge commit. There were no conflicts. The merge brings the upstream fix of `mcp_setup_moves`.

Round 5 (review of `e1d36f437`):

- The one request was a green `app suites: first_router_part`. The fix of #3698 (PR #3703) is on main. I merged `upstream/main` (`09ad779ee`) with a merge commit, `9ef208d71`.
- The merge had one conflict, in the generated `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (the tool count line). I took the file of main and wrote it again with its documented command. It differs from main only by the count (121) and the `insert_outline_text` row.
- No source of this PR changed. This PR does not change the test or the demo project.

## Tests

- Pin proof, round 4. I broke each fix and ran its pin. Then I restored the fix:
  - `a_composite_tree_of_empty_parts_is_refused_without_a_walk`: with the visit budget off, the test hung until a 90 s timeout. Restored: passed.
  - `the_flattened_points_of_a_text_are_bounded_before_they_are_made`: with the vertex budget off, `outlines()` accepted the text. Restored: passed.
  - `a_coordinate_outside_the_16_bit_range_is_refused`: with the range check off, the coordinate was accepted. Restored: passed.
- Geometry `outline_text`: 13 passed, 0 failed on the final head.
- App `insert_outline_text`: 4 passed, 0 failed on the final head.
- Pin proof, round 2: `nested_outlines_follow_the_nonzero_winding_fill`. With the `check_winding` call removed, the test failed at `crates/geometry/tests/outline_text.rs:233` (the same-direction `O` was accepted). With the call restored, it passed. The test also checks that an `O` with both directions swapped still has one hole, and that `II` stays two shapes.
- Pin proof, round 1: the four round-1 tests failed with the original reviewed source and passed with the fixes:
  - `large_curves_measure_inside_the_chord_tolerance`
  - `composite_offsets_use_the_component_transform`
  - `declared_table_lengths_bound_reads_with_trailing_bytes`
  - `declared_cmap_subtable_lengths_bound_reads`

- Pin proof, round 3: `cargo clippy -j 6 -p camcraft-gpu --all-targets -- -D warnings`, with rustc 1.99.1. Restoring the original range loop in the source produced **RED** at `crates/gpu/src/cut.rs:126`. Restoring the fixed dimension iterator in the source produced **GREEN**. The lint command pins this mechanical change.


Final head: `9ef208d7140316416504ca7d9e28083f55988f89`. Gate base: `upstream/main` `09ad779ee` (merged into this head). The build is from source (`CAMCRAFT_NO_SEED=1`).

- `cargo xtask gate test first_router_part --crate camcraft-app`: **GREEN**. 2 steps, 0 failed. `first_router_part`: 4 passed. `first_part_programs::first_router_part_posts_the_shipped_program`: passed.

title: feat(post): add the G-EDM 2-axis wire EDM post (g-edm.cps)
body:
## What changed

- New post `assets/posts/g-edm.cps`, registry name "G-EDM Wire EDM". It serves `wire_edm` machines only. "Generic ISO Wire EDM" stays the default (`WIRE_POSTS[0]`).
- The post writes Grbl-family words only: `G21` / `G20 G90 G17`, `G0` to the threading point, `G1`, `G2` / `G3` with incremental `I J`, and `M30`.
- The post writes no `%` fence, no `O` word, no `F`, no `G40` / `G41` / `G42`, and no work offset word.
- The post reads no `edm.codes`. The condition id is a comment. The header says that the operator sets the spark power at the controller.
- The header has `(NOT VERIFIED ON A CONTROL - CHECK BEFORE CUTTING)`.
- The post writes one vertical 2-axis wire section for each program.
- These items are refused by name, and no cut is written for the section:
  - a machine that is not `wire_edm`, a rotary, `edm.awt: true`;
  - `WireTaper` not 0, `WireFourAxis`, `WireU` / `WireV`, `WireAngle`;
  - each `COMP` record (G41 / G42);
  - skims;
  - a work offset other than G54;
  - `SpindleSpeed` above 0, `onToolChange`, `onCycle`, a `Z` change;
  - `AfterOperation` `home`, `stop` and `optional-stop`;
  - a second wire section in the same program.
- Registered in `crates/app/src/posting.rs` (`WIRE_POSTS`) and `crates/app/src/posting_files.rs` (`BUILTINS`, `embedded()`).
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`: `WIRE_POSTS` and `EXTENSIONS` name the new post.
- Docs: `assets/posts/AGENTS.md`, the user guide pages `posting.md` and `machines.md`, and `docs/decisions/2700-g-edm-post.md`.

## Cause

`wire-iso.cps` requires `edm.codes.condition` and `edm.codes.comp_off`, and it writes `%` fences. A G-EDM build sets spark power at the controller and has no condition word. A raw Grbl parser rejects `%`. So no shipped post served a G-EDM build.

## Readings

- #2697 has no new answer from the reporter. The unconfirmed items (`F` and Grbl `error:22`, `G40`, `G54`-`G59`, `M0` pauses, a return move) are not written. The decision file gives the reason for each.
- No `F` word: if G-RBLv3 keeps the Grbl `error:22` check, the controller stops at the first `G1`, before any cut. That is a visible stop, not a wrong cut.
- One section for each program: without a confirmed `M0`, the program cannot stop to cut the wire and thread it again. A `G0` to a second start point would pull the threaded wire through the work.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/app/tests/g_edm_post.rs` (9 tests):

- `g_edm_inch_and_arc_words`
- `g_edm_refuses_taper_four_axis_and_lean_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_radius_compensation_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_skims_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_a_mill_machine_and_a_milling_stream_by_name`
- `g_edm_refuses_what_the_controller_cannot_be_told`
- `g_edm_refuses_a_rapid_with_the_wire_threaded_by_name` (review round 1: a rapid between two cuts refuses by name, and no cut follows it)

Script suite `crates/post/tests/script_g_edm.rs`: 11 recorded streams, each a named refusal (`crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/g-edm/`).

Red before the fix: all 8 app pins failed with `built-in post G-EDM Wire EDM is not in the registry`.

Mutations (each guard turned off, the pins run, then restored):

- skim guard off: `g_edm_refuses_skims_by_name` red
- `onRadiusCompensation` guard off: `g_edm_refuses_radius_compensation_by_name` red
- one-section guard off: `g_edm_refuses_what_the_controller_cannot_be_told` red

- rapid-while-threaded guard off (`onRapid`, `if (threaded)`): `g_edm_refuses_a_rapid_with_the_wire_threaded_by_name` red

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` on head `880e5e3d2` (main `f35202134` merged): 797 steps, 0 failed, 1 stalled. The stalled step is `app build (--no-run)`, a cold build after a `cargo clean` with no output for 15 min. title: feat(cl): translate, XY turn, A/B turn and vertical mirror for toolpaths
body:
## What changed

- A new module `crates/cl/src/cl/transform.rs` with three sub-files (`transform_rotary.rs`, `transform_mirror.rs`, `transform_climb.rs`). `camcraft-app` re-exports it as `app::cl::transform`.
- `translate(tp, [dx, dy, dz])` shifts every move, arc center, canned cycle, compensated span and edge break.
- `transform_xy(tp, tx, ty, angle_deg, pivot)` turns the path in XY about a pivot and then shifts it. Nesting (#2166) can call it directly.
- `rotate_about_axis(tp, RotaryAxis::A | B, origin, angle_deg, chord_tol)` turns the path about X or Y. Each move states the turned tool axis. Arcs become chords within `chord_tol`, or return `ArcChordTolerance`.
- `mirror_plane(tp, MirrorPlane, MirrorMode)` mirrors the path across a vertical plane.
  - `GeometricMirror` gives the exact mirror image: G2 <-> G3 and G41 <-> G42.
  - `PreserveClimb(PassFamily)` mirrors and then runs each pass backwards between its entry and its retract. The lead-out becomes the lead-in. The arcs keep their original G2/G3, and the compensated spans keep their original side.
- `TransformError` names each refusal: `ThreadCycle`, `ProbeTouch`, `RotaryMove`, `TiltedMove`, `PlasmaCut`, `VerticalArc`, `CannedCycleTilt`, `FineBoreShift`, `ArcChordTolerance`, `HorizontalMirrorPlane`, `TiltedMirrorPlane`, `BadInput`, `NotReversible(why)`.
- The decisions are in `docs/decisions/3011-cl-transforms.md`.

## Cause

This is new work. The codebase had no shared transform for toolpaths. Patterns, mirror folders and nesting need one.

## Design

- All four transforms use one map, `p -> M p + t`, with `M` orthogonal.
- An arc keeps its plane only when `M` maps the plane normal exactly onto plus or minus itself. Its turn direction flips when `det(M)` times that sign is negative. This one rule gives the G2/G3 swap under a mirror. It also finds the XZ / YZ arcs that a transform cannot keep.
- Moves, arc centers and cycles snap to the coordinate lattice. Edge-break polylines do not snap, because a snap would move framed caps off orthonormal.
- `PreserveClimb` accepts only contour, profile and chamfer paths. It refuses these by name:
  - a helical ramp, adaptive clearing, multi-pass roughing and other families;
  - a ramp or helical entry;
  - a level change without a retract;
  - a cut before the first pass or after the last pass;
  - a link that is not on the clearance plane.

## Latest review fix (second safety read on `91cd4fe1a`)

1. **Fine boring under a turn or a mirror.** A `CycleKind::FineBore` cycle shifts the tip with a lateral rapid at the hole bottom. The oriented spindle stop fixes that direction on the machine. `transform_xy` and `mirror_plane` now refuse a fine-bore cycle when the matrix is not the identity, with the new error `FineBoreShift`. `translate` and a whole turn (0 or 360 degrees) still accept it. `rotate_about_axis` refuses every cycle already.
2. **`PreserveClimb` leads.** The reversed pass plunges where the old pass left its cut. The cl layer cannot tell a lead from the contour. The reversal now requires symmetry: the first cut move and the last cut move have one shape (straight or arc) and one length, within 2 um. A pass with a lead-in and no lead-out, or with a shorter lead-out, is refused by name with `NotReversible`.
3. **Notes.** The decision file now says that a geometric mirror of a thread-milling helix changes the hand of the thread. It also says that heights outside the path do not move with a Z translate.

New pins:

- `fine_bore_refuses_an_xy_turn_and_a_mirror_and_translates` (`transform_tests.rs`): a 180 and a 90 degree turn and a mirror refuse; a translate and a 360 degree turn accept; a drill cycle still turns and mirrors.
- `preserve_climb_refuses_a_lead_in_without_a_lead_out` (`transform_mirror_tests.rs`): the review case (5 mm lead-in, no lead-out) and a 2 mm lead-out refuse; a matching 5 mm lead-out reverses, and the reversed plunge is in the air.

Pin proof: I disabled the two new checks (`if false && ...`). `cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform` was RED: 24 passed, 2 failed (the two new pins). I restored the checks: GREEN, 26 passed.

Head: `b0efe2ee629a83ac78f732bdb3dbc639025ad824`. Base: `upstream/main` at `44c13a01d8879fbdcd424ca6653e61b5ecd9d12b`.

- `cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`: GREEN, 26 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl --all-targets -- -D warnings`: GREEN.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 1,077 steps, 0 failed, 16.2 minutes. It includes `cl suites: lib`, `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `golden_cl` and `clippy -D warnings`.
- `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`: GREEN, 241 steps, 0 failed, 28.3 minutes.

Goldens moved: none. The catalog and `golden_cl` suites ran and passed. No recorded program changed.

Not exercised: a trial merge with `upstream/main`. The runs test the PR head. A helix arc and an edge-break cap under a turn or a mirror still have no pin.

## Earlier review fix (collapsed arcs)

The latest review found that a collapsed arc could remove a tool axis change. Rounded chord endpoints could match after a preceding move at another pose.

The rotary transform now drops a collapsed chord only when its axis also matches the last emitted pose. It retains a changed axis as a straight move at the standing tip. The move keeps its kind and feed. The same rule retains an initial collapsed arc that states a pose. A distance tolerance cannot permit removal of a required rotation.

## Tests (pins)

The original 20 tests are in `crates/cl/src/cl/transform_tests.rs` and `transform_mirror_tests.rs` (`cargo test -p camcraft-cl --lib transform`):

- `translate_shifts_every_record_to_the_micron`, `translate_refuses_a_non_finite_offset`
- `transform_xy_turns_a_quarter_about_the_pivot_then_shifts`, `transform_xy_at_thirty_degrees_is_micron_accurate`, `transform_xy_refuses_a_vertical_arc_it_cannot_keep`
- `rotate_about_a_turns_the_point_and_states_the_axis`, `rotate_about_b_flattens_arcs_within_the_chord_tolerance`, `rotate_about_an_axis_by_zero_is_the_identity`, `rotate_about_an_axis_refuses_a_tilted_canned_cycle`
- `every_transform_refuses_thread_cycles_probe_touches_and_c_moves`
- `geometric_mirror_swaps_g2_g3_and_g41_g42`, `geometric_mirror_on_a_diagonal_plane_is_micron_accurate`, `mirror_refuses_horizontal_and_tilted_planes`, `mirror_refuses_tilted_moves`
- `preserve_climb_reverses_the_pass_between_entry_and_retract`, `preserve_climb_reverses_two_depths_linked_on_the_clearance_plane`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_helical_entry`, `preserve_climb_refuses_clearing_families_by_name`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_cut_before_the_first_pass`, `preserve_climb_refuses_a_level_change_without_a_retract`

The initial implementation report states that these pins did not compile before the API existed.

This round adds `rotate_about_a_preserves_the_axis_when_an_arc_collapses`. It checks a short arc after a rapid at another pose. It checks the transformed axis, standing tip, feed, move kind and chain. It also checks the straight-feed control and the unchanged-pose control.

Final head: `91cd4fe1a54a2aae98b95241bbcbbdf563f54c05`.

Pin proof for this round: the verifier saved the fixed rotary source outside the repository. It replaced only that source with the reviewed version from `defb39c9c512312df3ee4723476bc284237b6e33`. The new pin stayed in place.

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib rotate_about_a_preserves_the_axis_when_an_arc_collapses -- --nocapture
```

Result: RED, 0 passed and 1 failed. The test expected two moves but received one. The verifier restored the fix and ran:

```sh
CARGO_INCREMENTAL=0 RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache cargo test -j 24 -p camcraft-cl --lib transform
```

Result: GREEN, all 24 transform tests passed.

## Previous review fix and evidence

The previous review found that the arc sampler stops at 1,024 chords. A 1,000 mm semicircle exceeded the requested 0.0001 mm tolerance.

The rotary transform retains that bounded sampler. It samples at half the requested tolerance. It checks the curve error for the actual chord count and adds the endpoint rounding error. Circular arcs use the sagitta bound. Radius ramps use the sampler's second derivative bound. `ArcChordTolerance` refuses a path when the total bound exceeds `chord_tol`.

That round added these three pins:

- `rotate_about_a_refuses_an_arc_beyond_the_chord_budget`: refuses the review case. It also measures chord midpoint error on an accepted 1,000 mm semicircle.
- `rotate_about_b_bounds_arc_midpoints_in_each_plane`: measures analytic curve midpoint error in XY, XZ and YZ. It covers circular arcs, radius ramps, normal interpolation and both turn directions.
- `rotate_about_a_refuses_rounding_beyond_the_chord_tolerance`: refuses an arc whose endpoint rounding exceeds the tolerance.

Historical proof on `defb39c9c512312df3ee4723476bc284237b6e33`: restoring the rotary source from `a273ee018` made two pins fail. The chord-budget and rounding-refusal pins failed. Restoring the fix made all 23 transform tests pass. These results describe the previous round.

The initial implementation report records these mutation results:

- the G2/G3 flip: 3 pins red
- the G41/G42 swap: 2 pins red
- the side restore in the climb reversal: 1 pin red
- the probe refusal: 1 pin red
- the refusal of a cut before the first pass: 1 pin red
- the horizontal-plane refusal: 1 pin red
- the pass reversal: 2 pins red
- the tilted-cycle refusal: 1 pin red

title: feat(post): add RichAuto DSP A11 3-axis router post (.mmg format)
body:
## What changed

- New post `assets/posts/richauto.cps` for the RichAuto DSP A11 router controller.
- The post is registered as `"RichAuto DSP A11"` in `BUILTINS` (`crates/app/src/posting_files.rs`). It comes after Mach4, before Mach3.
- The output follows the `.mmg` program that a Laguna Swift A11 runs (#1907, comment of 2026-11-18). The comment of 2026-11-18 on this issue names that program as the conformance target.
  - The file extension is `.mmg`.
  - Each block has a sequence number: `N10`, then steps of 10. Comment lines and the `%` line have no number.
  - There are no spaces between words.
  - Lengths have three decimals. `F` is mm/min with one decimal.
  - Rapid is `G00` and feed is `G1`. The spindle starts with `M03S<rpm>` and stops with `M05`.
  - An axis word or an `F` word that does not change is not written.
  - The program ends with `M30` and then a `%` line.
- The setup block is `G21G90G17`. The post writes no `G54`, `G40`, `G80`, `G91.1`, `G94`, `G43`, `G49`, `T` or `M6` word.
- Offset 1 is the work origin that the operator sets on the pendant. Offsets 2 and higher are refused by name.
- Arcs use incremental `I`/`J`/`K` (`AbsCntr = Off`). An arc of more than 180 degrees is split.
- Drilling cycles are expanded to plain `G00`/`G1` moves, with the floor dwell and the bore spindle stop and restart.
- The `SpindleDwellMs` option writes `G04P<ms>` after the spindle start. The default is 0.
- The post refuses these by name: tapping, `G41`/`G42`, probing, rotary moves, `G96`, a second tool, an inch document, a bad rpm, a bad coolant, and a missing or low clearance plane.
- The post writes header notes (#2996) and WARN records as `(...)` comments.

## Cause

The shipped posts do not run safely on an A11. They write `G91.1`, `G53`, `T.. M6`, `G43` and canned cycles. A basic A11 firmware can refuse these words.

## Tests

- `crates/post/tests/script_richauto.rs` and `crates/post/tests/richauto_safety/mod.rs`: 43 tests, including the 11 recorded-stream goldens of `post_suite!`.
- The pin `richauto_writes_the_a11_mmg_block_format` was red on the older held script (format without `N`, `%`): `the program ends with %`. It is green on the new script.
- On `upstream/main` all the pins are red, because the post does not exist.
- `crates/app/tests/conformance.rs`: RichAuto is added to `POSTS`, `REFUSED` (`tap_plate`, "tapping"), the synth stream (G54, no tap) and `EXTENSIONS` (`mmg`). All 7 tests pass.
- `crates/post/tests/comment_escape.rs`: 22 text posts write both header notes. The native Agie dispatcher refuses them by name.
- Mutations. Each mutant was run against the pins, then the script was restored and the pins were green again:
  - no final `%` line: 8 tests red, including `richauto_writes_the_a11_mmg_block_format`;
  - spaces between words: 18 tests red;
  - no modal word omission: 11 tests red, including `unchanged_axis_and_feed_words_are_left_out`;
  - no `onComment` hook: `comment_escape::header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound` red;
  - no sequence step (all blocks `N0`): 7 tests red.
- The earlier coolant fix retains operation names in every coolant refusal. The pin is `richauto_safety::coolant_refusals_name_the_operation`.

## Fix round 3: coincident arc guard (review of `e276e3605`)

Finding: `onCircular` wrote an arc block whose written end was its written start. The A11 reads such a block as a full circle (#3442, #3474).

- `assets/posts/richauto.cps`: `onCircular` now asks the PRELUDE guard `arcFate(arcWord, arcIncOf(fu))`. It uses the words that this post writes: work coordinates, three decimals, incremental centres.
- A short arc under the output step posts as its straight feed move, or as no block. The refusals of `onCircular` stay before the guard. A "none" arc writes no plane word.
- The branch merges `upstream/main` at `3fc0e017b8f9ba3444cfc8b006186c94c87f6a3c`. The merge was clean. It brings `crates/post/tests/same_angle_arcs.rs` (#3474).
- Pins:
  - `("richauto", Kind::Mill)` in `POSTS` of `crates/post/tests/coincident_arcs.rs`.
  - `"richauto"` in `MILLS` of `crates/post/tests/same_angle_arcs.rs`.
  - `richauto_safety::an_arc_under_the_output_step_is_no_arc_block` compares the written words.
  - The arc reader `coincident_arcs/reader.rs` now reads the compact block form `N60G3X18.123Y5.432...`.
- Pin proof: with the guard disabled (`var fate = "arc"`), four tests were RED. With the guard, all were GREEN.
  - `coincident_arcs::every_post_writes_no_coincident_arc_block_and_keeps_its_real_arcs`. It reported the four blocks of the review.
  - `same_angle_arcs::every_post_writes_a_same_angle_arc_as_its_straight_move`.
  - `same_angle_arcs::a_same_angle_arc_about_the_written_incremental_centre_posts_as_its_straight_move`.
  - `richauto_safety::an_arc_under_the_output_step_is_no_arc_block`.

Results on the final head `319fd13e197b6e47140ca4554d1f316577307a3c`, base `upstream/main` `3fc0e017b`:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: **818 of 819 steps passed, 1 failed; 48.7 minutes**. The failed step is `app suites: first_router_part` (`first_router_part_project_loads_verifies_and_posts_to_grblhal`). It is the base defect #3698. It fails on plain main. It posts through grblHAL and does not use this post.

- No UI change. Screenshots do not apply.

## Earlier author refresh (head `e276e3605`)

The refresh merges `upstream/main` at `35e3bd173d084c73c6fb3e6819a0247b7060dcb5`.
It keeps both RichAuto and Mach3 registry entries, embedded scripts, conformance cases and extensions.
It keeps the separate text-post and native-refusal counters and all comment assertions.

The first quick run passed 794 of 795 steps on the earlier merge head.
The only failure was `app suites: mcp_setup_moves`. Its isolated repeat passed 0 of 1 steps.
That test still expected name order after undo, although upstream now uses creation order.
This refresh also imports upstream commit `1c6002baa313f0f31643acca790ea281fe929406` through PR #3603.
The upstream test now captures the setup list before deletion and checks both undo operations against that list.
Final verification on the new merge head passes as recorded below.

- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings`: **passed: `cargo clippy -j24 -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` (1 minute 6 seconds)**.
- Catalog and reached golden suites: **All passed in the final quick gate: `example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work`, `conformance`, `recorded_streams`, `solid_law_goldens` and `slot_dxf_sketch`**.
- Pin proof: **The old slot golden, the omitted RichAuto registry entry and the text-post count changed from 22 to 21 each made its pin fail (RED, exit 101). Restoring each fix made its pin pass (GREEN, exit 0)**. The slot pin is `slot_dxf_sketch::a_slot_outline_seeds_the_slot_and_cuts_it_to_size`.
- Registry pin: `conformance::every_builtin_registry_entry_compiles`.

- Comment pin: `comment_escape::header_notes_use_each_shipped_dialect_and_keep_the_full_surface_bound`.
- No UI changes are in this fix round. Screenshots do not apply.

## Goldens moved

No existing PR golden changed relative to the current upstream base.
The refresh imports `crates/app/tests/golden/slot_dxf_outline.cl` from upstream.
That upstream fix generated the v2 record with 15 moves, replacing the stale v1 record with 9 moves.

title: fix(post): block cutting tools at reserved numbers and names
body:
## What changed

Machine files accept `tooling.reserved` entries.
Each entry reserves a number, a name, or both for `probe` or `tool_setter`.
The reader and validator refuse malformed entries by key.
Stored projects retain the reservations.

New cutting tools skip reserved numbers.
A probe takes a declared probe pocket.
Tool edits and library imports refuse incompatible reserved numbers or names.
Verification and posting also refuse old unsafe assignments.
The existing GUI, script, and MCP commands use these checks.
Tool number zero remains refused.

The standalone post CLI checks its input before it creates or replaces output.
It retains the loaded tool across sections.
A new TOOL needs its own declared kind.
A stream with no tool selector cannot post motion on a machine with reservations.
Indexed lookups keep the checks bounded for long streams.

A machine that omits the field reserves nothing.
No shipped machine file reserves a pocket in this PR (see "Review round 2").

### Project file version 78 (breaking)

A stored machine can hold `reserved_tools`. `PROJECT_VERSION` steps from 77 to 78.
An older reader refuses a v78 file. It cannot drop the reservation and post a cutting tool at a reserved pocket.
The step is a pure step-up: a v77 file opens with no change.
The rule entries are in `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` and `crates/app/src/project/apply.rs`.

PR #3485 merged first and took 77 for the setup `order` key (#3447). This PR takes 78.
Main's v77 meaning is unchanged.

This is a breaking change of the project file.
Commit `8f541fdc3` is `fix(project)!:` and has the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer.

## Cause

Tool allocation considered only document numbers.
Machine files could not protect a probe pocket or a control-managed tool name.
The app and standalone post paths had no reservation check.

## Review round 2 (second review of `e6881bb0a`)

- Blocker, version step: done (above).
- T99 provenance: removed. I found no public Tormach document that names T99 as the probe pocket.
  The earlier #362 research calls T99 a convention of the PathPilot probing screens only.
  The 18 Tormach files are identical to `main` again. A follow-up can add T99 with a cited document.
- `assets/machines/AGENTS.md`: the `tooling.reserved` row is added.
- MCP text: the `add_tool` description now says that the number skips the machine's reservations.
  It changes in `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs`, `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md`.
- Body: refreshed. Parent #3157 merged, so the stack note and the parent's screenshots are removed.

## Review round 3 (review of `3b5f359ff`)

- Version step: now 78. The constant, the rule entries, the pins, the fixture and the decision say 78.
- NEW blocker, breaking-change marker: commit `8f541fdc3` has the `BREAKING CHANGE:` footer. The history is kept.
- Conflict with `main`: I merged `upstream/main` at `f2b2369ed` with a merge commit (`23685c1c7`).
  - `crates/app/src/project/file.rs` and `apply.rs`: the two sides stay. Main's v77 entry comes first, then the v78 entry of this PR.
  - `crates/app/tests/deburr_chord_width.rs`: main's side is taken. It has the same intent as the earlier change of this PR.

## Screenshots

This PR changes no UI file. No screenshot applies.

## Tests on the final head

### Pins and mutation proof (rounds 2 and 3)

title: feat(multiaxis): Multi-Axis Deburr - tilted chamfer-mill edge breaks with holder tilt-away
body:
## Second-review fixes (current round)

Final head: `fdb1630fef05fb9b46d20a1673e5e8540ae69a12`. These fixes answer the review on head `ebe55a46f`.

1. **Posted golden and the two rotary laws.** New suite `crates/app/tests/mcp_multiaxis_deburr_post.rs`. It posts three sections on the tilt head with the Fanuc post: an upright Deburr, the Multi-Axis Deburr, and an upright Deburr after it.
   - `the_three_section_tilthead_program_matches_its_golden` locks the program in `golden/nc/multiaxis_deburr_tilthead.nc`: retract, turn, approach, cut, retract, return.
   - `the_tilted_section_states_its_rotary_pose_before_its_first_tilted_feed` pins #3421. A rapid states A and B before the first tilted feed. The stated pose is the pose of that feed. No feed turns a rotary on the way in.

## What changed

- A new operation kind, **Multi-Axis Deburr** (`OpType::MultiAxisDeburr`), is appended at ordinal 46 in `Section::MultiAxis`. Stored kind ids do not move.
- It has every field of the 3D Deburr and five more: `axis_mode` (`Axis5` / `Axis4`), `lead_deg`, `lag_deg`, `max_tilt_deg` and `shank_avoid`.
- New kernel `camcraft_motion::multiaxis::multiaxis_deburr` (`deburr_axis.rs`, `deburr_pose.rs`):
  - The tool lays one cone flank on the chamfer plane of each break. The cut is the flat chamfer for every pose that turns the axis about the plane normal.
  - `Axis5` leans the axis inside `max_tilt_deg`. `Axis4` keeps the axis square to the A axis (about X).
  - Mandatory continuous facet checks cover the full cone and the supplied physical shank and holder. They cover each complete cut, entry and exit. The stored `shank_avoid` option cannot disable this guard.
  - An edge with no clear pose follows the Deburr's unreachable-edge policy: skip with a note, or refuse by name.
  - The tool enters and leaves along a checked, bounded axis line. The entire cone stays above `bottom_z`. Pose changes, gaps and chamfer-plane corners split runs.
  - Each run declares a framed flat `EdgeBreak` cap (#1891).
- The exposed-edge scan moved from `finishing3d/deburr.rs` into the shared `finishing3d/deburr_scan.rs`. The 3D Deburr calls it in the same order.
- App wiring: kind row, seed, sanity door (lead minus lag inside the cap), generate arm, cache stamp, project DTO (`multi_axis_deburr`), heights, setup sheet, section mode, WCS refusals, sim break bound.
- MCP: `add_operation`, `edit_operation` and `set_operation_geometry` work with the new kind through the generic tools.
- UI: `multiaxis_deburr_page.rs` (Geometry: size, filters, unreachable policy; Passes: axis mode, lean, max tilt, shank avoid; Heights; Feeds). The kind has its own original glyph (`assets/ui/svg/op-multiaxis-deburr.svg`, PNG from `cargo xtask icons`).

## Safety review fixes on the new head

Final head: `a312b20ebdb48c2505ec417c6008d5cc1c6569d4`.

- Each candidate trims the edge until the tip and the lowest cone-rim point stay at or above `bottom_z` on every pass.

title: feat(wire): export a selected Agie opening for zero-step inspection
body:
The DXF import and Wire Contour selection prerequisites merged in #3193 and #3205. This PR adds the native zero-step inspection export.

The maintainer confirmed that the dependency and Agie-CAM reference approvals from #2951 also apply here. This PR gets its own safety review and trial-merge test after #2951 merges. [Maintainer decision](https://github.com/NeoTech/Camcraft/pull/3219#issuecomment-7080044891)

## Change

Use `camcraft-cli export-agie-inspection <project> <operation> <new-directory>` for a saved operation.

A user can create an unassigned wire inspection operation on the Post page and choose one placed, closed DXF chain and an internal start. The user can save the operation and export a native Classic Cut 2S ISO/SBR/SBL directory with zero working steps. The CLI and MCP use the same entry points.

The exporter preserves the nominal line and circular arc geometry. It checks the source selection, closure, winding, rounding, arc extrema, start disk and supported mounted machine axes. It refuses a changed or unsuitable selection and a destination that exists. An inspection work does not become a qualified machining operation.

This first setup uses 10 mm height, a 3 mm internal start and a 0.25 mm wire. The reference piece has unknown physical X/Y dimensions. Its controller fields store zero length and breadth. The receipt identifies the unverified fixture, erosion settings, physical Z and perpendicular controller lead. It describes the controller’s quality request separately from an assigned erosion process. The nominal setup does not promise a historical start seam, lead or cut sequence.

## Verification on head `e99d91acc` (merge of main `09ad779ee`)

Commit `1b607db49` merges main at `09ad779ee`. Three files needed a hand edit:

- `crates/app/src/commands/operation/create.rs`: main's `slot_gate` stays. This PR's `wire_gate` stays skipped for an inspection. Main added `sharp_corners` to `WireContourOp`; the inspection literal sets it to `false`.
- `crates/ui/src/browser_files.rs`: main's picker list stays (main removed `LoadMachineDialog` and `SelectPostDialog`). This PR adds `ImportAgieDrawing` and keeps `ExportAgieInspection` in the `NO_EXPORT` arm.
- `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md`: regenerated with `camcraft-cli mcp reference`.

Commit `e99d91acc` makes `agie_inspection::section` draw nothing when there is no setup and no Agie machine. Main's test `the_post_page_without_setups_has_no_extra_separator` failed without it.

After the merge, `git diff origin/main...HEAD -- crates/post/Cargo.toml` is empty. This PR adds no dependency.

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 1,178 steps. The only red steps were the ui lib separator test (fixed in `e99d91acc`) and clippy `needless_range_loop` at `crates/gpu/src/cut.rs:126`. That lint comes from the local Rust toolchain and is also on main.
- After `e99d91acc`: `ui suites: lib` passed. Strict Clippy (`-D warnings`) passed on geometry, cl, tools, post, sim, motion and app.
- The `example_catalog` suites passed in the quick plan.
- `cargo xtask gate light`: 4 steps, all ok.
- Heavy lanes: not run. This PR is P6, so it gets no heavy step.

## Verification on head `d982d452b`

Commit `d982d452b` merges upstream main at `4e0c81964` into the contributor branch. The only manual resolution was the generated MCP reference. The compiled registry and the published reference list the same 119 tools. A trial merge with main at `6308a5db5` completed without conflicts.

The targeted author check passed 104 tests on this head. These covered post (6), MCP (3), desktop (3), application regressions (74) and geometry (18). Strict all-target Clippy passed for the four touched crates. The complete quick selector listed 1,048 steps. The author ran the targeted quick alternative.

The refreshed CLI imported an unchanged drawing, reopened the saved operations and exported two native jobs. All six files matched the controller-checked files byte for byte. Each receipt reported zero working steps. Repeat exports refused to overwrite either job.

The official heavy gate passed all 254 selected steps in 62.7 minutes on this revision. The command exited with status 0.

```sh
cargo xtask gate heavy --base 4e0c81964
```

## Earlier verification on `d13c5eed1`

Contributor head: `d13c5eed15251af0a903396c1d96bba298b644d0`. Parent: `2d0fa64841a1b42dbacb330f75f6bab61897da10`.

All eight scoped tests passed on this earlier head: two post tests, three MCP tests and three desktop tests. Strict all-target Clippy passed for geometry, post, app and UI. The independent synthetic export preserved every directed edge, arc center and resource link. It wrote one start, one work and zero steps. The checks include:

- `agie_inspection_accepts_listed_chain_and_checks_mounted_travel_in_the_wcs`
- `saved_selected_opening_exports_zero_steps_through_the_desktop_action`
- `unassigned_inspection_opening_survives_undo_redo_and_project_reopen`
- `setup_post_inspection_fields_and_submit_fit_the_visible_panel`

On this earlier revision, 252 of 253 heavy steps passed. The bulk release build failed to link two test binaries when the device ran out of space. The refreshed revision has its own gate run.

The desktop authoring and selection use a real undoable operation. The documented MCP reference was regenerated from the compiled CLI. The public selection returned by `list_features` can be passed directly to `create_agie_inspection`. A regression narrows the mount travel and reverses an axis. Each case refuses before file creation.

We used an offline VM running a copy of the actual Agie Classic Cut 2S control. The control opened native files produced by CAMCraft. We checked the program and ISO identities, nominal orientation, hole size and position, setup height, zero separation and zero working steps. Each work-level formal check blocked on undefined working technology. Each whole-piece check also flagged the low zero X/Y dimensions. Both control previews rendered the bound nominal profiles. An identical repeat import with the quality already present kept zero assigned working steps. Repeating an export to the same directory preserved the old files. No physical cut was made.

No model data, original job or simulator software is included. The public geometry tests are original synthetic cases. This inspection slice does not qualify a working erosion process, a physical slug restraint or an automatic cutting release. #3178 remains open for qualified curved die cutting. #3179 retains its physical process requirements.

## Desktop comparison

Both images use the same synthetic project and 750 by 830 pixel setup panel. The parent has the existing post controls. The new form shows the selected opening, wire and both start coordinates.

| Parent | This change |
| --- | --- |
| ![Parent setup Post panel](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/69865cfd9c4856f159fd63c5ba79b7b08724e264/issue-3179/setup-before.png) | ![Setup Post panel with the Agie inspection form](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/qsmits/Camcraft/69865cfd9c4856f159fd63c5ba79b7b08724e264/issue-3179/setup-after.png) |

Effort: high. No escalation.

Changelog: Export a selected closed DXF opening as a native, zero-step Classic Cut 2S inspection setup from desktop, CLI or MCP.

Refs #3178

title: feat(import): state the STEP length unit, and ask for it when the file has none
body: ## What changed A STEP model import states the length unit that the model was read in. A STEP file that states no length unit is never read in a guessed unit. - **Kernel** (`crates/kernel/src/step_assumed_unit.rs`, `solidcore_step.rs`, `solidcore_step_import.rs`): `read_step_assuming` and `import_step_model_assuming` take the caller's millimetres per unit. For a file whose contexts state no length unit, the unit is written into each representation context before the read. The tolerance, the edge-gap cap and the chord are then in the same unit as the geometry. A file that states its own unit keeps it. A stated size outside 0.001..=1000 mm is refused by name. - **Geometry** (`crates/geometry/src/step.rs`): `parse_open_assuming`. A file with no length unit and no caller unit is `StepError::MissingUnits`. `StepMesh` carries `length_units_mm` and `assumed_mm`. - **App**: - `ImportError::StepUnitsMissing`. - `ImportModel::within_in` and `from_bytes_in`, and the unit option on each import path: the file, the bytes, the sourced load and the cadmpeg conversion. - A unit for a file that is not STEP is refused by name before parsing, as a facet budget is. - The last import note names the unit: `length unit: in (stated by the file)`, `length unit: in (stated at import; the file states no length unit)`, or `... (stated by the file; the in stated at import is not used)`. - **MCP and script**: `import_model` takes `units` (`"mm"` or `"in"`). `cam.import` takes it as the fourth argument. `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` and `assets/scripts/cam.d.ts` are regenerated. - **UI**: a refused unitless import opens the **Length unit** modal (`egui_app/step_units_prompt.rs`), with the buttons Millimeters (mm), Inches (in) and Cancel. The answer goes through the command queue (`CommandKind::ResolveStepUnits`) and runs the same import again. The import that lands is one undoable command. Cancel and Escape import nothing. An import-as-fixture binding is kept for the second import. - **Docs**: `units-and-coordinates.md` (it said that a unitless STEP file "is kept as millimetres") and a new `troubleshooting.md` entry. The decision record is `docs/decisions/1874-step-length-units.md`. ## Screenshot The Length unit prompt for a STEP file that states no length unit (the status line under it says the same): ## Decisions (see the decision record) - The file's own unit wins over the caller's (the DXF import does the reverse, #1862). A STEP unit context is an exact statement of the CAD system. - The chosen unit is not recorded on the model. A linked-file re-import asks again. - Tool holders, fixtures and tool bodies from a unitless STEP file are refused by name, with no prompt. ## Pinning tests - `camcraft-kernel` `step_assumed_unit` (3): a unitless box reads 25.4² times the area in inches; the file's own unit wins; an out-of-range unit is refused by name. - `camcraft-app` `step_units_import` (5): the typed refusal; the inch and mm imports and their notes; the file's mm, in and m notes; a unit for an STL is refused; MCP `import_model` with no unit, a bad unit and `in`. - `camcraft-ui` lib `step_units_tests` (5): the question, the answer as one undoable import (inch is 25.4 times the mm width), Cancel, and no question for a file that states its unit. - `camcraft-ui` lib `egui_app::tests::step_units_prompt` (4): the labels, no prompt without a question, a unit button, Cancel and Escape. - Updated, because each STEP import now ends with the unit note: `import_step_outward` (3 tests) and `import_step_closed_shell` `a_flipped_face_is_named_in_the_import_result_and_the_mcp_answer`. They assert the unit note in place of "no notes". No assertion is weaker. ## Gates Final head b5637db2b (the review fixes on 2649bb17e), Windows x86_64, without sccache: - Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 1033 steps, 1032 ok. The one red step is `ai_guide_calls_match_live_tools_list`, the CRLF defect #3119, which this PR does not touch. - `cargo clippy -p camcraft-kernel -p camcraft-geometry -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean (kernel and geometry on 2649bb17e; they did not change after it). - Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): `kernel heavy` (17 steps), `motion heavy` (37 steps) and `app heavy` (198 steps), after one release build. 253 steps ok, 0 failed, 26.1 min. The known-fail steps of #1950 and #2849 are red as expected. (The run on 2649bb17e also had 253 steps ok.) - Note: with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=sccache`, two gate runs here failed with "can't find crate" (`num_enum`, then `flecs_ecs`) and the warning `ignoring -C extra-filename flag due to -o flag`. The runs without sccache are correct. This is a local cache matter, not this change. ## Review fixes (b5637db2b) - `crates/app/tests/cadmpeg_import.rs`: the eight `load_open_within` calls in the `#[cfg(unix)]` module pass `None` for the new `units` argument. This module does not compile on Windows, so it is not in the Windows gates above. It needs a build on Linux or macOS. - `State::take_step_units`: each import start takes the chosen unit, whatever its file. A unit never waits for a later import of the same file. Pinned by `step_units_tests::a_chosen_unit_never_waits_for_a_later_import_of_the_same_file`. - `troubleshooting.md`: the answer is not kept; the next import, a linked file's re-import included, asks again. ## Not exercised - A unitless file from the cadmpeg converter was not tried. That path uses the same `parse_model_open_in`. - `crates/app/src/mcp/tools.rs` and `crates/app/src/script/api.rs` were already over 400 lines. They grow by 2 and 7 lines. Changelog: A STEP import states the model's length unit, and a STEP file that states no unit is no longer read as millimetres: the desktop app asks for mm or inches, and MCP and scripts take `units` (#1874) Fixes #1874 🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)

title: Publish SHA256SUMS.txt with every release
body:
## What

The release workflow's `publish` job now writes a `SHA256SUMS.txt` covering every release asset and uploads it with the other files.

- A new step runs `sha256sum` in `dist/` over the same file patterns the job already publishes (zip, setup.exe, tar.gz, deb, rpm, dmg, AppImage, snap, flatpak, pkg.tar.zst), checks the result with `sha256sum -c`, and prints it to the log.
- `dist/SHA256SUMS.txt` is added to the `softprops/action-gh-release` file list.

The file uses standard `sha256sum` format (`<hash>  <filename>`), so users can verify a download with:

```
sha256sum -c --ignore-missing SHA256SUMS.txt
```

## Why

I've asked for CamCraft to be added to ArtCraft Launcher as a community app (storytold/craft-launcher#1545). The launcher checks every download, including downloads of community apps, against the release's `SHA256SUMS.txt`, so CamCraft can't be listed until its releases include one. Checksums also help anyone who downloads the files by hand.

Releases that are already published don't change. The file will appear starting with the next tag.

## Testing

- The YAML parses.
- I ran the step's script on sample files: it lists each asset once, `sha256sum -c` passes, and `release-body.md` isn't included.
- I haven't run it in a real release. That will happen on the next tag.

title: feat(motion): Bore gets a Helical strategy (one helix to the floor, then a floor circle)
body:
## What changed

- New `BoreStrategy` (`crates/motion/src/machining2d/bore_helix.rs`): `Rings` (the level ladder, the default and every earlier bore) or `Helical { spring_pass }`. `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` get the field `strategy`.
- A helical hole has these moves:
  1. A rapid over the helix start at the clearance height.
  2. A rapid down to the plunge height over the material.
  3. One continuous helix on the wall radius (`rc = R - r - leave`, the same circle as the last ring) to the floor.
  4. One flat floor circle. With `spring_pass`, a second floor circle.
  5. A feed to the centre at the floor, then a rapid up to clearance.
  
  A through hole's helix ends at the floor less the break-through. The helix is arcs of at most half a turn, so each arc posts as one G2/G3 with Z.
- The pitch is `stepdown`. The Heights tab calls it "Helix pitch" for a helical Bore. Climb is CCW, as for the rings.
- Two refusals in `BoreParams::validate`, before any move is built:
  - A hole that one helix cannot clear to the centre (`rc > floor reach`). For a flat end mill, the limit is twice the tool diameter. The message gives the core and the widest hole.
  - A helix steeper than 15 deg. The message gives the largest pitch that fits.
- Detect holes (`crates/app/src/operation/bore_reach.rs`) skips, and names, the holes that one helix cannot clear when the Bore is helical.
- Project file: `helical` and `spring_pass` on the `bore` record, written only when true. A ring ladder writes the same JSON as before. No version step (see the decision file).
- Stamp: the digest writes the strategy only for a helical Bore. A ring ladder keeps the stamp that it had.
- MCP: `list_operation_types` lists `helical` and `spring_pass` for `bore`. A params patch sets them.
- UI (`crates/ui/src/egui_app/holes_page.rs`): a Strategy combo and a Spring pass check on the Passes tab, the "Helix pitch" label on the Heights tab, and a Lead-in hint that the level links do not apply.
- Guide: a "Helical strategy" part in the Bore section of `site/content/guide/operations/operations-2d.md`, and two rows in `site/content/guide/reference/refusals.md`.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/2830-helical-bore.md`.
- Mechanical: each `BoreParams` and `OpParams::Bore` literal in the tests gets `strategy: Default::default()` (the ring ladder).

## Readings

The issue's counterbore, posted with `assets/posts/linuxcnc.cps`. The model is a revolved block with a Ø11 x 7 recess at the origin (top Z0). The tool is EM-0600-4FL (Ø6 flat), with a 1 mm pitch, climb, clearance 10 and retract 5. A scratch test built the document with the commands, then called `posting::post_script`. It is not committed. The status is Ok and the post has no warning. The cutting part of the program:

```
G0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10
G0 X2.5 Y0 Z2
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z0 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-0.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-1 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-1.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-2 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-2.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-3 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-3.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-4 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-4.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-5 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-5.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-6 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-6.5 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G3 X-2.5 Y0 Z-7 I-2.5 J0 F600
G3 X2.5 Y0 Z-7 I2.5 J0 F600
G1 X0 Y0 Z-7 F600
G0 X0 Y0 Z10
```

- The helix starts at the plunge height (Z2) and drops 0.5 mm in each half turn to Z-7. There is no straight plunge.
- The two flat arcs at Z-7 are the floor circle. The G1 goes off the wall to the centre before the retract.
- The same document with the Rings strategy also posts with no warning (95 lines; a G1 plunge at the centre for each of the 7 levels).
- The first `G0 X2.5 Y0` line comes before the `G0 X2.5 Y0 Z10` line: the post writes its approach first. The Rings program has the same pattern.

## Pinning tests

- `bore_helix` (motion, new):
  - `the_counterbore_is_one_helix_on_the_wall_then_a_floor_circle_and_never_a_plunge`: the issue's Ø11 x 7 counterbore with a Ø6 flat end mill at 1 mm per turn. No axial feed, no `Plunge` move, the arcs on `rc`, nine turns from 2 mm over the top to the floor, one floor circle, a feed to the centre, a retract.
  - `the_spring_pass_is_a_second_floor_circle`, `conventional_milling_turns_the_helix_clockwise`, `a_through_hole_helix_runs_on_by_the_break_through`.
  - `a_hole_one_helix_cannot_clear_is_refused_with_the_widest_it_can` (Ø12 passes, Ø14 is refused with "2.000 mm core" and "12.000 mm").
  - `a_helix_steeper_than_the_limit_is_refused_with_the_pitch_that_fits` (Ø6.5: 32.5 deg; the given pitch then passes).
  - `the_rings_strategy_is_the_default_and_keeps_its_centre_dive`.
- `bore_helical` (app, new):
  - `the_issue_counterbore_is_one_helix_and_never_plunges_into_the_block`: through `operation::generate`, with a centre-cutting and a non-centre-cutting tool. `first_solid_plunge` finds no plunge, the verifier gives no warning, 18 half-turn arcs, the floor reached. The ring ladder still dives.
  - `a_hole_too_wide_for_one_helix_is_refused_through_the_operation`.
  - `the_strategy_rides_the_project_file_and_an_older_file_reads_rings`.
  - `the_stamp_moves_when_the_strategy_changes`.
- `operation::bore_reach::tests::detect_for_a_helical_bore_skips_the_holes_one_helix_cannot_clear` (app lib).
- `egui_app::tests::bore_strategy` (ui lib, new): the Strategy row defaults to Rings, Helical shows the Spring pass check, and the Heights tab names the pitch.

## Gates

All gates ran on the final head 4bd091166. This head merges `upstream/main` at 2d98d87be and adds the `strategy` field to main's new Bore literal in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`.

- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`): 724 steps, 0 failed (113.0 min). It includes `motion suites: bore_helix`, `motion suites: equal_steps` and `app suites: bore_helical`.
- `cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings` on `camcraft-geometry`, `camcraft-cl`, `camcraft-tools`, `camcraft-post`, `camcraft-sim`, `camcraft-motion`, `camcraft-app` and `camcraft-ui`: clean.
- Heavy lanes (`cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main`): 240 steps (202 app heavy, 37 motion heavy, 1 build), 0 failed (63.8 min). The 6 known-fail steps (#1950, #2849) are red as expected.
- The earlier head c70e84309 had a quick gate of 687 steps and a heavy run of 231 steps, all green.

## Screenshots

The Bore operation page, rendered by the UI test harness (`egui_kittest`) from a real Bore operation.

| | Rings | Helical |
|---|---|---|
| Passes tab | ![Passes, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-rings.png) | ![Passes, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/passes-helical.png) |
| Heights tab | ![Heights, Rings](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-rings.png) | ![Heights, Helical](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/sn3ro/Camcraft/pr-screenshots/3103/heights-helical.png) |

- Passes tab: the Strategy combo shows the two strategies. The Spring pass check shows only for Helical.
- Heights tab: the last Levels row is "Stepdown" for Rings and "Helix pitch" for Helical.

## Not exercised

- No air cut on a machine. The reporter offered in the issue to test the counterbore case.
- No GUI check by hand. The UI tests assert the rows and the combo value.
- The Bore seed stepdown is the carried stepdown (often 5 mm). A Ø11 hole with a Ø6 tool at 5 mm per turn is 17.7 deg and is refused, with the pitch to type (4.2 mm). The page does not change the stepdown when the strategy changes.
- The helix does not read the Lead-in radial engagement limit or the lead feed percentage. It reads the plunge height, the stock top and the ramp feed.
- A hole wider than twice the tool diameter is refused for the helix. The issue permits a refusal. An inner helix followed by rings is not in this PR.
- A non-centre-cutting tool helixes like any other tool. The 15 deg limit keeps the descent shallow. No tool record has a ramp limit to read.

Changelog: The Bore operation has a Helical strategy: one continuous helix on the wall radius to the floor, one floor circle, an optional spring pass, then a move to the centre. It cuts a counterbore or a hole up to twice the tool diameter without a plunge.

Branch made from `upstream/main` at 2b95e5701. `upstream/main` merged in at 2d98d87be.

Fixes #2830

title: feat(2d): import SVG drawings as 2D sketch profiles
body:
## What changed

The SVG reader, `camcraft_geometry::svg`, reads drawings into the DXF `Document` type. It shares sketch chaining, nesting, `SketchData`, sketch entities, and project storage with DXF import.

- Read paths, lines, polylines, polygons, rectangles, circles, and ellipses.
- Apply group transforms and references to elements in the same file.
- Keep circular arcs analytic. Flatten Beziers and other ellipses within 0.005 mm.
- Read mm, cm, in, pt, pc, and px sizes, `viewBox`, and `preserveAspectRatio`.
- Reflect Y about the page height. Use top-level group labels or IDs as layers.
- Count unsupported content, hidden content, markers and paint-only stylesheets as skipped. This includes stylesheets inside `<defs>`.
- Add the undoable `ImportSvg` command, the `import_svg` MCP tool, and the `cam.importSvg` script verb.
- Update the user guide and MCP reference. Record decisions in `docs/decisions/1880-svg-import.md`.

## Refusals

The reader names malformed input, unsupported units, invalid sizes, singular transforms, and exceeded import limits. A file without physical units needs the caller's unit. A sized file refuses a caller unit.

The reader also refuses root `<svg>` transform attributes, and `transform-origin` and `transform-box` presentation attributes.

The reader finds a duplicate attribute name with a map. The scan that it replaces was quadratic in the attribute count of one tag.

The reader reads an inline `style` against an allow-list of the properties that cannot change geometry (`SAFE_PROPERTIES` in `svg/facts.rs`). The reader refuses each other property by name. The reader reads the style and the transform of an element one time, finds a `use` target in a map of the ids, and charges the shape data of each visit against a work budget.

The latest review fix (the delta safety read on `eaafd2e72`) closes the class "an input changes or hides a shape, and the import ignores it":

- A `<style>` sheet is checked with the same allow-list, with no selector matching (`svg/sheet.rs`). The reader refuses `display`, `visibility` and each property that is not on the list. A paint-only sheet imports.
- The reader refuses an `<?xml-stylesheet?>` instruction and a `<link rel="stylesheet">` by name.
- The reader refuses `animate`, `set`, `animateTransform`, `animateMotion`, `animateColor` and `discard` at each place in the tree.
- A child of a shape or of a `use` that is not `title`, `desc`, `metadata` or `style` is counted as `<child> in <parent>`.
- The reader refuses a reference to a DOCTYPE entity in content and in an attribute value. A namespace declaration is the exception.
- The reader refuses a `preserveAspectRatio` value that is not in the SVG grammar.
- A marker property that draws a marker is counted as `marker`.
- The user guide says that a shape with a stroke imports as its centre line.

## Validation on the final head

Head: `f96ea8fa0729e6432459182e45a60b7c4a096772`. It is a merge of `upstream/main` `d54580caddb37ab2a63044507577c506514ffa64` into the reviewed code head `671426992`.
The gates ran on this head with `--base upstream/main` at `d54580cad`.

| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` | PASS: 1,186 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 18.1 minutes |
| `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` | PASS: 95 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 24.0 minutes |
| `clippy -D warnings` | PASS: a step of the quick gate |
| `app suites: example_catalog`, `example_catalog_adaptive`, `example_catalog_edge_work` | PASS in the quick gate |
| `app suites: first_router_part`, `mcp_svg` | PASS in the quick gate |
| geometry `svg`, `svg_refusals`, `svg_style_safety`, `svg_tree_rules`, `svg_visibility` | 16 / 19 / 6 / 9 / 11 passed |

**Merge of main.** The merge had one conflict, in `docs/agents/mcp-tools.md` (a generated file: the tool count).
I wrote the file again with `cargo run -p camcraft-app --bin camcraft-cli -- mcp reference`. It differs from the file of main only in the count (121 tools) and the `import_svg` row.
The merge has no other hand edit. No source file had a conflict.
Main moved to `37aca7f8c` (#3620, the verifier island slices in `sim`) during the heavy run. `git merge-tree` of this head with that main is clean. The gates did not run against that main.
The heavy plan has 95 steps on this base. It had 255 steps on the base `2de071415`. I did not examine the cause of the difference.

Pin proof (`crates/geometry/tests/svg_tree_rules.rs`, 9 tests). For each row, the mutation was made, the binary ran, and the code was restored. With the code restored, all 9 tests pass in 0.2 s.

| Mutation | Red pin |
|---|---|
| The sheet is not checked | `svg_style_sheet_rules_that_hide_or_resize_a_shape_are_refused_by_name` |
| `display` and `visibility` in a sheet are accepted | the same test |
| A `;` outside a rule is skipped | the same test |
| A rule inside a rule is not refused | the same test |
| The text of a CDATA section in `<style>` is dropped | the same test |
| An `xml-stylesheet` instruction is skipped | `svg_external_style_sheets_are_refused_by_name` |
| A `<link rel="stylesheet">` is not refused | the same test |
| The animation list is not used | `svg_animation_elements_are_refused_by_name_at_each_place` |
| The children of a shape are not counted | `svg_elements_below_a_shape_or_a_use_are_counted_by_name` |
| The scan of the children charges no work | `svg_children_of_a_reused_shape_are_charged_against_the_work_budget` |
| The entity check is off | `svg_doctype_entity_references_are_refused_by_name` |
| An unknown alignment is xMin/yMin | `svg_preserve_aspect_ratio_places_the_view_box_and_refuses_an_unknown_value` |
| An unknown meet-or-slice word is `meet` | the same test |
| A marker attribute or inline declaration is not counted | `svg_marker_shapes_are_counted_as_skipped` |
| A marker in a sheet is not counted | `svg_paint_only_style_sheets_import_at_the_attribute_size` |

`svg_paint_only_style_sheets_import_at_the_attribute_size` pins that a usual paint sheet (`.cls-1{fill:none;stroke:#000}`, `@font-face`, `@charset`) still imports.
One existing test changed: `svg_stylesheets_inside_defs_and_tree_are_counted_as_skipped` had the sheet `.h{display:none}`. The reader now refuses that sheet, so the test uses a paint rule.

The pins of the earlier rounds are in `svg_style_safety.rs`, `svg_refusals.rs` and `svg_visibility.rs`. They passed in the quick gate.

## Goldens moved

None. The catalog suites ran and passed on the final head. The diff against `upstream/main` changes no recorded program, golden or snapshot PNG.

## Not exercised

- A posted G-code golden for an SVG profile remains in follow-up #3042. This fix round did not exercise it.
- The `import_svg` row in `.claude/skills/camcraft-mcp/SKILL.md` remains outside this fix round.
- Nested SVG viewports, selector matching of a style sheet, text to outlines, and embedded images remain outside this reader's scope.
- The merge with main `37aca7f8c` is not built and not gated. The gated base is `d54580cad`.
- The mutations of the pin table were not run again on the merge head. The merge changes no SVG source file and no SVG test.
- The description of the `import_svg` MCP tool is not changed.
- The four follow-ups of the first review on `eaafd2e72` (Inkscape long style, `vector-effect` attribute, the 5 s time limits, the skill row) are not changed.

No UI source changed. Before/after screenshots do not apply.

Changelog: Import SVG drawings (paths, shapes, group transforms, mm/cm/in/pt/pc/px sizes) as 2D profiles on the stock, with the `import_svg` MCP tool and `cam.importSvg`; an SVG with no physical size is refused until you state its unit.

Effort: high

Fixes #1880

body:

Final head: `fd9e31b9fd6d46be6b31acb6447d98c771b67978`.
The fix commit is `c6a612de3`. The head also merges upstream main `ddc4d8274` (two merges of main, no conflict, no hand edit).

This update fixes the two findings of the review of `9d5db9bec`.

1. The combined tree compiles again. `reservations::check_stream` (main's #3284) now has the two new records.
   - `Record::Jet(_)` is in the arm that has `Record::Torch(_)`. A jet is cutting: it needs a stated TOOL, and it obeys a reserved pocket.
   - `Record::Waterjet(_)` is in the arm that has `Record::Plasma(_)`. The header is no motion.

   - The reviewer's stream now posts `G1 X59.5 Y30 F300` then `G1 X70 Y30`, with no `G3` block and no warning.
   - Pins:
     - `every_post_writes_no_coincident_arc_block_and_keeps_its_real_arcs` (`coincident_arcs.rs`): `waterjet-iso` is in the `POSTS` table, with a flat witness that has the `WATERJET` header and a `JET ON` span.
     - `waterjet_post_writes_no_full_circle_for_an_arc_under_the_output_step` (`waterjet_iso_post.rs`): the reviewer's stream, mm and inch.
     - `waterjet_post_writes_a_same_angle_arc_as_its_straight_move` (`waterjet_iso_post.rs`): the #3474 witnesses and the #3500 offset-centre witnesses, mm and inch, and one normal quarter arc that stays `G3 X10 Y15 I-10 J0`.

| `Record::Jet(_)` moved to the no-motion arm | RED: `a_waterjet_stream_obeys_the_reserved_pockets` fails |

| Check | Result |

## Review fixes and final-head validation

Head of that round: `e302dc0f000ecde4f2a52ddb63fb9879b6004f5a`.

This update fixes the three findings of the review of `05243edc5`.

1. A section with no `WATERJET` header after a waterjet section is refused by name.
   - The engine now sets the section's current properties before `onSection`. The hook no longer reads a header that the previous `ENDSECTION` cleared.
   - The post refuses a jet word or a cut with no header in `jetOk` (new `headerOk`). It never drops the motion without a warning.
   - Pin: `waterjet_post_refuses_an_adjacent_section_with_no_header` (the review's input). The test checks the named refusal, the first section's `G1 X1 Y0 F300`, one nozzle comment and one `G54`.
2. Merge of upstream main `35940da16`. Conflicts resolved:
   - `engine.rs`: main's upright-after-tilt refusal and `machine::flatten` stay. `programBounds` is published after `set_machine`.

3. Quick gate on the final combined head: GREEN (below).

Mutation checks on pin 1:

- Engine refresh removed: RED (two nozzle comments).
- Engine refresh and post `headerOk` guard both removed: RED (no warning, the review's silent output).
- Both restored: GREEN.
- The post guard alone is a second guard. With the engine refresh in place, `startPreamble` refuses first, so the pin cannot isolate the post guard.

Final-head results:

- `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main`: GREEN. 1,131 steps, 0 failed, 0 stalled, 20.4 minutes.
- Clippy (gate step, `-p` all nine selected crates, `--all-targets -- -D warnings`): GREEN.
- `adaptive_troch_parallel`: passed in 16 s in the gate. The earlier 90 s timing failure did not repeat.
- `comment_escape`, `waterjet_engine`, `waterjet_iso_post`, `script_waterjet_iso`: pass on the merged tree.
