The PR remains a draft. No screenshots, logs, or review evidence are committed.

The sections below describe the original implementation and its historical validation. Their test counts and gate results are historical.

## What changed

- The post engine reads a `lineEnding` manifest entry. The value `"lf"` is the default. The value `"crlf"` ends each line with `\r\n`. The engine refuses any other value by name. The engine reads the entry after `onClose`, so `onOpen` can set it from a declared option.
- `machine.travel` gives the stated linear strokes `{X, Y, Z}` to scripts. Each value is `[min, max]` in mm, or `null`. The mirror now carries the `travel` of a linear axis. The raw door reads a vendor tree through `parse_mch`.
- The engine publishes `programBounds` before `onOpen`. It is the XY box of the cutting records, or `null`. Arcs count at the quarter points that they pass (`machine::move_extremes`). Rapids do not count.
- New stream records `WATERJET [ABRASIVE] [DWELL<ms>] [LAG<ms>]` and `JET ON C<id> <ROLE>` / `JET OFF C<id>`. The cl types are `cl::WaterjetCut` and `cl::JetSpan` (`crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs`). The reader takes the `.cnc` form and the `.cl` comment form.
- The new hooks `onJetOn` / `onJetOff` fire under a `JetLaw` (`cnc_jet.rs`). The law refuses by name: a jet with no header, an ON while a jet is on, a rapid while a jet is on, and a jet that stays on. It shares no state with the plasma `TorchLaw`.
- `linearizeArcs = true` posts each arc as chords through `onLinear`, at `chordTolerance` mm (0.01 when unstated). The engine refuses a bad tolerance by name. The chords come from `cl::Move::segments3`. The last chord ends on the arc's end point. All chord lines map to the arc record.
- A WCS flip on a waterjet section is refused by name, the same as for plasma.
- New post `assets/posts/waterjet-iso.cps` (generic ISO abrasive waterjet). It writes `G20`/`G21`, `G90 G94 G17 G40`, a work offset, and `G0`/`G1`/`G2`/`G3` (or G1 chords). It writes XY only. Each contour gets: water on, `G4` valve lag, abrasive on, `G4` pierce dwell, the cut, abrasive off, water off. The four M numbers, the G4 word form, the arc form and the line ending are declared options. The default M numbers (M10/M11, M12/M13) are placeholders, and the post header says so.
- The post refuses by name: an rpm (S, G95), a surface speed (G96), coolant, a section with no `WATERJET` header, a machine not declared `kind: waterjet`, a rotary, a cycle, a Z cutting move, and a cut outside the stated `machine.travel`.
- Docs: `docs/CNC-INTERMEDIATE.md` (records, properties, "Waterjet records") and `assets/posts/AGENTS.md` (hooks, sheet-cutting seams, the waterjet post).
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1882-waterjet-post.md`.

## Cause

This is new work for #1882. The engine wrote only `\n` lines. It did not publish linear travel or a cut box. It had no waterjet records or jet hooks, and no waterjet post was available.

## Tests

Pins (all red on the upstream sources, 17 of 17):

- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_engine.rs` (12 tests): `line_ending_crlf_ends_every_line_with_cr_lf`, `line_ending_other_words_are_refused_by_name`, `program_bounds_box_the_cut_moves_and_skip_rapids`, `machine_travel_publishes_the_linear_strokes`, `machine_travel_rides_the_mirror_and_the_raw_file`, `linearize_arcs_posts_chords_ending_on_the_arc_end`, `linearize_arcs_refuses_a_bad_tolerance_by_name`, `waterjet_records_fire_the_jet_hooks_with_their_properties`, `waterjet_records_round_trip_in_both_spellings`, `waterjet_law_refuses_what_the_stream_cannot_mean`, `waterjet_header_and_open_jet_end_with_their_section`, `waterjet_section_under_a_flipped_wcs_is_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/post/tests/waterjet_iso_post.rs` (7 tests): the goldens `plate.nc` (mm, G2/G3) and `plate_inch_chords.nc` (inch, G1 chords, CR LF, `G4 P` ms, custom M numbers), and the refusals for spindle words, a section that is not a waterjet cut, a machine that is not a waterjet, travel, a Z cut, a dry cut and a cycle.
- `crates/post/tests/script_waterjet_iso.rs`: the recorded-stream suite (11 refusal goldens; no recorded stream is a waterjet cut).
- `crates/cl/src/cl/jet.rs` unit tests: line round trip, bad words, span sanity.

Mutation checks (one guard changed, its pin run, the guard put back): 21 of 21 red. The guards: the CR LF join, the `lineEnding` refusal, the bounds publish, the rapid skip, the arc quarter points, the travel in props, the travel in the mirror, the chord branch, the tolerance check, the jet-hook check, the jet rapid law, the jet section end, the jet fire, the WCS-flip refusal, the post rpm, CSS, header, kind, travel and Z refusals, and the order abrasive off before water off.

Gate: `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` is green: 996 steps, 0 failed (wall 30.5 min; the `cl` change reaches each dependent crate). `cargo clippy -p camcraft-cl -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean.

Branch history: the first commit was squashed onto a newer main by mistake, so it reverted nine files of the Tormach lathe G76 work (#2952). The second commit restores them from main. The net diff against main has only the #1882 files (34 files). The four new Tormach lathe test binaries pass on the combined tree. The quick gate ran on the base `768fe23f0`, before that main change; main's change since then touches none of the files of this PR.

## Goldens moved

None. All goldens are new: `crates/post/tests/golden/waterjet/plate.nc`, `plate_inch_chords.nc` and the input `plate.cnc`, plus `crates/post/tests/recorded/golden/waterjet-iso/*.refusal`. No existing `.nc` or `.cl` golden changed.

## Not exercised

- No generator writes the waterjet records yet. The `Toolpath::waterjet` field and its `.cl` dump come with the WaterjetProfile operation (#1883). The input stream here is written by hand.
- The post is not in `posting::BUILTINS`, so the app does not offer it yet (see the decision record). A user can post with it as a file of their own (`serves = ["waterjet"]`).

title: feat(wire): support checked reentrant punch contours in native wire EDM jobs
body:
Stacked on #2964. Review the reentrant punch changes above the parent head `4a94c23ce`.

## What changed

This PR replaces the convex-only refusal of #2955 with checked reentrant corners. The work is ported onto the zero-step setup writer of #2984 and the measured stock heights of #2964. The old setup writer of this branch is not used.

- `crates/geometry/src/geometry/prism.rs`: `closed_vertical_prism` returns the footprint of a full-height vertical extrusion. The union of the top cap triangles must equal the union of the bottom cap triangles. The cap triangles must not overlap. Each side facet must lie on an oriented boundary face. The mesh must be one closed solid. The function examines each facet, also internal surfaces that slices do not find.
- `crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`: the job takes its contour from the verified cap footprint, not from a union of slices. A union of slices can add rounded vertices along a sloping face.
- `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs`: a reentrant corner is permitted when the rough offset of the selected stock thickness reaches the nominal vertex within 0.002 mm. The offset comes from `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`.
- `crates/post/src/agie/spacing.rs` (new): when the contour has a reentrant corner, each profile segment must hold both corner joins. Each pair of nonadjacent segments must keep the swept rough pass apart. The check uses the longest miter plus a full rough offset.
- The entry stays on a supporting exterior face. The ISO object keeps the nominal vertices. The SBL is the zero-step setup of main, with `ID_PUNCH c_punch` and the 1.0 mm separation.
- Refusal texts name the native wire EDM job (#3537).
- `examples/agie/notched-punch.*`: an original 40 × 20 mm punch with a 20 mm wide, 1 mm deep V notch.
- User guide and `docs/decisions/2956-agie-reentrant-punch.md`.

These readings are from the offline control on the old branch head `6201b325c`, before the port. That head wrote erosion steps in its own SBL.

- The control plotted all seven faces of the notched punch through the rough cut and three trims.
- Measured wire offsets were 0.245, 0.155, 0.140 and 0.134 mm.

- The plot kept the 1 mm separation and returned to the threading hole.
- The formal check of the control had zero job errors.

After the port, the notched job has the same SBL as the rectangular `CCSEP20` golden job on the same stock and start hole. Only the ISO object changes.

title: feat(post): support measured Agie QN2 stock heights
body:
Stacked on #2955. Review the [height changes above the parent](https://github.com/qsmits/Camcraft/compare/9787bf79e...4a94c23ce).

The native wire EDM job files post accepts a QN2 stock thickness of 15, 20, 40 or 80 mm. Before this change, it accepted only 20 mm. Each thickness has its own measured rough offset. The corner and face clearance checks use the offset of the selected thickness. Other thicknesses are refused.

| Stock thickness (mm) | Rough (mm) | Trim 1 (mm) | Trim 2 (mm) | Trim 3 (mm) |
| ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: | ---: |
| 15 | 0.245 | 0.155 | 0.140 | 0.134 |
| 20 | 0.245 | 0.155 | 0.140 | 0.134 |
| 40 | 0.260 | 0.170 | 0.140 | 0.130 |
| 80 | 0.266 | 0.176 | 0.143 | 0.133 |

## Port onto the ported #2955 (2026-11-23)

This branch now merges the ported #2955 (`9787bf79e`), which contains `main` with #2984 and #3537. No rebase and no force-push.

Conflicts: `crates/app/src/operation/agie_profile.rs`, `crates/post/src/agie/contour.rs`, `docs/user-guide/agie-wire-edm.md`. The files of the ported #2955 are the frame. The old `jescript.rs` writer of this branch is not used.

What the port did:
- The measured table moves into `camcraft_post::agie_setup` as `QN2_OFFSETS_UM`, next to the zero-step setup that writes the height.
- `PunchSetup20` gets a `height_um` field. `encode()` refuses a thickness that is not in the table (`SetupError::UnqualifiedHeight`).
- The SBL writes the height into `ID_HEIGHT` of the piece and of the work, and `-height` into `ID_POSPOSZ`. All other SBL lines stay the same.
- The operator review text names the thickness and the four offsets of that thickness. It is now a `String`.
- `prepare()` refuses an unmeasured thickness first, with the list of supported thicknesses. `check_punch_envelope` uses the measured rough offset of the thickness for the miter. The straight face margin is the rough offset plus the 0.125 mm wire radius, rounded up to 0.1 mm. That gives 0.4 mm for all four thicknesses.
- The app-side 20 mm check is removed. The post check is the single source.
- All #2984 and #2955 checks stay: zero steps, stock and start hole, separation 1.0 mm, convex envelope, oblique entry, corner clearance.
- A 20 mm job is byte for byte the same as before: the ISO, the SBR, the SBL golden `CCSEP20.SBL`, and the review text.
- Refusal texts do not name the machine (#3537).
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row names the four thicknesses.

Process change: yes

## Pinning tests
- `camcraft-post` `agie_safe_setup`:
  - `each_measured_qn2_height_sets_piece_work_and_review_offsets`: the height fields and the review offsets for each thickness. Only three SBL lines change against 20 mm.
  - `an_unmeasured_qn2_height_writes_no_setup`: the refusal for 0, -20, 12, 19.999, 20.001, 25, 39.999, 60 and 100 mm.

  - `only_a_measured_qn2_thickness_prepares_a_punch`: the refusal and its text.
  - `a_measured_height_changes_only_the_setup_height_fields`: the full export at 15, 40 and 80 mm. The ISO and SBR are the same as at 20 mm.
- `camcraft-app` `agie_native`: `qualified_qn2_heights_set_both_piece_and_work_with_stock_top_at_zero` and `an_incompatible_plate_or_datum_writes_no_agie_job` (from this PR).

Head `4a94c23ce`. It merges cleanly with `main`.

title: feat(wire): post convex punches with oblique faces as native job files
body:
The native wire EDM job files post accepts a convex prismatic punch with straight oblique faces. Before this change, it accepted only an axis-aligned rectangular punch.

## Port onto main (2026-11-23)

This branch is now merged with `main` (#2984 and #3537 included). The port keeps the writer and the setup of `main` as the frame. It adds the checks of this PR into that frame.

What stays from `main`, unchanged:
- `prepare()` builds the guarded zero-step `PunchSetup20` first. The stock span, the 20 mm stock, the micrometre start hole and the hole-in-stock checks run before the contour checks.
- `export_with_review` refuses a separation length that is not 1.0 mm.
- The ISO, SBR and SBL files go through `crates/post/src/agie_setup.rs`. The old `jescript.rs` writer of this branch is not used.
- The rectangular output is byte for byte the same. The tests of `main` for the rectangle pass without a change.

What this PR adds to `main`:
- `check_punch_envelope` replaces the rectangle refusal. It refuses a reentrant corner. It checks the 0.4 mm stock margin at each vertex. It checks the miter point of the 0.245 mm rough offset and the wire allowance at each corner.
- `entry_face` and `outside_seam` replace the old entry search. The entry can be on an oblique face. The 3 mm lead and the 3 mm face length on each side are measured along the face, in exact integer arithmetic. When the perpendicular foot falls between 0.00001 mm grid points, the post selects an exterior grid point within 0.00001 mm. It then checks the envelope again on the emitted lines.
- Refusal texts name the problem, not the machine (#3537).
- The examples `examples/agie/oblique-punch.camscript` and `slope-punch.camscript` use the post name "Native wire EDM job files".
- The `camcraft-mcp` skill row says "a convex straight-sided punch" in place of "rectangular punch".

Process change: yes

## Pinning tests (`camcraft-post` lib, `agie::tests`)
- `oblique_punch_preserves_nominal_vertices_and_perpendicular_seam`: the nominal path of the 3:4 pentagon, both windings, and the 3 mm face-length limit.
- `oblique_punch_posts_the_zero_step_setup_and_its_faces`: the full ISO file of the oblique punch through `export_with_review`, the SBL fields of the zero-step setup, and the refusal of separation 0.0 with no output directory.
- `oblique_seam_rounds_to_the_exterior_without_moving_nominal_vertices`: the exterior grid seam.
- `outward_rounding_cannot_consume_the_required_lead_clearance`: the grid refusal.
- `an_acute_miter_needs_more_stock_than_a_round_corner`: the corner-clearance refusal and the convex refusal.
- `every_face_keeps_the_straight_stock_margin`: the 0.4 mm face margin of `main` stays.
- `separation_needs_three_millimetres_on_each_side_of_the_entry`: the entry face-length refusal of `main`.

## Readings
Head `9787bf79e`. It merges cleanly with `main` at `09ad779ee`.
- `cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`: 11 steps, 0 failed. `camcraft-post` lib: 103 passed. Nine `camcraft-app` suites (the example catalog and first-part suites): 69 passed, 4 ignored (heavy).
- By name: `agie_native` 11 passed, `mcp_wire_contour` 8 passed, `mcp_doc_drift` 6 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- CLI: `examples/agie/oblique-punch.camscript` wrote `POLY20` (entry X-12.50000 Y0.00000, all five nominal vertices). `slope-punch.camscript` wrote `SLOPE20` (exterior entry X-12.64765 Y0.50336). The receipt of each says `"working_steps_generated": false`.
- Heavy lanes: `gate heavy --dry-run` reaches 61 `camcraft-app` heavy steps through the `post` dependency. This is a `P6` PR, so no heavy step is required ("Heavy lanes at review"). None ran.
- Light lane: `gate light --dry-run` plans 4 steps (`motion` lib, `adaptive_troch_parallel`, `app` `pocket_pass_start`). None of them is in the changed code. They did not run, because the local disks had no space for a release build. The review must run them.

## Not exercised

title: feat(2d): rest machining on the 2D Adaptive from the previous operations
body:
Stacked on #2822 (merge #2822 first).

This PR is a `feat`: it adds a parameter group. The default (off) does not change an output.

## What changed

The 2D Adaptive operation has the rest machining group.
With the group on, the operation cuts only what the earlier operations of the same setup left.

- `OpParams::Adaptive2D` has the field `rest: Option<RestParams>`. `None` is off and is the default.
- `machining2d::rest_adaptive_previous` (new, motion crate) reads the stock of the previous operations with `rest_stock_from_columns` (#2033). It gives that stock to the rest Adaptive planner `rest_adaptive` (#2031).
- Each plunge stands where that stock proves the whole cutter clear. The planner holds the optimal load on the material that stands.
- `adaptive::rest_levels` (new) gives the cut depths of the rest planner. The stock is read at exactly those depths.
- The group rides the existing `EditOperationParams` command (undo and redo), the project key `rest` of the 2D Adaptive and the MCP `edit_operation` parameter. A file without the key reads as off.
- The stamp writes byte `0xD9` and the allowance when the group is on. An operation without the group keeps its stamp.

Refused by name, at the edit and again at generation:

- An entered previous tool (`REST_ADAPTIVE_ENTERED`). An entered diameter does not prove where material is absent (#2031). The 2D Pocket keeps that mode.
- The Trochoidal method, arc turns, a tilt. The rest planner does not read them, so they are not dropped silently.
- A negative or non-finite allowance.

Refused by name at generation:

- An earlier operation with no toolpath, a stale toolpath, or a suppressed cut (the refusals of #2033).
- No stock ahead (`REST_ADAPTIVE_NO_STOCK`). The 2D Pocket cuts the whole pocket in this case. The 2D Adaptive does not, because the rest planner cannot enter a full pocket.
- A roughing pass that stops above the floor: "rest Adaptive has no entry with proved clearance".

## Cause

The rest Adaptive planner (#2031) had no door from an operation.
The retired Adaptive strategy of the 2D Pocket was its only possible caller (#2253).
The 2D Adaptive operation had no rest parameter and no producer of the proved stock.

## Two findings

- The column reading of #2033 leaves a band along each wall that an earlier tool cut to. On a 0.1 mm grid the band is 0.14 mm thick. With the film of #2033 (one cell diagonal) the planner read the band as rest material and refused the fixture ("would reach 23 passes by a retract"). The film is now `cell * (1 + sqrt 2)`. The band still stands for each plunge and each load reading. No pass is planned for it. The path note states the film.
- An allowance of 0.6 mm grew that band to 0.74 mm, and the planner found no entry. The allowance now grows only material that is thicker than the film. It never makes the standing material smaller.

## Tests

Red before the change: the pins use the new field and the new function, so they do not compile on unchanged code. The mutation results are the proof for each guard.

Pins, all new:

- `crates/app/tests/rest_adaptive_op.rs` (6 tests):
  - `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_what_the_simulated_roughing_pass_left`: the real job (60 x 40 pocket, 3 mm corners, 12 mm roughing tool, 4 mm rest tool) against an independent simulation of the roughing pass. Each standing column is cut. No plunge goes down a column that the roughing pass left under the cutter. No rapid is below the top of the stock, but a straight lift. Each feed stays at a corner.
  - `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_is_refused_by_name`
  - `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_is_refused_by_name_at_the_edit`
  - `a_document_past_the_door_is_refused_at_generation`
  - `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_a_project_file_key_and_moves_the_stamp`
  - `mcp_sets_the_group_refuses_the_entered_tool_undoes_and_the_project_keeps_it`
- `crates/app/src/operation/rest_op_tests.rs`: `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp`, `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool`.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/rest_prior_adaptive_tests.rs` (lib): `each_guard_is_pinned_and_its_removal_fails_the_pin`, `the_allowance_never_makes_the_standing_material_smaller`, `bad_rest_values_are_refused_by_name`.
- `crates/motion/tests/rest_adaptive/main.rs`: `the_column_stock_of_the_previous_operations_plans_the_rest_adaptive_pass` (the laws of #2031 on the column stock: verifier, plunges, rapids, load, coverage), `the_previous_operations_planner_refuses_what_it_cannot_prove`.

Mutations (one guard removed, its pin run, then restored and green):

| Guard removed | Pin | Mutant |
|---|---|---|
| generate: the rest planner is called | `the_rest_adaptive_pass_cuts_...` | red |
| generate: the refusals stand at generation | `a_document_past_the_door_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: entered tool refused | `what_the_rest_planner_does_not_read_...` | red |
| `rest_op`: Trochoidal refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: arc turns refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: tilt refused | same | red |
| `rest_op`: bad values refused without a tool | `the_adaptive_rest_group_refuses_bad_values_without_a_tool` | red |
| `rest_op`: the 2D Adaptive reads the previous operations (job stock, earlier-operation refusals) | `a_stock_that_does_not_prove_an_entry_...` | red |
| `params`: stamp byte `0xD9` | `the_adaptive_rest_group_moves_the_stamp` | red |
| `params`: the allowance in the stamp | same | red |
| project: the key is written | `the_group_is_an_undoable_edit_...` | red |
| project: the key is read | `mcp_sets_the_group_...` | red |
| motion: entered mode refused (`Guards::source`) | `each_guard_is_pinned_...` | red |
| motion: no stock refused (`Guards::stock`) | same | red |
| motion: the allowance grows the material (`Guards::allowance`) | same | red |
| motion: the film of the reading (one cell diagonal put back) | same | red |

The three motion guards have a switch in the code (`rest_prior_adaptive::Guards`), and the unit test turns each off.
The first run of the two stamp mutants and of the bad-value mutant stayed green on the app tests, because another path gave the same result. I added the two lib pins for them, and the mutants are red on those pins.

title: feat(2d): arc turns and their radius on Face, 2D Contour and Slot
body:
## What changed

Face, 2D Contour and Slot have the arc turns option with a corner arc radius. The parameters are `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`, the same as on 2D Pocket, 2D Adaptive and 2D Offset (#1733).

All three kinds can round their corners safely. No kind is left out.

- **2D Contour** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the tool radius, as before.
- **Face** had `blend_turns`. It gets `blend_radius`. No radius is the semicircle of half the row spacing, as before. A smaller radius gives two quarter arcs with a straight step between them. The step is one radius outside the overrun line, away from the footprint. With a radius, rows spaced wider than the tool diameter turn on arcs too.
- **Slot** gets `blend_turns` and `blend_radius`. Each row-end corner of the serpentine pass turns on one tangent arc. No radius is the tool radius. The new module is `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slot_turns.rs`.

The parameter door (`sane.rs`) refuses a radius below 0.01 mm on the three kinds. The generators refuse a radius larger than the tool radius, with the text of `corner_arc_radius`. The project file writes the keys only when they are set. The cache digest reads the radius only when the option is on.

The operation pages show the radius rows when the option is on. The Face page names its default "Arc radius = half the row spacing".

MCP: `edit_operation` sets the two fields through `EditOperationParams`. No new command and no new tool are necessary.

The type is `feat`, because the change adds parameters. The task template gave `fix`.

## Cause

The fix for #1733 gave the radius to the three pocket kinds only. Face and 2D Contour had the option without a radius. Slot did not have the option.

## Which corners turn, and why no arc cuts past the wall

- 2D Contour: only a corner that turns toward the air gets an arc. This is the law of `fillet.rs`, and it did not change. A corner that turns toward the part stays sharp, and the notes name it. A convex outside corner is such a corner, so an arc cannot leave material there.
- Face: each point of a turn is on or outside the overrun line, one tool radius from the footprint. The turn reaches one radius past that line at most.
- Slot: the pass is in the cutter-center stadium, which is convex. A fillet is inside the triangle of its corner and its two tangent points, and that triangle is inside the stadium. `fillet_corners` proves each triangle again and keeps a corner sharp if it cannot prove it. An arc leaves corner rest at the round end of the slot. The note states the largest rest.

## Tests

Pins in `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (13 tests):

- `face_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (review fix)
- `no_face_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_overrun_line`
- `a_face_radius_past_half_the_row_spacing_turns_on_the_semicircle`
- `a_face_radius_rounds_rows_spaced_wider_than_the_tool`
- `the_face_door_refuses_a_radius_no_control_can_cut_and_reads_none_when_off`
- `contour_corners_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_contour_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_contour_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `slot_row_ends_turn_on_tangent_arcs_of_the_given_radius`
- `no_slot_arc_turn_cuts_past_the_wall`
- `no_slot_radius_is_the_tool_radius_and_the_door_refuses_by_name`
- `a_one_row_slot_has_no_corner_and_says_so`

Pins in `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` (6 tests):

- `face_contour_and_slot_take_arc_turns_and_a_radius_through_edit_operation_and_undo`
- `a_radius_no_control_can_cut_is_refused_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_project_file_keeps_the_radius_and_a_default_file_has_no_key`
- `generation_cuts_the_face_and_the_slot_turns_at_the_radius_asked`
- `generation_refuses_a_radius_past_the_tool_radius_by_name_on_each_kind`
- `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp`

Two unit tests in `blend.rs`: `a_user_radius_turns_on_corner_arcs_where_the_stride_has_room` and `a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` (review fix). Two unit tests there changed with the plan type (`bool` became `Option<Turn>`).

Red before the change: yes. On the unchanged code the motion pin does not compile, because `FaceParams`, `ContourParams` and `SlotParams` have no such fields (`error[E0560]`).

Mutation results. Each mutation put one guard back to the old behaviour. Each pin went red, and green again after the restore.

| Face digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |
| Contour digest without the radius | `the_stamp_tells_a_radius_from_none_and_a_default_op_keeps_its_stamp` | red |

| Face takes the semicircle when half the spacing is less than 0.005 mm past the radius (review fix) | `a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short`, `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius` | red (`actual radii: [0.012500000000000178]` for 0.01 mm) |

### Review fix: the Face radius bound

`corner_turn` in `blend.rs` gave the semicircle when half the row spacing was less than 0.005 mm past the radius. That semicircle is larger than the radius. Now:

- If half the spacing is not more than the radius (1e-9 mm float margin), the turn is the semicircle, as before. Its radius is not larger than the requested radius.
- If half the spacing is more than the radius by 0.005 mm or less, the turn uses two corner arcs. Their radius is half the spacing minus 0.005 mm, which is less than the requested radius. The straight step stays 0.01 mm.
- If that radius is below 0.01 mm, the turn stays sharp. The status line counts it as the `Tiny` refusal ("row spacing below the 0.020 mm arc resolution").

Pins: `crates/motion/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs::a_face_turn_never_exceeds_the_radius_when_the_straight_step_is_short` (the reviewer's 60 x 10.025 mm case and three other spacings), and the unit test `blend::law::a_short_step_never_turns_on_an_arc_larger_than_the_radius`.

### Review fix: the exhaustive test literals

The latest review found missing required fields in nine exhaustive test literals from main. The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`.

- Face literals have `blend_radius: None` in `chamfer_partly_bevelled`, `first_traverse`, `first_traverse_table`, `setup_move_order`, `stock_copy_hole`, `vouch_fidelity` and `vouch_fidelity_mcp`.
- Slot literals have `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None` in `tilt_basis0_edited_file` and `tilt_stock_cap`.
- Current main adds the same missing Face default in `first_traverse_mill_turn` and `model_fidelity_wide`. These literals have `blend_radius: None` too.

- Current main also adds a Contour literal and a Slot literal in `crates/motion/tests/equal_steps.rs`. The Contour literal has `blend_radius: None`. The Slot literal has `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None`.

- The test helper in `crates/app/src/operation/first_traverse.rs` also has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `operation::first_traverse::tests::a_mill_turn_judges_its_milling_kinds_in_the_mill_order`.

- The Contour literal in `crates/app/tests/equal_steps.rs` has `blend_radius: None`. Its pin is `equal_steps::edit_sets_equal_steps_and_undo_restores_the_remainder_ladder`.

The fix adds 18 default-field lines in fourteen files. All changed literals are in tests. It changes no runtime source logic.

Runtime pins: eleven app suites passed 47 tests. Motion `equal_steps` passed 13 tests. The app first-traverse unit pin passed one test. App `equal_steps` passed six tests.

Mutation: removing the added defaults gave compiler error `E0063` in the affected literals. Restoring the defaults made all fourteen affected suites compile and pass.

Final head: `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`

Quick gate: 761 steps passed on final head `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`, against upstream main `aa4c785dbd53715f1d811524dc99c688b9380cba`. The first run passed all 123 motion steps. The app build then stopped on a stale local `camcraft_kernel` artifact (`E0463`) after the check profile changed. After rebuilding that local artifact, `cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main --only app --only ui` passed all 638 selected steps, with 0 failed, in 38.6 minutes. These two runs cover the quick plan: 7,028 tests passed, 0 failed and 115 ignored. No source change was needed for the artifact failure.

Heavy lanes: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base upstream/main` passed on final head `4adba68fd814090bac6f28bc2acd4e0eb4675200`: 237 steps, 0 failed, in 44.3 minutes. The reached motion and app heavy lanes ran. The lanes ran 100 passing tests and six expected failures: three for #1950 and three for #2849. There were 0 unexpected failures. Motion had 38 steps and 57 passing tests. App had 198 steps and 43 passing tests. The shared build was one step.

Clippy: `cargo clippy -j 16 -p camcraft-motion -p camcraft-app -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings` passed in 40.41 seconds.

The results above are for the old head `4adba68fd`. The results for the current head are in the next section.

### Review fix: the merge conflicts with main

The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `6ffa808ae`. Four files had conflicts. Each resolution keeps the two sides:

- `crates/app/tests/first_router_part.rs`, `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_images.rs` and `crates/ui/src/egui_app/tests/guide_projects.rs`: the Contour literals keep `blend_radius` from this PR and `chain_overrides` from main.
- `crates/motion/src/machining2d/mod.rs`: `mod slot_turns;` from this PR and `mod undercut;` from main both stay.

Main added literals that do not have the new fields. These got the defaults:

- `blend_radius: None` in `crates/motion/tests/contour_tab_lead.rs`, `crates/app/tests/klartext_builtin.rs` (two literals) and `crates/app/tests/first_traverse_table_tilt.rs`.
- `blend_turns: false` and `blend_radius: None` in the Slot literal of `crates/app/tests/posting_rotaries_first.rs`.
- The Contour literal of this PR's `crates/app/tests/arc_turn_kinds.rs` got `chain_overrides: Vec::new()`.

After the merge, `crates/app/src/operation/params.rs` had 402 lines, and `params_files_stay_under_the_line_law` failed. Commit `8716a45fd` moves the Face and Contour radius writes into `digest::write_blend_radius`. The digest bytes do not change. The file now has 392 lines.

The merged `sane.rs`, `generate.rs`, `params_impl.rs` and `first_traverse.rs` keep each guard of main. This PR only adds its fields there.

Pins and mutations:

- Without `blend_radius` in `contour_tab_lead` or `chain_overrides` in `first_router_part`, the build gave `E0063`. After the restore, both compiled and passed.

### Review fix: the new Contour and Slot literals

The latest review found two new exhaustive literals from main without the required defaults. The branch includes upstream main `6e1805bfdae52fcfea71a946d381dfbfdefc79f5`. Merge commit `e79d3248ec63dde01891fd4ca165098d6026cd62` has no conflicts.

### Review fix: the Slot conflict with main (#2906 wall lap)

The branch now includes a merge of upstream main `a2c35e0eb`. Merge commit `22f3ffb98` resolves one conflict in `slot()` in `crates/motion/src/machining2d/slots.rs`. The two behaviors stay:

- The #1759 arc turns round the serpentine rows only. `rows` is a copy of the pass before the lap points join it.
- The #2906 wall lap follows the rows in the same walk. The new helper `slot_turns::with_lap` puts the rounded walk (or the straight rows, when nothing rounds) first, then the lap.

Commit `d80eccfab` updates the app pin: the sharp Slot pass now has the lap's cap arcs.

title: fix(ui): name the platform's command key in shortcut hints
body:
Fork synced at v0.18.0 (branch cut from upstream/main at 0757563d).

## What changed

- New `crates/ui/src/shortcut_keys.rs`: `command_key()` returns `Cmd` on macOS and `Ctrl` elsewhere (`cfg!(target_os = "macos")`); `chord("Shift+O")` builds `Cmd+Shift+O` or `Ctrl+Shift+O`.
- Command-shortcut hints now go through `chord`: ribbon tips in `panes.rs` (`tip_of`: New, Open, Open project, Save, Save as, Post, Undo, Redo), the operation bar hints in `op_page.rs` (Apply, Clear toolpath, Delete), the machine-cell hover in `machines_pane.rs`, and the cleared-toolpath status in `state.rs`.
- The click-to-add pick hints go through `command_key()` / `chord` too (review fix): `geo_page.rs` `edge_hint()` (was the const `EDGE_HINT`) and `click_selects_hint()`, and `boundary.rs` `hints()` (was the const `HINTS`). The picks read `mods.command` (`edge_pick.rs`, `interact.rs`, `feature_click.rs`, #1238), so on macOS the add key is Cmd. The bindings are unchanged.
- `command_key_for(macos: bool)`: pure form of `command_key()`, so both answers are tested on any host.
- `gcode_view.rs` Ctrl+C is a code comment only; there is no user-visible hint string for it, so nothing changed there.
- Structural tip-table test (`tips_match_the_imgui_table`) now asserts through `chord`, not literals, so it passes on every OS.
- Decision record: `docs/decisions/1239-cmd-hints.md`.

## Pinning tests

- `egui_app::tests::tips_match_the_imgui_table` (structural, tip strings for New/Open/Save/Post/Undo/Redo via `chord`)
- `shortcut_keys::tests::command_key_names_the_platform_key` (`Cmd` under macOS cfg, `Ctrl` otherwise)
- `shortcut_keys::tests::chord_prefixes_the_platform_key`
- `shortcut_keys::tests::command_key_for_names_both_platforms` (`Cmd`/`Ctrl` on every host)
- `shortcut_keys::tests::pick_hints_name_the_command_key` (edge hint, "Click selects" hover, boundary pick help)

## How tested

- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --lib -- --test-threads=1` from `crates/ui` (after merging upstream/main, head 415b2bd7): 620 passed, 0 failed, 5 ignored (includes the pinning tests above).
- `cargo test -p camcraft-ui --test feedback` from `crates/ui`: 6 passed.
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-ui --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean.
- PNG snapshots untouched.

## Not exercised

- The Windows/Linux branch (`Ctrl`) ran only through `command_key_for(false)` and the cfg-independent assertions; this Mac is macOS, so the `Cmd` branch is what the run covered.
- No headless run of the app to see the hover text on screen; the strings are asserted, not painted.
- No change to any key binding (out of scope).

Changelog: Shortcut hints name Cmd on macOS (Ctrl elsewhere) instead of Ctrl for command shortcuts (#1239, PR #1293)

Fixes #1239
